- Root: ر-و-ض (rawḍa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A garden, meadow, or verdant place; a place of lush growth and beauty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The spiritual garden of righteous deeds and knowledge that yields the fruits of the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a physical garden. Metaphorical: the collection of prophetic sayings that cultivate the soul.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʾIḍāfa (Construct State) — The title "Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn" is a genitive construction, where "Gardens" is the head noun and "the Righteous" is its specifier, indicating possession or close association.
chapters.translation:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Praise be to Allah, the One, the Subduer, the Mighty, the Forgiving, who wraps the night over the day as a reminder for those with hearts and sight, and as an insight for those of understanding and reflection. He is the One who awakened from His creation those He chose, making them renounce this worldly abode, occupying them with watchfulness over Him and continuous thought, with constant adherence to admonition and remembrance. He granted them success in striving in His obedience and preparing for the abode of permanence, and in being wary of what displeases Him and necessitates the abode of ruin, and in maintaining this across changing states and conditions. I praise Him with the most complete and purest praise, the most encompassing and abundant. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, the Most Kind, the Most Generous, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. And I bear witness that our master Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger, His beloved and intimate friend, the guide to a straight path, and the caller to a true religion. May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, upon all the other Prophets, upon the family of each, and upon all the righteous.

To proceed: Allah the Exalted has said: {«And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me.»} [Qur’an 51:56-57]. This is a clear declaration that they were created for worship. Therefore, it is incumbent upon them to attend to that for which they were created and to turn away from the worldly pleasures through renunciation (zuhd), for it is an abode of perishing, not a place of eternal stay; a mount of passage, not a home of joy; a point of separation, not a land of permanence. For this reason, the most vigilant of its people are the worshippers, and the wisest of people within it are the ascetics. Allah the Exalted has said: {«The example of the worldly life is but like rain which We have sent down from the sky that the plants of the earth absorb – [those] from which men and livestock eat. Until, when the earth has taken on its adornment and is beautified and its people suppose that they have capability over it, there comes to it Our command by night or by day, and We make it as a harvest reaped, as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We explain in detail the signs for a people who give thought.»} [Qur’an 10:24]. The verses on this meaning are numerous.

How excellent is the saying of the poet:
"Indeed, for Allah there are servants who are intelligent; They abandoned the world and feared trials.
They looked at it, and when they knew That it was not a home for any living being,
They made it a sea and took Righteous deeds within it as ships."

Since its condition is as I have described, and our condition and the purpose of our creation is as I have presented, it is incumbent upon the responsible person (mukallaf) to take himself along the path of the righteous, to follow the way of those of intellect and insight, to prepare for what I have indicated, and to be concerned with what I have alerted to. The most correct path for him in this, and the most guiding way he can take, is to be disciplined by what is authentically reported from our Prophet, the master of the first and the last, and the most noble of the predecessors and successors, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him and upon all the other Prophets. Allah the Exalted has said: {«And cooperate in righteousness and piety»} [Qur’an 5:2]. It is authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: «Allah is in the aid of the servant as long as the servant is in the aid of his brother», and that he said: «Whoever guides to good has a reward like the reward of the one who does it», and that he said: «Whoever calls to guidance has a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without that diminishing anything from their rewards», and that he said to ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him: «For by Allah, if Allah guides through you a single man, that is better for you than red camels». So I saw fit to compile a concise collection of authentic hadiths, encompassing what would be a path for its reader to the Hereafter, and a means of attaining his inward and outward etiquettes. It is a collection of encouragements (targhīb) and warnings (tarhīb), and all types of etiquettes for the wayfarers (sālikīn): from hadiths on renunciation (zuhd), disciplining the soul (riyāḍāt al-nufūs), refining character (tahdhīb al-akhlāq), purifying the hearts and their treatment, safeguarding the limbs and removing their crookedness, and other goals of the knowers of Allah (ʿārifīn).

I have committed myself in it to mention only authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) and clear hadiths, attributed to the well-known authentic books. I begin the chapters from the Mighty Qur’an with noble verses, and I adorn what needs clarification or explanation of a hidden meaning with precious notes. If I say at the end of a hadith: "Agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh)", its meaning is: narrated by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

I hope that if this book is completed, it will be a driver for the one who attends to it towards good deeds, and a barrier for him from all types of abominations and destructive acts. I ask a brother who benefits from anything in it to supplicate for me, for my parents, my teachers, all our loved ones, and all Muslims. Upon Allah the Most Kind is my reliance, and to Him is my delegation and my support. Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best disposer of affairs. There is no might and no power except with Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Chapter 1: On Sincerity (Ikhlāṣ) and Bringing the Intention (Niyyah) into All Actions, Words, and States, Apparent and Hidden**

Allah the Exalted has said: {«And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and to establish prayer and to give zakah. And that is the correct religion.»} [Qur’an 98:5]. And He said: {«Never will reach Allah their meat nor their blood, but what reaches Him is the piety (taqwā) from you.»} [Qur’an 22:37]. And He said: {«Say, "Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it."»} [Qur’an 3:29].

**Hadith 1:**
On the authority of the Commander of the Believers, Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ibn Nufayl ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Riyāḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qurṭ ibn Razāḥ ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib al-Qurashī al-ʿAdawī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: «Verily, actions are but by intentions, and for every person is only what he intended. So whoever's emigration (hijrah) was to Allah and His Messenger, then his emigration is to Allah and His Messenger. And whoever's emigration was for worldly gain to acquire, or for a woman to marry, then his emigration is to what he emigrated for.» Agreed upon its authenticity. It was narrated by the two Imams of hadith, Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mughīrah ibn Bardizbah al-Juʿfī al-Bukhārī, and Abū al-Ḥusayn Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj ibn Muslim al-Qushayrī al-Naysābūrī, may Allah be pleased with them both, in their two Ṣaḥīḥs, which are the most authentic books ever compiled.

**Hadith 2:**
On the authority of the Mother of the Believers, Umm ʿAbd Allāh ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «An army will attack the Kaʿbah, and when they are in a desert plain (baydāʾ) of the earth, the first and last of them will be swallowed up by the earth.» She said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, how will the first and last of them be swallowed up, when among them are their markets and those who are not from them? He said: «The first and last of them will be swallowed up, then they will be resurrected according to their intentions.» Agreed upon. This is the wording of al-Bukhārī.

**Hadith 3:**
On the authority of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: «There is no emigration (hijrah) after the conquest [of Mecca], but rather jihad and intention. And if you are called to mobilize, then mobilize.» Agreed upon. Its meaning: There is no emigration from Mecca because it has become an abode of Islam.

**Hadith 4:**
On the authority of Abū ʿAbd Allāh Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a military expedition, and he said: «Indeed, there are men in Medina who, whenever you travel a distance or cross a valley, they are with you; they were kept back by illness.» In another narration: «Except that they share with you in the reward.» Narrated by Muslim. Al-Bukhārī also narrated it on the authority of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We returned from the expedition of Tabūk with the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: «Indeed, there are people we left behind in Medina who, whenever we traversed a mountain pass or a valley, they were with us; they were kept back by a valid excuse.»

**Hadith 5:**
On the authority of Abū Yazīd Maʿn ibn Yazīd ibn al-Akhnas, may Allah be pleased with them all — he, his father, and his grandfather were Companions — who said: My father Yazīd took out some dinars to give in charity and placed them with a man in the mosque. I came and took them and brought them to him. He said: By Allah, I did not intend you. So I took my case to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: «For you is what you intended, O Yazīd, and for you is what you took, O Maʿn.» Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

**Hadith 6:**
On the authority of Abū Isḥāq Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ Mālik ibn Uhayb ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Zuhrah ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy al-Qurashī al-Zuhrī, may Allah be pleased with him — one of the ten given glad tidings of Paradise — who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to visit me during the Farewell Pilgrimage due to a severe illness I had. I said: O Messenger of Allah, I have reached, as you see, a severe state of illness, and I am a man of wealth, and I have no heir except a daughter of mine. Shall I give two-thirds of my wealth in charity? He said: «No.» I said: Then half, O Messenger of Allah? He said: «No.» I said: Then a third? He said: «A third, and a third is much (or great). Indeed, if you leave your heirs wealthy, that is better than leaving them poor, begging from people. And indeed, you will not spend an expenditure seeking thereby the Face of Allah, except that you will be rewarded for it, even the morsel you place in your wife's mouth.» I said: O Messenger of Allah, will I be left behind after my companions? He said: «Indeed, you will not be left behind and do a deed seeking thereby the Face of Allah, except that you will be increased in degree and rank by it. And perhaps you will be left behind until some people benefit by you and others are harmed by you. O Allah, complete for my companions their emigration and do not turn them back on their heels. But the unfortunate one is Saʿd ibn Khawlah» — the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lamented for him because he died in Mecca. Agreed upon.

**Hadith 7:**
On the authority of Abū Hurayrah ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣakhr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Indeed, Allah does not look at your bodies, nor at your forms, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.» Narrated by Muslim.

**Hadith 8:**
On the authority of Abū Mūsā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays al-Ashʿarī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about a man who fights out of bravery, fights out of tribal zeal (ḥamiyyah), and fights out of showing off (riyāʾ) — which of that is in the cause of Allah? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is the highest, then he is in the cause of Allah.» Agreed upon.

**Hadith 9:**
On the authority of Abū Bakrah Nufayʿ ibn al-Ḥārith al-Thaqafī, may Allah be pleased with him: The Prophet ﷺ said: «If two Muslims meet with their swords, then the killer and the killed are in the Fire.» I said: O Messenger of Allah, this is the killer, so what about the killed? He said: «He was eager to kill his companion.» Agreed upon.

**Hadith 10:**
On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «The prayer of a man in congregation is more excellent than his prayer in his market and his house by twenty-some degrees. That is because when one of them performs ablution and does it well, then comes to the mosque with no intention other than prayer, nothing impels him except prayer — he does not take a step except that he is raised a degree by it and a sin is removed from him by it, until he enters the mosque. When he enters the mosque, he is in prayer as long as the prayer is what detains him. And the angels send blessings upon one of you as long as he remains in his place of prayer, saying: 'O Allah, have mercy on him. O Allah, forgive him. O Allah, accept his repentance,' as long as he does not harm anyone and does not break his ablution.» Agreed upon, and this is the wording of Muslim. His saying ﷺ: «yunahizuhu» is with a fatḥa on the yāʾ and hāʾ and a zāy, meaning: it impels him and rouses him.

**Hadith 11:**
On the authority of Abū al-ʿAbbās ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, relating from his Lord, Blessed and Exalted, that he said: «Indeed, Allah has written down the good deeds and the evil deeds, and then clarified that. So whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, Allah the Blessed and Exalted writes it down with Him as a complete good deed. And if he intends it and does it, Allah writes it down as ten good deeds up to seven hundred times, up to many multiples. And if he intends an evil deed and does not do it, Allah the Exalted writes it down with Him as a complete good deed. And if he intends it and does it, Allah writes it down as a single evil deed.» Agreed upon.

**Hadith 12:**
On the authority of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: «Three men from among those before you set out, until nightfall brought them to a cave, and they entered it. Then a rock rolled down from the mountain and blocked the entrance of the cave upon them. They said: 'Nothing will save you from this rock except that you supplicate to Allah with your righteous deeds.' One of them said: 'O Allah, I had two elderly parents, and I would not give my family or wealth to drink before them. One day, my search for trees took me far away, and I did not return to them until they had slept. I milked their evening drink for them, but found them sleeping. I disliked waking them, and I disliked giving my family or wealth to drink before them. So I remained — the cup in my hand — waiting for them to wake up, until dawn broke, while the children were crying at my feet. They woke up and drank their evening drink. O Allah, if I did that seeking Your Face, then relieve us from what we are in because of this rock.' The rock moved aside a little, but they could not get out. The other said: 'O Allah, I had a cousin — in one narration: I loved her as intensely as any man loves women — and I sought her for myself, but she refused me, until a year of famine afflicted her. She came to me, and I gave her one hundred and twenty dinars on the condition that she would let me have my way with her. She did, until when I was able over her — in one narration: when she sat between my legs — she said: 'Fear Allah, and do not break the seal except by its right.' So I left her, while she was the most beloved of people to me, and I left the gold I had given her. O Allah, if I did that seeking Your Face, then relieve us from what we are in.' The rock moved aside, but they still could not get out. The third said: 'O Allah, I hired laborers and paid them their wages, except one man who left his due and went away. I invested his wage until his wealth grew much. He came to me after a while and said: 'O servant of Allah, pay me my wage.' I said: 'All that you see — camels, cattle, sheep, and slaves — is your wage.' He said: 'O servant of Allah, do not mock me!' I said: 'I am not mocking you.' So he took it all and drove it away, leaving nothing. O Allah, if I did that seeking Your Face, then relieve us from what we are in.' The rock moved aside, and they walked out.» Agreed upon.

**Chapter 2: On Repentance (Tawbah)**

The scholars said: Repentance is obligatory from every sin. If the disobedience is between the servant and Allah the Exalted, not involving a right of a human being, it has three conditions:
1. That he desists from the sin.
2. That he regrets having done it.
3. That he resolves never to return to it.
If any of the three is missing, his repentance is not valid.
If the sin involves a right of a human being, its conditions are four: these three, and that he absolves himself of the right of its owner. If it is wealth or similar, he returns it to him. If it is a hadd punishment for slander (qadhf) or similar, he enables him to exact it or seeks his forgiveness. If it is backbiting (ghībah), he asks to be absolved of it. It is obligatory to repent from all sins. If he repents from some of them, his repentance from that sin is valid according to the people of truth, and the rest remains upon him. The evidences from the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the Ummah have clearly established the obligation of repentance.

Allah the Exalted has said: {«And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you might succeed.»} [Qur’an 24:31]. And He said: {«And that you seek forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him.»} [Qur’an 11:3]. And He said: {«O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance (tawbatan naṣūḥā).»} [Qur’an 66:8].

**Hadith 13:**
On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: «By Allah, I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him more than seventy times a day.» Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

**Hadith 14:**
On the authority of al-Agharr ibn Yasār al-Muzanī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «O people, repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness, for I repent one hundred times a day.» Narrated by Muslim.

**Hadith 15:**
On the authority of Abū Ḥamzah Anas ibn Mālik al-Anṣārī — the servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Allah is more delighted with the repentance of His servant than one of you who finds his camel after losing it in a desolate land.» Agreed upon. In a narration of Muslim: «Allah is more intensely delighted with the repentance of His servant when he repents to Him than one of you who was on his mount in a desolate land, and it slipped away from him, carrying his food and drink. He despaired of it, and came to a tree and lay down in its shade, having despaired of his mount. While he was in that state, suddenly it was standing before him. He took hold of its reins, then said out of intense joy: 'O Allah, You are my servant and I am your Lord!' — erring out of intense joy.»

**Hadith 16:**
On the authority of Abū Mūsā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays al-Ashʿarī, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: «Indeed, Allah the Exalted stretches out His Hand at night to accept the repentance of the one who sinned during the day, and stretches out His Hand during the day to accept the repentance of the one who sinned during the night, until the sun rises from its setting place (west).» Narrated by Muslim.

**Hadith 17:**
On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Whoever repents before the sun rises from its setting place (west), Allah will accept his repentance.» Narrated by Muslim.

**Hadith 18:**
On the authority of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: «Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he is not in the throes of death (yugharghir).» Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A ḥasan hadith."

**Hadith 19:**
On the authority of Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, who said: I came to Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl, may Allah be pleased with him, to ask him about wiping over the leather socks (khuffayn). He said: What has brought you, O Zirr? I said: Seeking knowledge. He said: Indeed, the angels lower their wings for the seeker of knowledge, pleased with what he seeks. I said: Indeed, there is something troubling my chest regarding wiping over the socks after defecation and urination, and I was a companion of the Prophet ﷺ, so I came to ask you: have you heard him mention anything about that? He said: Yes, he used to command us, when we were on a journey — or travelers — not to remove our socks for three days and their nights, except in the case of major ritual impurity (janābah), but [we could wipe] for defecation, urination, and sleep. I said: Did you hear him mention anything about love (al-hawā)? He said: Yes, we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and while we were with him, a Bedouin called him with a loud voice: O Muḥammad! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ answered him with a similar voice: «Here I am (hāʾum)». I said to him: Woe to you! Lower your voice, for you are with the Prophet ﷺ and you have been forbidden from this! He said: By Allah, I will not lower it. The Bedouin said: A man loves a people but has not yet caught up with them? The Prophet ﷺ said: «A man is with those he loves on the Day of Resurrection.» He continued narrating to us until he mentioned a gate in the west, whose width is a journey of forty or seventy years — Sufyān, one of the narrators, said: towards Syria — which Allah the Exalted created on the day He created the heavens and the earth, open for repentance, and it will not be closed until the sun rises from it. Narrated by al-Tirmidhī and others, who said: "A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith."

**Hadith 20:**
On the authority of Abū Saʿīd Saʿd ibn Mālik ibn Sinān al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: «Among those before you was a man who killed ninety-nine people. He asked about the most knowledgeable person on earth, and was directed to a monk. He came to him and said: 'I have killed ninety-nine people; is there any repentance for me?' He said: 'No.' So he killed him, completing one hundred. Then he asked about the most knowledgeable person on earth, and was directed to a scholar. He said: 'I have killed one hundred people; is there any repentance for me?' He said: 'Yes, and who stands between you and repentance? Go to such-and-such a land, for there are people who worship Allah the Exalted; worship Allah with them, and do not return to your land, for it is an evil land.' So he set out, and when he was halfway there, death came to him. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. The angels of mercy said: 'He came repentant, turning his heart to Allah the Exalted.' The angels of punishment said: 'He never did any good.' An angel came to them in the form of a human, and they made him a judge between them. He said: 'Measure the distance between the two lands; whichever he is closer to, he belongs to it.' They measured and found him closer to the land he intended, so the angels of mercy took him.» Agreed upon. In another narration in the Ṣaḥīḥ: «He was closer to the righteous village by a span, so he was made of its people.» In another narration in the Ṣaḥīḥ: «Allah the Exalted revealed to this one [the evil land] to move away, and to this one [the righteous land] to come closer, and said: 'Measure the distance between them.' They found him closer to this one by a span, and he was forgiven.» In another narration: «He leaned with his chest towards it.»

**Hadith 21:**
On the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik — who was the guide of Kaʿb, may Allah be pleased with him, from among his sons when he became blind — who said: I heard Kaʿb ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, narrate his story when he stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the expedition of Tabūk. Kaʿb said: I never stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in any expedition he fought except the expedition of Tabūk. However, I had stayed behind from the expedition of Badr, but no one was blamed for staying behind from it; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims had only gone out to intercept the caravan of Quraysh, until Allah the Exalted brought them together with their enemy without prior appointment. And I witnessed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the night of al-ʿAqabah when we pledged ourselves to Islam, and I would not love to have been present at Badr instead of it, even though Badr is more famous among people than it.

The story of my staying behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the expedition of Tabūk is that I was never stronger nor more affluent than when I stayed behind from him in that expedition. By Allah, I had never gathered two mounts before that, until I gathered them in that expedition. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never intended an expedition without concealing it with another, until that expedition. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out in intense heat, facing a long journey, a desert, and a great number of enemies. He made clear to the Muslims their situation so they could prepare for their expedition, and informed them of the direction he intended. The Muslims with the Messenger of Allah were many, and no written register could encompass them — meaning the diwān. Kaʿb said: So any man who wanted to stay behind thought he could conceal it, as long as no revelation from Allah had come down concerning him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on that expedition when the fruits and shade had ripened, and I was inclined towards it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims with him prepared, and I began to go out in the morning to prepare with him, but I would return without having done anything, saying to myself: I am able to do that when I wish. This continued with me until the matter became serious for the people. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out in the morning with the Muslims, and I had not prepared anything. Then I went out and returned without preparing anything. This continued until they hurried and the expedition was missed. I thought of setting out to catch up with them — would that I had done it! But that was not decreed for me. I began, after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had left, to go out among the people, and it grieved me that I saw no one to emulate except a man accused of hypocrisy, or a man whom Allah the Exalted had excused among the weak. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not mention me until he reached Tabūk. While he was sitting among the people at Tabūk, he said: «What has happened to Kaʿb ibn Mālik?» A man from Banū Salamah said: O Messenger of Allah, his two cloaks and his looking at his sides have detained him. Muʿādh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: Evil is what you said! By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing of him but good. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent. While he was in that state, he saw a man in white clothes shimmering in the mirage. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Be Abū Khaythamah.» And indeed it was Abū Khaythamah al-Anṣārī, the one who had given in charity a ṣāʿ of dates when the hypocrites mocked him.

Kaʿb said: When I heard that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was returning from Tabūk, my distress came upon me. I began to think of lying and saying: How will I escape his anger tomorrow? I sought the help of every person of opinion from my family in that. When it was said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was near, the falsehood left me, and I knew that I would never be saved by anything from him. So I resolved to tell him the truth. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in the morning. Whenever he returned from a journey, he would begin at the mosque, pray two rakʿahs, then sit for the people. When he did that, those who had stayed behind came to him, apologizing and swearing to him. They were about eighty men. He accepted their public declarations, took their pledge, sought forgiveness for them, and left their inner secrets to Allah the Exalted, until I came. When I greeted him, he smiled the smile of one who is angry. Then he said: «Come here.» I came walking until I sat before him. He said to me: «What kept you back? Did you not buy your mount?» I said: O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, if I were sitting with anyone else among the people of this world, I would think I could escape his anger with an excuse, for I have been given eloquence. But by Allah, I knew that if I told you today a lying tale to please you, Allah would soon make you angry with me. And if I told you a true tale, for which you would be angry with me, I hope for the good outcome from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. By Allah, I had no excuse. By Allah, I was never stronger nor more affluent than when I stayed behind from you. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «As for this one, he has spoken the truth. Get up until Allah judges concerning you.» Some men from Banū Salamah followed me and said to me: By Allah, we never knew you had committed a sin before this. You have failed in not apologizing to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as the others who stayed behind apologized. The Messenger of Allah's seeking forgiveness for you would have been sufficient for your sin. Kaʿb said: By Allah, they kept rebuking me until I wanted to go back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and lie to myself. Then I said to them: Has anyone else faced this with me? They said: Yes, two men faced it with you; they said what you said, and it was said to them what was said to you. I said: Who are they? They said: Murārah ibn al-Rabīʿ al-ʿAmrī, and Hilāl ibn Umayyah al-Wāqifī. They mentioned to me two righteous men who had witnessed Badr, and in them there was an example. So I went on when they mentioned them to me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the people from speaking to us — the three of us — from among those who stayed behind. The people avoided us — or he said: they changed towards us — until the earth itself became strange to me, and it was not the earth I knew. We remained in that state for fifty nights. As for my

قدما بلا تردد بتوبة صادقة قبل فوات الأوان {فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره

أن تصيبهم فتنة أو يصيبهم عذاب أليم}] النور: 63 [، واعلم أن الله خلق لكل

إنسان أنفاسا معدودة وساعات محدودة، عند انقضائها تقف دقات قلبه، ويطوى

سجله، ويحال بينه وبين هذه الدار، إما إلى دار أنس وبهجة، وإما إلى دار

شقاء ووحشة، فمن زرع كلمات طيبة وأعمالا صالحة أدخله الله الجنة ونعمه

بالنعيم المقيم، ومن زرع أعمالا سيئة وكلمات قبيحة دخل النار، قال تعالى:

{وإن يستغيثوا يغاثوا بماء كالمهل يشوي الوجوه بئس الشراب وساءت مرتفقا}

[الكهف: 29] وتذكر قوله تعالى: {فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل

مثقال ذرة شرا يره} [الزلزلة: 7 - 8] فكل ما تعمله في هذه الدنيا الفانية

تنال جزاءه إن خيرا فخير وإن  شرا فشر، وتذكر دائما أن الحياة نفس يذهب ولا

يرجع، ولا ينفع الندم بعدها فاعمل لنفسك ولا تقدم ما يفنى على ما يبقى.
# أخي الكريم: إن أجمل سعادة وأعظم لذة يجدها الإنسان في هذه الحياة

الفانية هي طاعة الله ومحبته والقرب إليه وكثرة الدعاء وقد صرح تائبون

كثيرون بأنهم وجدوا أعظم متعة تمتعوها هي القرب إلى الله تعالى وحسن الظن

به وكثرة مراقبته، وأكثر من الدعاء والذكر والاستغفار فلك في 
# كل تسبيحة عشر حسنات، حاول أن لا تجعل وقتك يذهب سدى، أكثر من قراءة

القرآن فلك في كل حرف عشر حسنات، اقرأ كتب العلم والأحاديث النبوية، فقه

نفسك بأمور دينك، عليك بكثرة التطوع والإكثار من صلاة النافلة، وقد قال

النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إنك لن تسجد لله سجدة إلا رفعك بها درجة وحط

عنك بها خطيئة» (1). كن داعيا إلى الله تعالى، كن آمرا للناس بالمعروف

وناهيا لهم عن المنكر، قال تعالى: {ومن أحسن قولا ممن دعا إلى الله وعمل

صالحا وقال إنني من المسلمين} [فصلت: 33]، إياك وأعراض الناس لا تذكر أحدا

بسوء، ولا تغتب أحدا، ولا تؤذي أحدا، وقد قال النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«المسلم من سلم المسلمون من لسانه ويده» (2)، وقال أيضا: «كل المسلم على

المسلم حرام دمه وعرضه وماله» (3)، وهذا نبينا الكريم قد حذرنا من احتقار

المسلمين فقال: «بحسب امرئ من الشر أن يحقر أخاه المسلم» (4) فإذا كان

استحقاره عظيما عند الله فكيف بإنزال الضر به.
# كن رقيبا على نفسك ولسانك فكل كلام تنطقه تحاسب عليه إن كان
# خيرا فخير وإن كان شرا فشر، وقد قال النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إنك لم

تزل سالما ما سكت، فإذا تكلمت كتب لك أو عليك» (5)، وقال أيضا: «رحم الله

عبدا قال خيرا فغنم أو سكت عن شر فسلم» (6) حافظ على نظرك فلا تنظر إلى

محرم، وحافظ على سمعك فلا تسمع محرما، قال تعالى: {إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد

كل أولئك كان عنه مسؤولا} [الإسراء: 36]. حافظ على جوارحك فلا تفعل  محرما.

ولا تنظر إلى صغر المعصية وتحسب الأمر هينا، ولكن انظر إلى من تعصي.

# الزم هذا الدعاء: «اللهم أحسن عاقبتنا في الأمور كلها وأجرنا من خزي

الدنيا وعذاب الآخرة».
# هذا وبالله التوفيق وصلى الله على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه وسلم.
# وكتب
# ماهر بن ياسين بن فحل الدكتور
# العراق - الأنبار - الرمادي
# دار الحديث
# 26/ 2/1426ه‍
#

| مقدمة المؤلف الإمام النووي
# بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
# الحمد لله الواحد القهار، العزيز الغفار، مكور (1) الليل على النهار،

تذكرة لأولي القلوب والأبصار، وتبصرة لذوي الألباب والاعتبار، الذي أيقظ من

خلقه من اصطفاه فزهدهم في هذه الدار، وشغلهم بمراقبته وإدامة الأفكار،

وملازمة الاتعاظ والادكار، ووفقهم للدأب في طاعته، والتأهب لدار القرار،

والحذر مما يسخطه ويوجب دار البوار، والمحافظة على ذلك مع تغاير الأحوال

والأطوار، أحمده أبلغ حمد وأزكاه، وأشمله وأنماه، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله

البر الكريم، الرؤوف الرحيم، وأشهد أن سيدنا محمدا عبده ورسوله، وحبيبه

وخليله، الهادي إلى صراط مستقيم، والداعي إلى دين قويم، صلوات الله وسلامه

عليه، وعلى سائر النبيين، وآل كل، وسائر الصالحين.
# أما بعد، فقد قال الله تعالى: {وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون ما أريد

منهم من رزق وما أريد أن يطعمون} [الذاريات: 56 - 57] وهذا تصريح بأنهم

خلقوا للعبادة، فحق عليهم الاعتناء بما خلقوا له والإعراض عن حظوظ الدنيا

بالزهادة، فإنها دار نفاد لا محل إخلاد، ومركب عبور لا منزل حبور، ومشرع

انفصام لا موطن دوام، فلهذا كان الأيقاظ من أهلها هم العباد، وأعقل الناس

فيها هم الزهاد. قال الله تعالى: {إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من

السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض مما يأكل الناس والأنعام حتى إذا أخذت الأرض

زخرفها وازينت وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها أتاها أمرنا ليلا أو نهارا

فجعلناها حصيدا كأن لم تغن بالأمس كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يتفكرون} [يونس:

24]. والآيات في هذا المعنى كثيرة. 
# ولقد أحسن القائل (1):
# إن لله عبادا فطنا ... طلقوا الدنيا وخافوا الفتنا
# نظروا فيها فلما علموا ... أنها ليست لحي وطنا
# جعلوها لجة  واتخذوا ... صالح الأعمال فيها سفنا
# فإذا كان حالها ما وصفته، وحالنا وما خلقنا له ما قدمته؛ فحق على المكلف

أن يذهب بنفسه مذهب الأخيار، ويسلك مسلك أولي النهى والأبصار، ويتأهب لما

أشرت إليه، ويهتم لما نبهت عليه. وأصوب طريق له في ذلك، وأرشد ما يسلكه من

المسالك، التأدب بما صح عن نبينا سيد الأولين والآخرين، وأكرم السابقين

واللاحقين، صلوات الله وسلامه عليه وعلى سائر النبيين. وقد قال الله تعالى:

{وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى} [المائدة:2] وقد صح عن رسول الله - صلى الله

- Root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Return, turning back; repentance as a return to one's original sound state
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theologically, tawbah is the soul's return from disobedience to obedience, from distance to proximity with Allah
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "returning"; metaphorically denotes the heart's turning away from sin toward Allah
- Root: ز-ر-ع (z-r-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sowing seeds in earth; cultivation
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Metaphor for deeds as seeds whose harvest appears in the Hereafter
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Majāz — actions are likened to seeds; the afterlife is the harvest field
- Root: ر-ق-ب (r-q-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Watching, guarding, observing
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Murāqabah — the servant's constant awareness that Allah observes him
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal watching; metaphorically, the heart's vigilance over itself

chapters.translation:
I say — and with Allah is success:

Advance without hesitation toward sincere repentance before the time passes, for Allah Most High has said: {«So let those who oppose his command beware, lest a trial strike them or a painful punishment afflict them»} [al-Nūr: 63]. And know that Allah has created for every human being numbered breaths and limited hours; when they come to an end, the beats of his heart cease, his record is rolled up, and a barrier is placed between him and this abode — either to a dwelling of intimacy and delight, or to a dwelling of misery and desolation. So whoever sows good words and righteous deeds, Allah will admit him to Paradise and grace him with everlasting bliss; and whoever sows evil deeds and foul words will enter the Fire. Allah Most High said: {«And if they cry for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass that scalds the faces — how wretched the drink, and how evil a resting place»} [al-Kahf: 29]. And recall His saying: {«So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it»} [al-Zalzalah: 7–8]. So everything you do in this fleeting world, you will receive its recompense — if good, then good; if evil, then evil. And always remember that life is a breath that departs and does not return, and regret after it avails nothing. So work for yourself, and do not prefer what perishes over what endures.

My noble brother: The most beautiful happiness and the greatest pleasure a person finds in this fleeting life is obedience to Allah, love of Him, drawing near to Him, and abundance of supplication. Many repentant sinners have testified that the greatest delight they ever experienced was drawing near to Allah Most High, thinking well of Him, and constantly observing His watchfulness. And increase in supplication, remembrance (dhikr), and seeking forgiveness — for in every glorification (tasbīḥah) you have ten good deeds. Strive not to let your time pass in vain. Increase in reading the Qur'an, for in every letter you have ten good deeds. Read books of knowledge and Prophetic hadiths; make yourself learned in the matters of your religion. Be diligent in supererogatory acts and abundant in voluntary prayer (al-nāfilah). The Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — said: «You will not prostrate to Allah with a single prostration except that He raises you by it a degree and removes from you by it a sin.» Be a caller to Allah Most High; be one who commands people to good and forbids them from evil. Allah Most High said: {«And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, works righteousness, and says, 'Indeed, I am among the Muslims'»} [Fuṣṣilat: 33]. Beware of people's honor — do not mention anyone with evil, do not backbite anyone, and do not harm anyone. The Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — said: «The Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.» And he also said: «Everything of a Muslim is sacred to another Muslim: his blood, his honor, and his wealth.» And this noble Prophet of ours has warned us against belittling Muslims, saying: «It is sufficient evil for a person that he belittles his Muslim brother.» So if his belittlement is grave in the sight of Allah, then how much more so is inflicting harm upon him?

Be a watcher over yourself and your tongue, for every word you utter you will be held to account for — if it is good, then good; if it is evil, then evil. The Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — said: «You remain safe as long as you remain silent; but when you speak, it is written for you or against you.» And he also said: «May Allah have mercy on a servant who said good and profited, or remained silent from evil and was safe.» Guard your gaze — do not look at what is forbidden. Guard your hearing — do not listen to what is forbidden. Allah Most High said: {«Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of these will be questioned»} [al-Isrā': 36]. Guard your limbs — do not commit what is forbidden. And do not look at the smallness of the sin and deem the matter trivial; rather, look at the One whom you are disobeying.

Persist in this supplication: «O Allah, make good our end in all matters, and save us from the disgrace of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.»

This is it — and with Allah is success. May Allah send blessings upon our Master Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and grant them peace.

Written by:
Dr. Māhir ibn Yāsīn ibn Faḥl
Iraq — Anbar — Ramadi
Dār al-Ḥadīth
26/2/1426 AH

THE AUTHOR'S INTRODUCTION — IMAM AL-NAWAWĪ

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Praise be to Allah, the One, the Subduer, the Mighty, the Forgiving — He who wraps the night over the day, as a reminder for those possessed of hearts and sight, and an insight for those possessed of intellect and reflection. He who awakened from among His creation those whom He chose, making them renounce this abode, occupying them with watchfulness over Him and constancy of thought, and adherence to admonition and remembrance. He granted them success in persevering in His obedience, in preparing for the abode of permanence, and in fearing what incurs His displeasure and necessitates the abode of ruin — and in maintaining all this amidst changing states and conditions. I praise Him with the most complete and purest praise, the most comprehensive and most abundant. And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah — the Righteous, the Generous, the Kind, the Merciful. And I bear witness that our Master Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, His beloved and intimate friend, the guide to a straight path, and the caller to a sound religion. May Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, upon all the Prophets, upon the families of all of them, and upon all the righteous.

To proceed: Allah Most High has said: {«And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I do not seek from them any provision, nor do I ask that they feed Me»} [al-Dhāriyāt: 56–57]. This is an explicit declaration that they were created for worship. So it is incumbent upon them to attend to that for which they were created, and to turn away from the shares of this world through renunciation (zuhd) — for it is a house of passing away, not a place of remaining; a crossing mount, not a dwelling of joy; a point of severance, not a homeland of permanence. For this reason, the vigilant among its people are the worshippers, and the most intelligent of people in it are the ascetics. Allah Most High said: {«The likeness of the life of this world is only as water which We send down from the sky; then the plants of the earth mingle with it, of which men and cattle eat — until when the earth has taken on its adornment and is beautified, and its people suppose that they have power over it, there comes to it Our command by night or by day, and We make it as a harvest reaped, as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We explain the signs in detail for a people who reflect»} [Yūnus: 24]. And the verses on this meaning are many.

And how excellently the poet said:

"Indeed, for Allah there are intelligent servants — they released this world and feared trials.
They looked into it, and when they knew — that it is not for any living being a homeland,
They made it a sea, and took — righteous deeds within it as ships."

So when its condition is as I have described, and our condition and that for which we were created is as I have presented — then it is incumbent upon the accountable person (al-mukallaf) to take himself along the path of the righteous, to traverse the way of those possessed of sound intellect and sight, to prepare for what I have indicated, and to concern himself with what I have drawn attention to. And the most correct path for him in that, and the most rightly guided course he can take, is to discipline himself with what is authentically established from our Prophet, the master of the first and the last, and the most noble of the predecessors and successors — may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and upon all the Prophets. For Allah Most High has said: {«And cooperate in righteousness and piety»} [al-Mā'idah: 2]. And it is authentically established from the Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — [that he said...]

chapters.title_en: Section 3 — On Sincerity (Ikhlāṣ) and Bringing the Intention (Niyyah) to Presence in All Acts, Words, and States, Both Apparent and Hidden
chapters.arabic_text:
عليه وسلم - أنه قال: «والله في عون العبد ما كان العبد في عون أخيه» (2)،

وأنه قال: «من دل على خير فله مثل أجر فاعله» (3) وأنه قال: «من دعا إلى

هدى كان له من الأجر مثل أجور من تبعه لا ينقص ذلك من أجورهم شيئا» (4)

وأنه قال لعلي - رضي الله عنه: «فوالله لأن يهدي الله بك رجلا واحدا خير لك

من حمر (5) النعم» (6) فرأيت أن أجمع مختصرا من الأحاديث الصحيحة، مشتملا

على ما يكون طريقا لصاحبه إلى الآخرة، ومحصلا لآدابه الباطنة والظاهرة.

جامعا للترغيب والترهيب وسائر أنواع آداب السالكين: من أحاديث الزهد

ورياضات النفوس، وتهذيب الأخلاق، وطهارات القلوب وعلاجها، وصيانة الجوارح

وإزالة 
# اعوجاجها، وغير ذلك من مقاصد العارفين.
# وألتزم فيه أن لا أذكر إلا حديثا صحيحا من الواضحات، مضافا إلى الكتب

الصحيحة المشهورات. وأصدر الأبواب من القرآن العزيز بآيات كريمات، وأوشح ما

يحتاج إلى ضبط أو شرح معنى خفي بنفائس من التنبيهات. وإذا قلت في آخر حديث:

متفق عليه فمعناه: رواه البخاري ومسلم.
# وأرجو إن تم هذا الكتاب أن يكون سائقا للمعتني به إلى الخيرات حاجزا له

عن أنواع القبائح والمهلكات. وأنا سائل أخا انتفع بشيء منه أن يدعو لي (1)،

ولوالدي، ومشايخي، وسائر أحبابنا، والمسلمين أجمعين. وعلى الله الكريم

اعتمادي، وإليه تفويضي واستنادي، وحسبي الله ونعم الوكيل، ولا حول ولا قوة

إلا بالله العزيز الحكيم. 
# بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

$ 1 - باب الإخلاص وإحضار النية في جميع الأعمال والأقوال والأحوال البارزة  والخفية
# قال الله تعالى: {وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين حنفاء

ويقيموا الصلاة ويؤتوا الزكاة وذلك دين القيمة} [البينة: 5]، وقال تعالى:

{لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم} [الحج: 37]، وقال

تعالى: {قل إن تخفوا ما في صدوركم أو تبدوه يعلمه الله} [آل عمران: 29].
#

| 1 - 
# وعن أمير المؤمنين أبي حفص عمر بن الخطاب بن نفيل بن عبد العزى بن رياح

بن عبد الله بن قرط بن رزاح بن عدي بن كعب (1) بن لؤي بن غالب القرشي

العدوي - رضي الله عنه - قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يقول:

«إنما الأعمال بالنيات، وإنما لكل امرىء ما نوى، فمن كانت هجرته إلى الله

ورسوله، فهجرته إلى الله ورسوله، ومن كانت هجرته لدنيا يصيبها، أو امرأة

ينكحها، فهجرته إلى ما هاجر إليه». متفق على صحته. رواه إماما المحدثين،

أبو عبد الله محمد بن إسماعيل بن إبراهيم بن المغيرة بن بردزبه الجعفي

البخاري، وأبو الحسين مسلم بن الحجاج بن مسلم القشيري النيسابوري رضي الله

عنهما في صحيحيهما اللذين هما أصح الكتب المصنفة. (2)

| 2 - 
# وعن أم المؤمنين أم عبد الله عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت: قال رسول الله -

صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يغزو جيش الكعبة فإذا كانوا ببيداء من الأرض يخسف

بأولهم وآخرهم».
# قالت: قلت: يا

| [ص: 10]
# رسول الله، كيف يخسف بأولهم وآخرهم وفيهم أسواقهم (1) ومن ليس منهم؟!

قال: «يخسف بأولهم وآخرهم ثم يبعثون على نياتهم». متفق عليه. (2) هذا لفظ

البخاري.

| 3 - 
# وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت: قال النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا

هجرة بعد الفتح، ولكن جهاد ونية، وإذا استنفرتم (1) فانفروا». متفق عليه.

(2)
# ومعناه: لا هجرة من مكة لأنها صارت دار إسلام.

| 4 - 
# وعن أبي عبد الله جابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري رضي الله عنهما، قال: كنا مع

النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في غزاة، فقال: «إن بالمدينة لرجالا ما سرتم

مسيرا، ولا قطعتم واديا، إلا كانوا معكم حبسهم المرض». وفي رواية: «إلا

شركوكم في الأجر». رواه  مسلم. (1)
# ورواه البخاري عن أنس - رضي الله عنه - قال: رجعنا من غزوة تبوك مع النبي

- صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال: «إن أقواما خلفنا بالمدينة ما سلكنا شعبا (2)

ولا واديا، إلا وهم معنا؛ حبسهم العذر».

| 5 - 
# وعن أبي يزيد معن بن يزيد بن الأخنس - رضي الله عنهم - وهو وأبوه وجده

صحابيون، قال: كان أبي يزيد أخرج دنانير يتصدق بها، فوضعها عند رجل في

المسجد، فجئت فأخذتها فأتيته بها. فقال: والله، ما إياك أردت، فخاصمته إلى

رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال: «لك ما نويت يا يزيد، ولك ما أخذت

يا معن». رواه البخاري. (1)

| 6 - 
# وعن أبي إسحاق سعد بن أبي وقاص مالك بن أهيب بن عبد مناف بن زهرة بن كلاب

(1) بن مرة بن كعب بن لؤي القرشي الزهري - رضي الله عنه - أحد العشرة (2)

المشهود لهم بالجنة - رضي الله عنهم - قال: جاءني رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - يعودني عام حجة الوداع من وجع اشتد بي، فقلت: يا رسول الله،

إني قد بلغ بي من الوجع ما ترى، وأنا ذو مال ولا يرثني إلا ابنة لي،

أفأتصدق بثلثي مالي؟ قال: «لا»، قلت: فالشطر يا رسول الله؟ فقال: «لا»،

قلت: فالثلث يا رسول الله؟ قال: «الثلث والثلث كثير - أو كبير - إنك إن تذر

ورثتك أغنياء خير من أن تذرهم عالة (3) يتكففون الناس، وإنك لن تنفق نفقة

تبتغي بها وجه الله إلا أجرت عليها حتى ما تجعل في في امرأتك»، قال: فقلت:

يا رسول الله، أخلف (4) بعد أصحابي؟ قال: «إنك لن تخلف فتعمل عملا تبتغي به

وجه الله إلا ازددت به درجة ورفعة، ولعلك أن تخلف حتى ينتفع بك أقوام ويضر

بك آخرون. اللهم أمض لأصحابي هجرتهم ولا تردهم على أعقابهم، لكن البائس سعد

بن خولة» يرثي له رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن مات بمكة. متفق

عليه. (5)

| 7 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة عبد الرحمان بن صخر - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله -
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ل-ص (khalasa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Purity and clarity of a thing from admixture; the essence of a substance free from dross.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ikhlāṣ in worship is the purification of the act from every motive other than the Divine Countenance — the theological opposite of shirk (associationism) in intention.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — pure gold; metaphorical (majāz) — the heart's devotion stripped of all worldly aims.
- Root: ن-و-ي (nawā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Intent, purpose, resolve; the heart's direction toward an aim.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Niyyah is the volitional orientation (qaṣd) that distinguishes acts of obedience from mere habit, and differentiates one act of worship from another.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical distance; metaphorical — the soul's journey toward its goal, as in hijrah (emigration).
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Restriction (al-Ḥaṣr bi-innamā) — the particle «إنما» restricts the predicate to the subject, establishing that the value of deeds is exclusively contingent upon intention.
chapters.translation:
I say — may Allah grant us success:

Know that the Commander of the Believers, Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ibn Nufayl — may Allah be pleased with him — narrated that the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Verily, actions are but by intentions, and verily, every man shall have only what he intended. So whoever's emigration (hijrah) was to Allah and His Messenger, his emigration is to Allah and His Messenger; and whoever's emigration was for a worldly gain he seeks, or a woman he wishes to marry, then his emigration is to that which he emigrated.» This is agreed upon as authentic. It was narrated by the two Imams of hadith: Abū ʿAbdillāh Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Mughīrah ibn Bardizbah al-Juʿfī al-Bukhārī, and Abū al-Ḥusayn Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj ibn Muslim al-Qushayrī al-Naysābūrī — may Allah be pleased with them both — in their two authentic collections, which are the most authentic books ever compiled.

And from the Mother of the Believers, Umm ʿAbdillāh ʿĀʾishah — may Allah be pleased with her — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «An army will march against the Kaʿbah, and when they reach a barren plain (baydāʾ) of the earth, the first of them and the last of them will be swallowed up by the earth.» She said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, how can the first and last of them be swallowed, when among them are their merchants and those who are not of them? He said: «The first and last of them will be swallowed, then they will be resurrected according to their intentions.» Agreed upon. This is the wording of al-Bukhārī.

And from ʿĀʾishah — may Allah be pleased with her — who said: The Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «There is no emigration (hijrah) after the conquest, but rather jihad and intention; and if you are summoned to mobilize, then mobilize.» Agreed upon. Its meaning: there is no emigration from Mecca, for it has become an abode of Islam.

And from Abū ʿAbdillāh Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī — may Allah be pleased with them both — who said: We were with the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — on a campaign, and he said: «Verily, there are men in Medina who, whatever journey you have traveled, and whatever valley you have crossed, were with you — illness having detained them.» And in another narration: «They shared with you in the reward.» Narrated by Muslim. Al-Bukhārī narrated it from Anas — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: We returned from the campaign of Tabūk with the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — and he said: «Verily, there are people we left behind in Medina who, whatever mountain pass we traversed, or valley we crossed, were with us — a valid excuse having detained them.»

And from Abū Yazīd Maʿn ibn Yazīd ibn al-Akhnas — may Allah be pleased with them all — and he, his father, and his grandfather were all Companions — who said: My father Yazīd had brought out some dinars to give in charity, and he placed them with a man in the mosque. I came and took them, and brought them to him. He said: By Allah, I did not intend you! So I disputed with him before the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — and he said: «You shall have what you intended, O Yazīd, and you shall have what you took, O Maʿn.» Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

And from Abū Isḥāq Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ Mālik ibn Uhayb ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Zuhrah ibn Kilāb ibn Murrah ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy al-Qurashī al-Zuhrī — may Allah be pleased with him — one of the ten given glad tidings of Paradise — may Allah be pleased with them all — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — came to visit me during the Farewell Pilgrimage due to an illness that had become severe upon me. I said: O Messenger of Allah, my illness has reached the extent you see, and I am a man of wealth, and none inherits from me except a single daughter. Shall I give two-thirds of my wealth in charity? He said: «No.» I said: Then half, O Messenger of Allah? He said: «No.» I said: Then a third? He said: «A third, and a third is much — or great. Verily, if you leave your heirs wealthy, that is better than leaving them poor, begging from people. And verily, you shall not spend an expenditure seeking thereby the Face of Allah, except that you will be rewarded for it — even the morsel you place in your wife's mouth.» He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, will I be left behind after my companions? He said: «Verily, you shall not be left behind and perform a deed seeking thereby the Face of Allah, except that you will be raised thereby in degree and rank. And perhaps you will be left behind until some people benefit by you, and others are harmed by you. O Allah, complete the emigration of my companions, and do not turn them back on their heels. But the wretched one is Saʿd ibn Khawlah» — the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — grieving for him, for he had died in Mecca. Agreed upon.

And from Abū Hurayrah ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣakhr — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Verily, Allah does not look at your bodies, nor at your forms, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.» Narrated by Muslim.

And from Abū Mūsā ʿAbdillāh ibn Qays al-Ashʿarī — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — was asked about a man who fights out of valor, and a man who fights out of tribal zeal, and a man who fights for show — which of them is in the path of Allah? He said: «Whoever fights so that the Word of Allah be the highest, he is in the path of Allah.» Agreed upon.

And from Abū Bakrah Nufayʿ ibn al-Ḥārith — may Allah be pleased with him — that the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «When two Muslims meet with their swords, both the killer and the killed are in the Fire.» I said: O Messenger of Allah, this is the killer — so what of the killed? He said: «Verily, he was eager to kill his companion.» Agreed upon.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «The prayer of a man in congregation is twenty-five times more excellent than his prayer in his house or in his market. That is because when he performs ablution and perfects it, then goes out to the mosque, seeking nothing but the prayer, then every step he takes raises him a degree and removes from him a sin, until he enters the mosque. And when he enters, he is in prayer as long as the prayer detains him, and the angels send blessings upon him as long as he remains in his place of prayer, saying: O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy upon him. And one of you remains in prayer as long as he awaits the prayer.» Agreed upon.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Whoever goes to the mosque in the morning or the evening, Allah prepares for him a hospitality in Paradise, morning and evening.» Agreed upon.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — that the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Whoever purifies himself in his house, then walks to one of the houses of Allah to fulfill an obligation of the obligations of Allah, then his two steps — one of them removes a sin, and the other raises him a degree.» Narrated by Muslim.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Shall I not guide you to that by which Allah erases sins and raises degrees?» They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: «Completing the ablution despite hardship, and many steps to the mosques, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer — that is the ribāṭ (garrisoning the frontier).» Narrated by Muslim.

And from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣakhr — may Allah be pleased with him — that the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «When you see a man frequenting the mosques, then bear witness to his faith.» And in a narration: «Bear witness to his faith, for Allah said: {Verily, the mosques of Allah are only to be maintained by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day} [al-Tawbah: 18].» Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, who said: a good and authentic hadith.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Whoever performs ablution and perfects it, then comes to the Friday prayer, listens and remains silent, his sins between that Friday and the next are forgiven, plus three days. And whoever touches the pebbles has committed a vain act.» Narrated by Muslim.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «The five daily prayers, and the Friday prayer to the next Friday, are an expiation for what is between them, as long as one avoids the major sins.» Narrated by Muslim.

And from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — say: «Whoever performs ablution and perfects it, then prays the obligatory prayer, his sins that were between it and the previous prayer are forgiven.» Narrated by Muslim.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «The angels pray for one of you as long as he remains in his place of prayer, as long as he does not break his ablution, saying: O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy upon him.» Agreed upon.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Whoever says: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, one hundred times in a day, his sins are erased, even if they were like the foam of the sea.» Agreed upon.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Whoever says: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent — one hundred times in a day, it is for him the equivalent of freeing ten slaves, and one hundred good deeds are written for him, and one hundred sins are erased from him, and it is a protection for him from Satan for that day until evening. And no one brings anything better than what he brought, except a man who does more than that.» Agreed upon.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Whoever says: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah — one hundred times in the morning and one hundred times in the evening, no one comes on the Day of Resurrection with anything better than what he brought, except a man who said the like of what he said, or more.» Narrated by Muslim.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Whoever says: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah — one hundred times, his sins are erased, even if they were like the foam of the sea.» Narrated by Muslim.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Two words are light on the tongue, heavy in the balance, beloved to the Merciful: Glory be to Allah and by His praise; Glory be to Allah the Mighty.» Agreed upon.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Whoever says: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent — ten times, it is as if he freed four slaves from the children of Ismāʿīl.» Narrated by Muslim.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Whoever says: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest — it is for him a charity from every good deed he has done.» Narrated by Muslim.

And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Whoever says: There is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest — his Lord confirms him and says: There is no god but Me, and I am the Greatest. And whoever says: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner — his Lord confirms him and says: There is no god but Me, alone, with no partner. And whoever says: There is no god but Allah, His is the dominion and His is the praise — his Lord confirms him and says: There is no god but Me, Mine is the dominion and Mine is the praise. And whoever says: There is no god but Allah, and there is no power and no strength except in Allah — his Lord confirms him and says: There is no god but Me, and there is no power and no strength except in Me.» Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, who said: a good and authentic hadith.

صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن الله لا ينظر  إلى أجسامكم، ولا إلى صوركم، ولكن

ينظر إلى قلوبكم وأعمالكم». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 8 - 
# وعن أبي موسى عبد الله بن قيس الأشعري - رضي الله عنه - قال: سئل رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن الرجل يقاتل شجاعة، ويقاتل حمية، ويقاتل

رياء، أي ذلك في سبيل الله؟ فقال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قاتل

لتكون كلمة الله هي العليا، فهو في سبيل الله». متفق عليه. (1)

| 9 - 
# وعن أبي بكرة نفيع بن الحارث الثقفي - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - قال: «إذا التقى المسلمان بسيفيهما فالقاتل والمقتول في

النار». قلت: يا رسول الله،
# هذا القاتل فما بال المقتول؟ قال: «إنه كان حريصا على قتل صاحبه». متفق

عليه. (1)

| 10 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «صلاة الرجل في جماعة تزيد على صلاته في سوقه وبيته بضعا (1) وعشرين

درجة، وذلك أن أحدهم إذا توضأ فأحسن الوضوء، ثم أتى المسجد لا يريد إلا

الصلاة، لا ينهزه إلا الصلاة: لم يخط خطوة إلا رفع له بها درجة، وحط عنه

بها خطيئة حتى يدخل المسجد، فإذا دخل المسجد كان في الصلاة ما كانت الصلاة

هي تحبسه، والملائكة يصلون على أحدكم ما دام في مجلسه الذي صلى فيه،

يقولون: اللهم ارحمه، اللهم اغفر له، اللهم تب عليه، ما لم يؤذ فيه، ما لم

يحدث فيه». متفق عليه، (2) وهذا لفظ مسلم.
# وقوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ينهزه» هو بفتح الياء والهاء وبالزاي: أي

يخرجه وينهضه.

| 11 - 
# وعن أبي العباس عبد الله بن عباس بن عبد المطلب رضي الله عنهما، عن رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فيما يروي عن ربه، تبارك وتعالى، قال: «إن

الله كتب الحسنات والسيئات ثم بين ذلك، فمن هم (1) بحسنة فلم يعملها كتبها

الله تبارك وتعالى عنده حسنة كاملة، وإن هم بها فعملها كتبها الله عشر

حسنات إلى سبعمئة ضعف إلى أضعاف كثيرة، وإن هم بسيئة فلم يعملها كتبها الله

تعالى عنده حسنة  كاملة، وإن هم بها فعملها كتبها الله سيئة واحدة». متفق

عليه. (2)

| 12 - 
# وعن أبي عبد الرحمان عبد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنهما، قال:

سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يقول: «انطلق ثلاثة نفر (1) ممن كان

قبلكم حتى آواهم المبيت إلى غار فدخلوه، فانحدرت صخرة من الجبل فسدت عليهم

الغار، فقالوا: إنه لا ينجيكم من هذه الصخرة إلا أن تدعوا الله بصالح

أعمالكم. 
# قال رجل منهم: اللهم كان لي أبوان شيخان كبيران، وكنت لا أغبق (1) قبلهما

أهلا ولا مالا، فنأى (2) بي طلب الشجر يوما فلم أرح عليهما حتى ناما، فحلبت

لهما غبوقهما فوجدتهما نائمين، فكرهت أن أوقظهما وأن أغبق قبلهما أهلا أو

مالا، فلبثت - والقدح على يدي - أنتظر استيقاظهما حتى برق الفجر والصبية

يتضاغون (3) عند قدمي، فاستيقظا فشربا غبوقهما. اللهم إن كنت فعلت ذلك

ابتغاء وجهك ففرج عنا ما نحن فيه من هذه الصخرة، فانفرجت شيئا لا يستطيعون

الخروج منه.
# قال الآخر: اللهم إنه كانت لي ابنة عم، كانت أحب الناس إلي - وفي رواية:

كنت أحبها كأشد ما يحب الرجال النساء - فأردتها على نفسها (4) فامتنعت مني

حتى ألمت بها سنة من السنين فجاءتني فأعطيتها عشرين ومئة دينار على أن تخلي

بيني وبين نفسها ففعلت، حتى إذا قدرت عليها - وفي رواية: فلما قعدت بين

رجليها، قالت: اتق الله ولا تفض الخاتم إلا بحقه (5)، فانصرفت عنها وهي أحب

الناس إلي وتركت الذهب الذي أعطيتها. اللهم إن كنت فعلت ذلك ابتغاء وجهك

فافرج عنا ما نحن فيه، فانفرجت الصخرة، غير أنهم لا يستطيعون الخروج منها.
# وقال الثالث: اللهم استأجرت أجراء وأعطيتهم أجرهم غير رجل واحد ترك الذي

له وذهب، فثمرت أجره حتى كثرت منه الأموال، فجاءني بعد حين، فقال: يا عبد

الله، أد إلي أجري، فقلت: كل ما ترى من أجرك: من الإبل والبقر والغنم

والرقيق، فقال: يا عبد الله، لا تستهزىء بي! فقلت: لا أستهزئ بك، فأخذه كله

فاستاقه فلم يترك منه شيئا. اللهم إن كنت فعلت ذلك ابتغاء  وجهك فافرج عنا

ما نحن فيه، فانفرجت الصخرة فخرجوا يمشون». (6) متفق عليه. (7)

$ 2 - باب التوبة
# قال العلماء: التوبة واجبة من كل ذنب، فإن كانت المعصية بين العبد وبين

الله تعالى لا تتعلق بحق آدمي فلها ثلاثة شروط:
# أحدها: أن يقلع عن المعصية.
# والثاني: أن يندم على فعلها.
# والثالث: أن يعزم أن لا يعود إليها أبدا.
# فإن فقد أحد الثلاثة لم تصح توبته.
# وإن كانت المعصية تتعلق بآدمي فشروطها أربعة: هذه الثلاثة، وأن يبرأ من

حق صاحبها، فإن كانت مالا أو نحوه رده إليه، وإن كانت حد قذف ونحوه مكنه

منه أو طلب عفوه، وإن كانت غيبة استحله منها. ويجب أن يتوب من جميع الذنوب،

فإن تاب من بعضها صحت توبته عند أهل الحق من ذلك الذنب وبقي عليه الباقي.

وقد تظاهرت دلائل الكتاب والسنة، وإجماع الأمة على وجوب التوبة.
# قال الله تعالى: {وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيه المؤمنون لعلكم تفلحون}

[النور: 31]، وقال تعالى: {وأن استغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه} [هود: 3]،

وقال تعالى: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا توبوا إلى الله توبة نصوحا} [التحريم:

8].
#

| 13 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - يقول: «والله إني لأستغفر الله وأتوب إليه في اليوم أكثر من سبعين

مرة». رواه البخاري. (1)

| 14 - 
# وعن الأغر بن يسار المزني - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم: «يا أيها الناس، توبوا إلى الله واستغفروه، فإني أتوب في

اليوم مائة مرة». رواه مسلم. (1)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ظ-ر (na-ẓa-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To look, to gaze, to consider with perception; the physical act of sight (ruʾyah) versus the inward glance of divine assessment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine "looking" (naẓar) is an expression of His mercy and acceptance (riḍwān), not a corporeal act; it denotes His turning toward a servant with compassion or away with disregard.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sight is impossible for Allah; here it is a metaphor (majāz) for His judgment and recompense based on the heart's sincerity, not outward form.
- Root: ق-ت-ل (qa-ta-la)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fight, to kill; the act of combat with intent to slay.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the sacred law, qitāl is sanctioned solely for the elevation of Allah's word; the intention (niyyah) determines its validity as jihād fī sabīlillāh.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal act of fighting is neutral; its value is metaphorical—transformed by the underlying motive (shajāʿah, ḥamiyyah, riyāʾ) into either worship or blameworthy aggression.
- Root: ت-و-ب (ta-wa-ba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To return, to revert; the act of turning back from a path.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tawbah is the servant's return to Allah from disobedience, entailing cessation (iqlāʿ), regret (nadam), and resolve (ʿazm); it is a covenant of renewal.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally "returning," but metaphorically the soul's turning from sin to obedience, requiring the abandonment of the transgression as a condition of authenticity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The particle "idhā" introduces a conditional protasis, with the apodosis governed by the resultant state; e.g., "idhā tawaddaʾa... lam yakhṭu khaṭwah" (when he performs ablution... he does not take a step) demonstrates the binding of consequence to condition, requiring precise temporal sequencing.
chapters.translation:
The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Indeed, Allah does not look at your bodies, nor at your forms, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.»} Narrated by Muslim. (1)

| 8 -
# And on the authority of Abū Mūsā ʿAbdullāh ibn Qays al-Ashʿarī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a man who fights out of courage (shajāʿah), and a man who fights out of tribal zeal (ḥamiyyah), and a man who fights out of ostentation (riyāʾ)—which of these is in the path of Allah? So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is the highest, then he is in the path of Allah.»} Agreed upon. (1)

| 9 -
# And on the authority of Abū Bakrah Nufayʿ ibn al-Ḥārith al-Thaqafī, may Allah be pleased with him: That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«When two Muslims meet with their swords, then the killer and the killed are in the Fire.»} I said: O Messenger of Allah, this is the killer—what then of the killed? He said: {«Indeed, he was eager to kill his companion.»} Agreed upon. (1)

| 10 -
# And on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«A man's prayer in congregation exceeds his prayer in his marketplace and his house by twenty-some degrees. That is because when one of them performs ablution and perfects his ablution, then comes to the mosque intending nothing but the prayer, nothing impelling him but the prayer—he does not take a single step except that he is raised one degree thereby, and one sin is removed from him thereby, until he enters the mosque. When he enters the mosque, he is in a state of prayer as long as the prayer is what detains him. And the angels send blessings upon one of you as long as he remains in his place where he prayed, saying: O Allah, have mercy on him; O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, turn in repentance upon him—as long as he does not harm anyone therein, as long as he does not invalidate his ablution therein.»} Agreed upon, (2) and this is the wording of Muslim.
# And his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«yanhazuhu»}—it is with a fatḥah on the yāʾ and the hāʾ, and with a zāy: meaning, it impels him out and rouses him.

| 11 -
# And on the authority of Abū al-ʿAbbās ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in what he narrates from his Lord, Blessed and Exalted, who said: {«Indeed, Allah has written down the good deeds and the evil deeds, then He clarified that. So whoever intends a good deed and does not perform it, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, writes it down with Him as a complete good deed. And if he intends it and performs it, Allah writes it down as ten good deeds up to seven hundred multiples, up to many multiples. And if he intends an evil deed and does not perform it, Allah, Exalted, writes it down with Him as a complete good deed. And if he intends it and performs it, Allah writes it down as a single evil deed.»} Agreed upon. (2)

| 12 -
# And on the authority of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: {«Three men set out from among those before you, until the night's lodging brought them to a cave, and they entered it. Then a rock rolled down from the mountain and sealed the cave upon them. They said: Nothing will save you from this rock except that you supplicate Allah with your righteous deeds.
# One of them said: O Allah, I had two elderly parents, and I would not give my family or wealth to drink before them. One day, the search for trees took me far away, and I did not return to them until they had fallen asleep. So I milked their evening drink for them, and I found them sleeping. I disliked waking them, and I disliked giving my family or wealth to drink before them. So I remained—the cup in my hand—waiting for their awakening until the dawn broke, and the children were crying with hunger at my feet. Then they awoke and drank their evening drink. O Allah, if I did that seeking Your Face, then relieve us from what we are in of this rock. So it opened a little, but they could not exit from it.
# The other said: O Allah, I had a cousin—she was the most beloved of people to me—and in one narration: I loved her as intensely as men love women. I sought her for myself, but she refused me, until a year of famine afflicted her. Then she came to me, and I gave her one hundred and twenty dinars on the condition that she yield herself to me. She did, until when I was able over her—and in one narration: when she sat between my legs—she said: Fear Allah, and do not break the seal except by its right. So I turned away from her, though she was the most beloved of people to me, and I left the gold I had given her. O Allah, if I did that seeking Your Face, then relieve us from what we are in. So the rock opened, but they could not exit from it.
# The third said: O Allah, I hired laborers and gave them their wages, except one man who left his due and went away. So I invested his wage until wealth multiplied from it. Then he came to me after a time and said: O servant of Allah, pay me my wage. I said: All that you see is your wage—of camels, cattle, sheep, and slaves. He said: O servant of Allah, do not mock me! I said: I do not mock you. So he took it all and drove it away, leaving nothing of it. O Allah, if I did that seeking Your Face, then relieve us from what we are in. So the rock opened, and they walked out.»} (6) Agreed upon. (7)

$ 2 - Chapter on Repentance (Tawbah)
# The scholars said: Repentance is obligatory from every sin. If the disobedience is between the servant and Allah, Exalted, not involving a right of a human being, then it has three conditions:
# First: that he desists from the disobedience.
# Second: that he regrets having done it.
# Third: that he resolves never to return to it.
# If any of the three is missing, his repentance is not valid.
# If the disobedience involves a human being, then its conditions are four: these three, and that he absolves himself of the right of its owner. If it is wealth or the like, he returns it to him. If it is a hadd punishment for slander (qadhf) or the like, he enables him to exact it or seeks his pardon. If it is backbiting (ghībah), he asks him to absolve him. And it is obligatory to repent from all sins. If he repents from some of them, his repentance is valid, according to the people of truth (ahl al-ḥaqq), for that particular sin, and the rest remains upon him.
# And the evidences of the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the Ummah have concurred on the obligation of repentance.
# Allah, Exalted, said: {«And turn in repentance to Allah, all of you, O believers, that you may succeed»} [al-Nūr: 31], and He said: {«And that you seek forgiveness of your Lord, then repent to Him»} [Hūd: 3], and He said: {«O you who believe, repent to Allah with sincere repentance»} [al-Taḥrīm: 8].
#

| 13 -
# And on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: {«By Allah, I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him in the day more than seventy times.»} Narrated by al-Bukhārī. (1)

| 14 -
# And on the authority of al-Agharr ibn Yasār al-Muzanī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«O people, repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness, for I repent in the day one hundred times.»} Narrated by Muslim. (1)

chapters.title_en: Section 5 — On Sincere Repentance (Al-Tawbah) and the Vastness of Divine Mercy
chapters.arabic_text:
| 15 - 
# وعن أبي حمزة أنس بن مالك الأنصاري - خادم رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لله أفرح

بتوبة عبده من أحدكم سقط على بعيره وقد أضله في أرض فلاة (1)». متفق عليه.

(2)

| [ص: 15]
# وفي رواية لمسلم: «لله أشد فرحا بتوبة عبده حين يتوب إليه من أحدكم كان

على راحلته بأرض فلاة، فانفلتت منه، وعليها طعامه وشرابه فأيس منها، فأتى

شجرة فاضطجع في ظلها وقد أيس من  راحلته، فبينما هو كذلك إذ هو بها قائمة

عنده، فأخذ بخطامها (3)، ثم قال من شدة الفرح: اللهم أنت عبدي وأنا ربك!

أخطأ من شدة الفرح».

| 16 - 
# وعن أبي موسى عبد الله بن قيس الأشعري - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - قال: «إن الله تعالى يبسط يده بالليل ليتوب مسيء النهار،

ويبسط يده بالنهار ليتوب مسيء الليل، حتى تطلع الشمس من مغربها». رواه

مسلم. (1)

| 17 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «من تاب قبل أن تطلع الشمس من مغربها تاب الله عليه». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 18 - 
# وعن أبي عبد الرحمان عبد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنهما، عن النبي

- صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «إن الله - عز وجل - يقبل توبة العبد ما لم

يغرغر (1)». رواه الترمذي، (2) وقال: «حديث حسن».

| 19 -
