She would say to him: 'What an excellent man — a man who has not touched our bed, nor searched our private place (kanaf), since we came to him.' When this went on for a long time, he mentioned it to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: 'Bring him to me.' So I met him afterward, and he said: 'How do you fast?' I said: 'Every day.' He said: 'And how do you complete the Qur'an?' I said: 'Every night.' And he mentioned something similar to what has preceded. And he used to recite to some of his family the seventh [portion] which he would recite, presenting it during the day so that it would be lighter for him at night; and when he wanted to gain strength, he would break his fast for some days and count them, then fast an equal number, disliking to abandon anything upon which the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had left him."

All these narrations are authentic; most are in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs, and a few in one of them.

---

**Hadith 151** — On the authority of Abū Rabīʿī Ḥanẓalah ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Usayyidī, the scribe, one of the scribes of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, met me and said: "How are you, O Ḥanẓalah?" I said: "Ḥanẓalah has become a hypocrite (nāfaqa)!" He said: "Glory be to Allah! What are you saying?!" I said: "When we are with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, he reminds us of Paradise and the Fire as if we see them with our very eyes (kaʾannā raʾy al-ʿayn). But when we leave the presence of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, we fondle our wives, our children, and our livelihoods, and we forget much of that." Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "By Allah, we indeed encounter the like of this." So I and Abū Bakr set out until we entered upon the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. I said: "Ḥanẓalah has become a hypocrite, O Messenger of Allah!" The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "And what is that?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, when we are with you, you remind us of the Fire and Paradise as if we see them with our very eyes; but when we leave your presence, we fondle our wives, our children, and our livelihoods, and we forget much of that." The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "By Him in Whose hand is my soul, if you were to persist in what you are upon when with me, and in remembrance, the angels would shake your hands on your beds and in your paths. But, O Ḥanẓalah, an hour and an hour" — three times. Narrated by Muslim.

His saying "Rabīʿī" is with kasrah on the rāʾ. And "al-Usayyidī" is with ḍammah on the hamzah and fatḥah on the sīn, followed by a shaddah on the yāʾ with kasrah. His saying "ʿāfasnā" is with the unpointed ʿayn and sīn, meaning: we handled and played with. And "al-ḍayʿāt" (the livelihoods) means: the means of subsistence.

---

**Hadith 152** — On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: While the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was delivering a sermon, he noticed a man standing [in the sun]. He asked about him, and they said: "This is Abū Isrāʾīl, who has vowed to stand in the sun, not to sit, not to seek shade, not to speak, and to fast." The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Command him to speak, to seek shade, and to sit, and to complete his fast." Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

---

**Section 15 — On Persevering in Righteous Deeds**

Allah, the Exalted, has said: {«ألم يأن للذين آمنوا أن تخشع قلوبهم لذكر الله وما نزل من الحق ولا يكونوا كالذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبل فطال عليهم الأمد فقست قلوبهم»} [al-Ḥadīd: 16] — "Has not the time come for those who believe that their hearts should be humbled (takhshaʿa) to the remembrance of Allah and what has come down of the truth, and that they should not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and the term was prolonged for them, so their hearts became hard?" And He, the Exalted, said: {«وقفينا بعيسى ابن مريم وآتيناه الأنجيل وجعلنا في قلوب الذين اتبعوه رأفة ورحمة ورهبانية ابتدعوها ما كتبناها عليهم إلا ابتغاء رضوان الله فما رعوها حق رعايتها»} [al-Ḥadīd: 27] — "And We sent following in their footsteps Jesus, son of Mary, and We gave him the Gospel, and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy and monasticism (rahbāniyyah), which they innovated — We did not prescribe it for them except [seeking] the pleasure of Allah — but they did not observe it with due observance." And He, the Exalted, said: {«ولا تكونوا كالتي نقضت غزلها من بعد قوة أنكاثا»} [al-Naḥl: 92] — "And do not be like her who unravels her thread after its strength, into broken strands." And He, the Exalted, said: {«واعبد ربك حتى يأتيك اليقين»} [al-Ḥijr: 99] — "And worship your Lord until certainty (al-yaqīn) comes to you."

As for the ḥadīths, among them is the ḥadīth of ʿĀʾishah: "And the most beloved of religion to him was that upon which its practitioner persevered (mā dāwama ṣāḥibuhu ʿalayhi)." This has already preceded in the previous section.

---

**Hadith 153** — On the authority of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever sleeps past his nightly portion (ḥizb) — or past part of it — and then recites it between the dawn prayer and the noon prayer, it is written for him as if he had recited it in the night." Narrated by Muslim.

chapters.title_en: Section 22 — The Command to Preserve the Sunnah and Its Etiquettes
chapters.arabic_text:
| 154 - 
# وعن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما، قال: قال رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم: «يا عبد الله، لا تكن مثل فلان، كان يقوم الليل فترك قيام

الليل». متفق عليه. (1)

| 155 - 
# وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت: كان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

إذا فاتته الصلاة من الليل من وجع أو غيره، صلى من النهار ثنتي عشرة ركعة.

رواه مسلم. (1)

$ 16 - باب في الأمر بالمحافظة على السنة وآدابها
# قال الله تعالى: {وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا} [الحشر:

7]، وقال تعالى: {وما ينطق عن الهوى إن هو إلا وحي يوحى} [النجم:3 - 4]،

وقال تعالى: {قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله ويغفر لكم

ذنوبكم} [آل عمران: 31]، وقال تعالى: {لقد كان لكم في رسول الله أسوة حسنة

لمن كان يرجو الله واليوم الآخر} [الأحزاب:21]، وقال تعالى: {فلا وربك لا

يؤمنون حتى يحكموك فيما شجر بينهم ثم لا يجدوا في أنفسهم حرجا مما قضيت

ويسلموا تسليما} [النساء: 65]، وقال تعالى: {فإن تنازعتم في شيء فردوه إلى

الله والرسول} [النساء: 59] قال العلماء: معناه إلى الكتاب والسنة، وقال

تعالى: {من يطع الرسول فقد أطاع الله} [النساء:80]، وقال تعالى: {وإنك

لتهدي إلى صراط مستقيم صراط الله} [الشورى: 52 - 53]، وقال تعالى: {فليحذر

الذين يخالفون عن أمره أن تصيبهم فتنة أو يصيبهم عذاب أليم} [النور: 63]،

وقال تعالى: {واذكرن ما يتلى في بيوتكن من آيات الله والحكمة} [الأحزاب:

34]، والآيات في الباب  كثيرة.
# 
# وأما الأحاديث:

| 156 - 
# فالأول: عن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

قال: «دعوني ما تركتكم، إنما أهلك من كان قبلكم كثرة سؤالهم واختلافهم على

أنبيائهم، فإذا نهيتكم عن شيء فاجتنبوه، وإذا أمرتكم بأمر فأتوا منه ما

استطعتم». متفق عليه. (1)

| 157 - 
# الثاني: عن أبي نجيح العرباض بن سارية - رضي الله عنه - قال: وعظنا رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - موعظة بليغة وجلت منها القلوب، وذرفت منها

العيون، فقلنا: يا رسول الله، كأنها موعظة مودع فأوصنا، قال: «أوصيكم بتقوى

الله، والسمع والطاعة، وإن تأمر عليكم عبد حبشي، وإنه من يعش منكم فسيرى

اختلافا كثيرا، فعليكم بسنتي وسنة الخلفاء الراشدين المهديين، عضوا عليها

بالنواجذ، وإياكم ومحدثات الأمور؛ فإن كل بدعة ضلالة». رواه أبو داود

والترمذي، وقال: «حديث حسن صحيح» (1).

| [ص: 73]
# «النواجذ» بالذال المعجمة: الأنياب، وقيل: الأضراس.

| 158 - 
# الثالث: عن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم

- قال: «كل أمتي يدخلون الجنة إلا من أبى (1)». قيل: ومن يأبى يا رسول

الله؟ قال: «من أطاعني دخل الجنة، ومن عصاني فقد أبى». رواه البخاري. (2)

| 159 - 
# الرابع: عن أبي مسلم، وقيل: أبي إياس سلمة بن عمرو بن الأكوع - رضي الله

عنه: أن رجلا أكل عند رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بشماله، فقال: «كل

بيمينك» قال: لا أستطيع. قال: «لا استطعت» ما منعه إلا الكبر فما رفعها إلى

فيه. رواه مسلم. (1)

| 160 - 
# الخامس: عن أبي عبد الله النعمان بن بشير رضي الله عنهما، قال: سمعت رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يقول: «لتسون صفوفكم، أو ليخالفن الله بين

وجوهكم». متفق عليه. (1)
# وفي رواية لمسلم: كان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يسوي صفوفنا حتى

كأنما يسوي بها القداح (2) حتى إذا رأى أنا قد عقلنا عنه. ثم خرج يوما فقام

حتى كاد أن يكبر فرأى رجلا باديا صدره، فقال: «عباد الله، لتسون صفوفكم أو

ليخالفن الله بين وجوهكم».

| 161 - 
# السادس: عن أبي موسى - رضي الله عنه - قال:  احترق بيت بالمدينة على أهله

من الليل، فلما حدث رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بشأنهم، قال: «إن هذه

النار عدو لكم، فإذا نمتم، فأطفئوها عنكم». متفق عليه. (1)

| 162 - 
# السابع: عنه، قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن مثل ما بعثني

الله به
# من الهدى والعلم كمثل غيث أصاب أرضا فكانت منها طائفة طيبة، قبلت الماء

فأنبتت الكلأ

| [ص: 74]
# والعشب الكثير، وكان منها أجادب (1) أمسكت الماء فنفع الله بها الناس،

فشربوا منها وسقوا وزرعوا، وأصاب طائفة منها أخرى إنما هي قيعان لا تمسك

ماء ولا تنبت كلأ، فذلك مثل من فقه في دين الله ونفعه بما بعثني الله به

فعلم وعلم، ومثل من لم يرفع بذلك رأسا ولم يقبل هدى الله الذي أرسلت به».

متفق عليه. (2)
# «فقه» بضم القاف على المشهور وقيل بكسرها: أي صار فقيها.

| 163 - 
# الثامن: عن جابر - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «مثلي ومثلكم كمثل رجل أوقد نارا فجعل الجنادب والفراش يقعن فيها،

وهو يذبهن عنها، وأنا آخذ بحجزكم عن النار، وأنتم تفلتون من يدي (1)». رواه

مسلم. (2)
# «الجنادب»: نحو الجراد والفراش، هذا هو المعروف الذي يقع في النار. و

«الحجز»: جمع حجزة وهي معقد الإزار والسراويل.

| 164 - 
# التاسع: عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أمر بلعق (1) الأصابع

والصحفة (2)، وقال: «إنكم لا تدرون في أيها البركة». رواه مسلم. (3)
# وفي رواية له: «إذا وقعت لقمة أحدكم فليأخذها، فليمط ما كان بها من أذى،

وليأكلها ولا يدعها للشيطان، ولا يمسح يده بالمنديل حتى يلعق أصابعه فإنه

لا يدري في أي طعامه البركة».
# وفي رواية له: «إن الشيطان يحضر أحدكم عند كل شيء من شأنه، حتى يحضره عند

طعامه، فإذا سقطت من أحدكم اللقمة فليمط ما كان بها من أذى، فليأكلها ولا

يدعها للشيطان».
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To guard, preserve, retain; vigilance in keeping something from loss or corruption.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Sharīʿah context, denotes steadfast adherence to divine commands and prophetic practice as a form of worshipful preservation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal guarding of a physical object; metaphorical here for internalizing and enacting the Sunnah.
- Root: س-ن-ن (s-n-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A path, way, or course; to lay down a precedent or trodden road.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The prophetic way (Sunnah) as the divinely guided normative practice, distinct from innovation (bidʿah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal trodden path; metaphorical for the established prophetic model of conduct.
- Root: ب-د-ع (b-d-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To originate, create anew; something unprecedented.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In religious terminology, an innovation in matters of faith—reprehensible deviation from the prophetic model.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal origination; metaphorical for religious novelty lacking scriptural or prophetic sanction.
- Sībawayh Rule: Command and Prohibition Syntax (Ṣīghat al-Amr wa al-Nahy) — The imperative "take" (khudhū) and "refrain" (intahū) in {«وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا»} operate as binding legal obligations, with the prohibition carrying the force of absolute avoidance.
chapters.translation:
I say — and success is with Allah:

Know that the Commander of the Believers, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him), said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: «Actions are but by intentions, and every man shall have only that which he intended. So whoever emigrates for the sake of Allah and His Messenger, his emigration is for Allah and His Messenger; and whoever emigrates for worldly gain or for a woman he intends to marry, his emigration is for that which he emigrated.» — Agreed upon (by al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

---

**Hadith 154** — On the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «O ʿAbdullāh, do not be like so-and-so; he used to stand in night prayer, then he abandoned night prayer.» — Agreed upon.

**Hadith 155** — On the authority of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) missed the night prayer due to pain or any other cause, he would pray twelve rakʿahs during the day. — Narrated by Muslim.

---

**Chapter 16 — On the Command to Preserve the Sunnah and Its Etiquettes**

Allah the Exalted said: {«And whatsoever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatsoever he forbids you, refrain from it»} [al-Ḥashr: 7]. And He said: {«Nor does he speak from desire; it is but a revelation revealed»} [al-Najm: 3–4]. And He said: {«Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins»} [Āl ʿImrān: 31]. And He said: {«Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have a beautiful example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day»} [al-Aḥzāb: 21]. And He said: {«But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what disputes between them, then find no discomfort in their hearts from what you have decreed, and submit fully»} [al-Nisāʾ: 65]. And He said: {«If you dispute over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger»} [al-Nisāʾ: 59]. The scholars said: Its meaning is to the Book and the Sunnah. And He said: {«Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah»} [al-Nisāʾ: 80]. And He said: {«And indeed, you guide to a straight path — the path of Allah»} [al-Shūrā: 52–53]. And He said: {«So let those who oppose his command beware, lest a trial befall them or a painful punishment afflict them»} [al-Nūr: 63]. And He said: {«And remember what is recited in your homes of the verses of Allah and the wisdom»} [al-Aḥzāb: 34]. The verses on this topic are many.

**As for the hadiths:**

**First (156)** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: «Leave me as I have left you; indeed, those before you were destroyed by their excessive questioning and their disagreement with their prophets. So when I forbid you from something, avoid it; and when I command you with something, do of it what you are able.» — Agreed upon.

**Second (157)** — On the authority of Abū Najīḥ al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) gave us an eloquent exhortation that made hearts tremble and eyes shed tears. We said: O Messenger of Allah, it is as if it were a farewell admonition — so counsel us. He said: «I counsel you to fear Allah, and to hear and obey, even if a slave from Abyssinia is appointed over you. For whoever among you lives will see much disagreement. So adhere to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly-guided caliphs; bite onto it with your molar teeth. And beware of newly-invented matters, for every innovation is a misguidance.» — Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, who said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.

[Page 73] — «Al-Nawājidh» (with the dotted dhāl): the canine teeth; it is also said: the molars.

**Third (158)** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «All of my nation will enter Paradise, except those who refuse.» It was said: And who refuses, O Messenger of Allah? He said: «Whoever obeys me enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys me has refused.» — Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

**Fourth (159)** — On the authority of Abū Muslim — and it is said: Abū Iyās — Salamah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Akwaʿ (may Allah be pleased with him): A man ate with his left hand in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). He said: «Eat with your right hand.» The man said: I cannot. He said: «May you not be able!» — nothing prevented him but pride, and he never raised it to his mouth again. — Narrated by Muslim.

**Fifth (160)** — On the authority of Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: «Straighten your rows, or Allah will cause discord among your faces.» — Agreed upon. In a narration of Muslim: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to straighten our rows until it was as if he were straightening arrows, until he saw that we had understood from him. Then one day he came out and stood until he was about to say the takbīr, when he saw a man with his chest protruding, and he said: «O servants of Allah, straighten your rows, or Allah will cause discord among your faces.»

**Sixth (161)** — On the authority of Abū Mūsā (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: A house in Medina burned down over its inhabitants at night. When the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) was informed of their matter, he said: «This fire is an enemy to you; so when you sleep, extinguish it from you.» — Agreed upon.

**Seventh (162)** — On his authority, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «The likeness of what Allah has sent me with of guidance and knowledge is like abundant rain that fell upon a land. A portion of it was good soil that accepted the water and produced much vegetation and herbage. Another portion was barren ground that held the water, and Allah benefited the people through it — they drank from it, gave drink, and cultivated. And another portion was flat land that neither held water nor produced vegetation. Such is the likeness of one who gains understanding in the religion of Allah and benefits from what Allah sent me with — he learns and teaches. And the likeness of one who does not lift his head to that, nor accepts the guidance of Allah with which I was sent.» — Agreed upon. [Page 74] — «Faqiha» (with ḍammah on the qāf, according to the well-known reading; it is also said with kasrah): i.e., he became a jurist.

**Eighth (163)** — On the authority of Jābir (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «My likeness and your likeness is like a man who kindled a fire, and the locusts and moths began falling into it, while he was shooing them away. I am seizing you by your waists from the fire, and you are slipping from my hands.» — Narrated by Muslim. «Al-Janādib»: something like locusts and moths — this is the well-known thing that falls into fire. And «al-ḥujaz»: the plural of ḥujzah, which is the knot of the waist-wrapper and trousers.

**Ninth (164)** — On his authority: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded licking the fingers and the plate, and said: «Indeed, you do not know in which of them the blessing lies.» — Narrated by Muslim. In another narration of his: «When a morsel of one of you falls, let him take it, wipe off any dirt on it, and eat it — and not leave it for Satan. And let him not wipe his hand with a napkin until he licks his fingers, for he does not know in which of his food the blessing lies.» In yet another narration of his: «Indeed, Satan attends to one of you in every matter of his concern, until he attends to him at his food. So when a morsel falls from one of you, let him wipe off any dirt on it and eat it — and not leave it for Satan.»

chapters.title_en: Section 23 — On the Obligation of Submitting to Allah's Judgment, the Prohibition of Innovations, and the Reward of Establishing Good or Evil Precedents
chapters.arabic_text:
| 165 - 
# العاشر: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، قال: قام فينا رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - بموعظة، فقال: «يا أيها الناس، إنكم محشورون إلى الله تعالى

حفاة عراة غرلا {كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده وعدا علينا إنا كنا فاعلين}

[الأنبياء: 103] ألا وإن أول الخلائق يكسى يوم القيامة إبراهيم - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - ألا وإنه سيجاء برجال من أمتي فيؤخذ بهم ذات الشمال، فأقول: يا

رب أصحابي. فيقال: إنك لا تدري ما أحدثوا بعدك. فأقول كما قال العبد

الصالح: {وكنت عليهم شهيدا ما دمت فيهم} إلى قوله: {العزيز الحكيم}

[المائدة: 117 - 118] (1) فيقال لي: إنهم لم يزالوا مرتدين على أعقابهم منذ

فارقتهم (2)». متفق عليه. (3)
# «غرلا»: أي غير مختونين.

| 166 - 
# الحادي عشر: عن أبي سعيد عبد الله بن مغفل - رضي الله عنه - قال: نهى

رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن الخذف (1)، وقال: «إنه لا يقتل الصيد،

ولا ينكأ (2) العدو، وإنه يفقأ (3) العين، ويكسر السن». متفق عليه. (4)
# وفي رواية: أن قريبا لابن مغفل خذف فنهاه، وقال: إن رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم -
# نهى عن الخذف، وقال: «إنها لا تصيد صيدا» ثم عاد، فقال: أحدثك أن رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - نهى عنه، ثم عدت تخذف!؟ لا أكلمك أبدا (5).

| 167 - 
# وعن عابس بن ربيعة، قال: رأيت عمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنه - يقبل الحجر

| [ص: 76]
# يعني: الأسود - ويقول: إني أعلم أنك حجر ما تنفع ولا تضر، ولولا أني رأيت

رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يقبلك ما قبلتك (1). متفق عليه. (2)

$ 17 - باب في وجوب الانقياد لحكم الله وما يقوله من دعي إلى ذلك وأمر بمعروف أو نهي عن منكر
# قال الله تعالى: {فلا وربك لا يؤمنون حتى يحكموك فيما شجر بينهم ثم لا

يجدوا في أنفسهم حرجا مما قضيت ويسلموا تسليما} [النساء: 65]، وقال تعالى:

{إنما كان قول المؤمنين إذا دعوا إلى الله ورسوله ليحكم بينهم أن يقولوا

سمعنا وأطعنا وأولئك هم المفلحون} [النور: 51].
# وفيه من الأحاديث: حديث أبي هريرة المذكور (1) في أول الباب قبله وغيره

من الأحاديث فيه.

| 168 - 
# عن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: لما نزلت على رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم: {لله ما في  السماوات وما في الأرض وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو

تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله} الآية [البقرة: 283] اشتد ذلك على أصحاب رسول الله

- صلى الله عليه وسلم - فأتوا رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ثم بركوا

على الركب، فقالوا: أي (1) رسول الله، كلفنا من الأعمال ما نطيق: الصلاة

والجهاد والصيام والصدقة، وقد أنزلت عليك هذه الآية ولا نطيقها. قال رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أتريدون أن تقولوا كما قال أهل الكتابين (2)

من قبلكم: سمعنا وعصينا؟ بل قولوا: سمعنا وأطعنا غفرانك ربنا وإليك المصير»

فلما اقترأها (3) القوم، وذلت بها ألسنتهم أنزل الله تعالى في إثرها: {آمن

الرسول بما أنزل إليه من ربه والمؤمنون كل آمن بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله

لا نفرق بين أحد من رسله وقالوا سمعنا وأطعنا غفرانك ربنا وإليك المصير}

[البقرة: 285].

| [ص: 77]
# فلما فعلوا ذلك نسخها الله تعالى، فأنزل الله - عز وجل: {لا يكلف الله

نفسا إلا وسعها لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت ربنا لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو

أخطأنا} [البقرة: 286] قال: نعم {ربنا ولا تحمل علينا إصرا كما حملته على

الذين من قبلنا} قال: نعم {ربنا ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به} قال: نعم

{واعف عنا واغفر لنا وارحمنا أنت مولانا فانصرنا على القوم الكافرين} قال:

نعم. رواه مسلم. (4)

$ 18 - باب في النهي عن البدع ومحدثات الأمور
# قال الله تعالى: {فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال} [يونس: 32]، وقال تعالى:

{ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء} [الأنعام: 38]، وقال تعالى: {فإن تنازعتم في

شيء فردوه إلى الله والرسول} [النساء: 59] أي الكتاب والسنة. وقال تعالى:

{وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل فتفرق بكم عن سبيله}

[الأنعام: 153]، وقال تعالى: {قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله

ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم} [آل عمران:31] والآيات في الباب كثيرة معلومة.
# 
# وأما الأحاديث فكثيرة جدا، وهي مشهورة فنقتصر على طرف منها:

| 169 - 
# عن عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من
# أحدث في أمرنا هذا ما ليس منه  فهو رد (1)». متفق عليه.
# وفي رواية لمسلم: «من عمل عملا ليس عليه أمرنا فهو رد (2)». (3)

| 170 - 
# وعن جابر - رضي الله عنه - قال: كان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

إذا خطب احمرت عيناه، وعلا صوته، واشتد غضبه، حتى كأنه منذر جيش، يقول:

«صبحكم ومساكم» ويقول: «بعثت أنا والساعة كهاتين» ويقرن بين أصبعيه السبابة

والوسطى، ويقول: «أما بعد، فإن خير الحديث كتاب الله، وخير الهدي هدي محمد

- صلى الله عليه وسلم - وشر الأمور محدثاتها،

| [ص: 78]
# وكل بدعة ضلالة» ثم يقول: «أنا أولى بكل مؤمن من نفسه، من ترك مالا

فلأهله، ومن ترك دينا أو ضياعا (1) فإلي وعلي» (2) رواه مسلم. (3)
# وعن العرباض بن سارية - رضي الله عنه - حديثه السابق (4) في باب المحافظة

على السنة.

$ 19 - باب فيمن سن سنة حسنة أو سيئة
# قال الله تعالى: {والذين يقولون ربنا هب لنا من أزواجنا وذرياتنا قرة

أعين واجعلنا للمتقين إماما} [الفرقان: 74]، وقال تعالى: {وجعلناهم أئمة

يهدون بأمرنا} [الأنبياء: 73].
#

| 171 - 
# عن أبي عمرو جرير بن عبد الله - رضي الله عنه - قال: كنا في صدر النهار
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ش-ر (ḥ-sh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To gather, assemble, muster for a purpose; collective driving toward a destination.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The eschatological gathering of all creatures for reckoning (ḥashr) — a fixed divine decree, not metaphorical.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical assembly of bodies; no majāz here, as it pertains to the unseen (ghayb) affirmed by revelation.
- Root: غ-ر-ل (gh-r-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Uncircumcised; the prepuce (ghurla) remaining intact; a state of primordial creation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Signifies the original state of Adam's progeny — resurrection in the exact condition of first creation, without alteration.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical state, not metaphorical; denotes nakedness and uncircumcision as marks of divine power over re-creation.
- Root: خ-ذ-ف (kh-dh-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To throw a small pebble or stone by placing it between the thumb and forefinger and flicking it.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A futile act — neither hunting nor warfare; a vain pastime.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal action; the prohibition is on its uselessness and potential harm, not on any symbolic meaning.
- Root: ب-د-ع (b-d-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To originate, create something without prior example; innovation (bidʿah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In religious matters — introducing what is not from the Sacred Law (Sharīʿah); every such innovation is misguidance (ḍalālah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in the sense of "newly invented"; the Prophet's statement "every innovation is misguidance" is a universal (ʿāmm) legal ruling, not rhetorical hyperbole.
- Root: س-ن-ن (s-n-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pave a path, establish a way; a trodden path (sunnah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A normative practice — either commendable (ḥasanah) or blameworthy (sayyiʾah); the doer bears its reward or sin plus that of those who follow.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — a path laid down; metaphorical extension to any precedent, good or evil, that others emulate.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-jazāʾ) — In "من أحدث في أمرنا هذا ما ليس منه فهو رد" (Whoever innovates in this affair of ours what is not from it, it is rejected), the conditional particle "man" governs a protasis and apodosis; the apodosis "فهو رد" is a nominal sentence with an implied subject (huwa) referring to the innovation, establishing a universal legal ruling. Also, the accusative of specification (tamyīz) in "حفاة عراة غرلا" — these are adverbial accusatives describing the state (ḥāl) of the resurrected.
chapters.translation:
**Hadith 165 — The Tenth (of the Section on the Resurrection):**
Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stood among us with an admonition, and said: «O people, you will be gathered to Allah Almighty barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised — {As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it — a promise binding upon Us; indeed, We will do it} [Al-Anbiyāʾ 21:103]. Verily, the first of creation to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection will be Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him. Verily, men from my Ummah will be brought, and they will be taken to the left (toward Hell), and I will say: 'O my Lord, my companions!' It will be said: 'You do not know what they innovated after you.' So I will say as the righteous servant (ʿĪsā) said: {And I was a witness over them while I dwelt among them} up to His saying: {the Mighty, the Wise} [Al-Māʾidah 5:117–118]. Then it will be said to me: 'They have not ceased turning back on their heels (as apostates) since you departed from them.'» — Agreed upon (Al-Bukhārī and Muslim).
Note: "Ghurla" (uncircumcised) means: not circumcised.

**Hadith 166 — The Eleventh:**
Abū Saʿīd ʿAbdullāh ibn Mughaffal, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade flicking pebbles (al-khadhf), and said: «It does not kill game, nor wound the enemy, yet it knocks out an eye and breaks a tooth.» — Agreed upon.
In another narration: A relative of Ibn Mughaffal flicked a pebble, and he forbade him, saying: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade flicking pebbles, and said: «It does not catch game.» Then the man did it again, so he said: "I tell you that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade it, and then you return to flicking pebbles?! I will never speak to you again."

**Hadith 167:**
ʿĀbis ibn Rabīʿah said: I saw ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, kissing the Stone — meaning the Black Stone — and saying: "I know that you are a stone that neither benefits nor harms, and were it not that I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, kissing you, I would not kiss you." — Agreed upon.

**Section 17 — On the Obligation of Submitting to Allah's Judgment, and What One Says Who Is Called to That, or Is Commanded to Good or Forbidden from Evil:**
Allah Almighty said: {But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge in what has broken out between them, then find no discomfort in their hearts from what you have ruled, and submit in full submission} [Al-Nisāʾ 4:65]. And He said: {The only saying of the believers when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them is that they say: "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful} [Al-Nūr 24:51].
Among the hadiths in this section is the hadith of Abū Hurayrah mentioned at the beginning of the previous section, and other hadiths.

**Hadith 168:**
Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: {To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it} [Al-Baqarah 2:284], this weighed heavily upon the companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. So they came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and knelt on their knees, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, we have been tasked with deeds we can bear: prayer, jihad, fasting, and charity. But this verse has been revealed to you, and we cannot bear it." The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «Do you wish to say as the People of the Two Books before you said: "We hear and we disobey"? Rather, say: "We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return."» When the people recited it, and their tongues became accustomed to it, Allah Almighty revealed after it: {The Messenger believes in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and [so do] the believers. Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they say: "We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return"} [Al-Baqarah 2:285].
When they did that, Allah abrogated it, and Allah — Mighty and Majestic — revealed: {Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. For it is what it has earned, and against it is what it has acquired. Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err} — He said: "Yes." {Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden as You laid upon those before us} — He said: "Yes." {Our Lord, do not burden us with what we cannot bear} — He said: "Yes." {And pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so grant us victory over the disbelieving people} — He said: "Yes." — Narrated by Muslim.

**Section 18 — On the Prohibition of Innovations (Bidʿah) and Newly Invented Matters:**
Allah Almighty said: {So what is after truth except misguidance?} [Yūnus 10:32]. And He said: {We have neglected nothing in the Book} [Al-Anʿām 6:38]. And He said: {If you dispute over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger} [Al-Nisāʾ 4:59] — meaning the Book and the Sunnah. And He said: {And that this is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow [other] ways, lest they scatter you from His path} [Al-Anʿām 6:153]. And He said: {Say: "If you love Allah, follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins"} [Āl ʿImrān 3:31]. The verses on this topic are many and well-known.
As for the hadiths, they are very numerous and famous, so we will limit ourselves to a portion of them:

**Hadith 169:**
ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «Whoever innovates in this affair of ours what is not from it, it is rejected.» — Agreed upon.
In a narration of Muslim: «Whoever does a deed that is not upon our affair, it is rejected.»

**Hadith 170:**
Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gave a sermon, his eyes reddened, his voice rose, and his anger intensified, until he seemed like a warner of an army, saying: «May you be warned morning and evening.» And he said: «I and the Hour were sent like these two» — and he joined his index and middle fingers — and he said: «To proceed: The best of speech is the Book of Allah, and the best of guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the worst of matters are their innovations, and every innovation is misguidance.» Then he said: «I am more entitled to every believer than his own self. Whoever leaves wealth, it is for his family; whoever leaves a debt or dependents, then they are for me and upon me.» — Narrated by Muslim.
And the hadith of al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah, may Allah be pleased with him, has preceded in the section on adhering to the Sunnah.

**Section 19 — On Whoever Establishes a Good or Evil Precedent (Sunnah Ḥasanah or Sayyiʾah):**
Allah Almighty said: {And those who say: "Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and our offspring comfort of eyes, and make us leaders for the righteous"} [Al-Furqān 25:74]. And He said: {And We made them leaders guiding by Our command} [Al-Anbiyāʾ 21:73].

**Hadith 171:**
Abū ʿAmr Jarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh, may Allah be pleased with him, said: We were in the early part of the day...

chapters.title_en: Section 24 — On the Excellence of Establishing a Good Sunnah, and the Condemnation of Establishing an Evil One; and On Guiding to Good and Calling to Guidance or Misguidance; and On Cooperation in Righteousness and Piety
chapters.arabic_text:
عند رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فجاءه قوم عراة مجتابي النمار أو

العباء، متقلدي السيوف، عامتهم من مضر بل كلهم من مضر، فتمعر رسول الله -

صلى الله عليه وسلم - لما رأى بهم من الفاقة (1)، فدخل ثم خرج، فأمر بلالا

فأذن وأقام، فصلى ثم خطب، فقال: «{يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من

نفس واحدة} إلى آخر الآية: {إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا} [النساء: 1]، والآية

الأخرى التي في آخر الحشر: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله ولتنظر نفس ما

قدمت لغد} [الحشر: 18] تصدق رجل من ديناره، من درهمه، من ثوبه، من صاع بره،

من صاع تمره - حتى قال - ولو بشق تمرة» فجاء رجل من الأنصار بصرة كادت كفه

تعجز عنها، بل قد عجزت، ثم تتابع الناس حتى رأيت كومين من طعام وثياب، حتى

رأيت وجه رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يتهلل كأنه مذهبة. فقال رسول

الله - صلى الله  عليه وسلم: «من سن في الإسلام سنة حسنة فله أجرها، وأجر من

عمل بها بعده، من غير أن ينقص من أجورهم شيء، ومن سن في الإسلام سنة سيئة

كان عليه وزرها، ووزر من عمل بها من بعده، من غير أن ينقص من أوزارهم شيء»

(2) رواه مسلم. (3)

| [ص: 79]
# قوله: «مجتابي النمار» هو بالجيم وبعد الألف باء موحدة، والنمار جمع نمرة

وهي كساء من صوف مخطط. ومعنى «مجتابيها»، أي: لابسيها قد خرقوها في رؤوسهم.

و «الجوب» القطع، ومنه قوله تعالى: {وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد}

[الفجر: 9] أي نحتوه وقطعوه. وقوله: «تمعر» هو بالعين المهملة: أي تغير.

وقوله: «رأيت كومين» بفتح الكاف وضمها: أي صبرتين. وقوله: «كأنه مذهبة» هو

بالذال المعجمة وفتح الهاء والباء الموحدة قاله القاضي عياض وغيره وصحفه

بعضهم، فقال: «مدهنة» بدال مهملة وضم الهاء وبالنون وكذا ضبطه الحميدي (4).

والصحيح المشهور هو الأول. والمراد به على الوجهين: الصفاء والاستنارة.

| 172 - 
# وعن ابن مسعود - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«ليس من نفس تقتل ظلما إلا كان على ابن آدم الأول كفل (1) من دمها، لأنه

كان أول من سن القتل». متفق عليه. (2)

$ 20 - باب في الدلالة على خير والدعاء إلى هدى أو ضلالة
# قال تعالى: {وادع إلى ربك} [القصص: 87]، وقال تعالى: {ادع إلى سبيل ربك

بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة} [النحل: 125]، وقال تعالى: {وتعاونوا على البر

والتقوى} [المائدة:2]، وقال تعالى: {ولتكن منكم أمة يدعون إلى الخير} [آل

عمران:104].
#

| 173 - 
# وعن أبي مسعود عقبة بن عمرو الأنصاري البدري - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال

رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من دل على خير فله مثل أجر فاعله». رواه

مسلم. (1)

| 174 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«من دعا إلى هدى، كان له من الأجر مثل أجور من تبعه، لا ينقص ذلك من أجورهم

شيئا، ومن دعا إلى ضلالة، كان عليه من الإثم مثل آثام من تبعه، لا ينقص ذلك

من آثامهم شيئا». رواه  مسلم. (1)

| 175 - 
# وعن أبي العباس سهل بن سعد الساعدي - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - قال يوم خيبر: «لأعطين الراية غدا رجلا يفتح الله على

يديه، يحب الله ورسوله، ويحبه الله ورسوله»، فبات الناس يدوكون ليلتهم أيهم

يعطاها. فلما أصبح الناس غدوا على رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كلهم

يرجو أن يعطاها. فقال: «أين علي ابن أبي طالب؟» فقيل: يا رسول الله، هو

يشتكي عينيه. قال: «فأرسلوا إليه» فأتي به فبصق رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - في عينيه، ودعا له فبرىء حتى كأن لم يكن به وجع، فأعطاه الراية.

فقال علي - رضي الله عنه: يا رسول الله، أقاتلهم حتى يكونوا مثلنا؟ فقال:

«انفذ على رسلك حتى تنزل بساحتهم، ثم ادعهم إلى الإسلام، وأخبرهم بما يجب

عليهم من حق الله تعالى فيه، فوالله لأن يهدي الله بك رجلا واحدا خير لك من

حمر النعم». متفق عليه. (1)
# قوله: «يدوكون»: أي يخوضون ويتحدثون. وقوله: «رسلك» بكسر الراء وبفتحها

لغتان، والكسر أفصح.

| 176 - 
# وعن أنس - رضي الله عنه: أن فتى من أسلم، قال: يا رسول الله، إني أريد

الغزو وليس معي ما أتجهز به، قال: «ائت فلانا فإنه قد كان تجهز فمرض»

فأتاه، فقال: إن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يقرئك السلام، ويقول:

أعطني الذي تجهزت به، فقال: يا فلانة، أعطيه الذي تجهزت به، ولا تحبسي منه

شيئا، فوالله لا تحبسين منه شيئا فيبارك لك فيه. رواه مسلم. (1)

$ 21 - باب في التعاون على البر والتقوى
# قال الله تعالى: {وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى} [المائدة: 2]، وقال تعالى:

{والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وتواصوا بالحق

وتواصوا بالصبر} [العصر: 1 - 2] قال الإمام الشافعي - رحمه الله - كلاما

معناه: إن الناس أو أكثرهم في غفلة عن تدبر هذه السورة (1).

| 177 - 
# وعن أبي عبد الرحمان زيد بن خالد الجهني - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من جهز غازيا في سبيل الله فقد غزا، ومن  خلف

غازيا في أهله بخير فقد غزا». متفق عليه. (1)

| 178 - 
# وعن أبي سعيد الخدري - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم

- بعث بعثا إلى بني لحيان من هذيل، فقال: «لينبعث من كل رجلين أحدهما

والأجر بينهما». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 179 - 
# وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لقي

ركبا بالروحاء (1)، فقال: «من القوم؟» قالوا: المسلمون، فقالوا: من أنت؟

قال: «رسول الله»، فرفعت إليه امرأة صبيا، فقالت: ألهذا حج؟ قال: «نعم، ولك

أجر». رواه مسلم. (2)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-و-ب (j-w-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "cutting" or "piercing through"; al-jawb is the act of splitting or cutting open, as in cutting a garment for the head.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic usage, jāba (as in {«وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد»}) denotes hewing and carving through solid rock, implying penetration with effort.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is physical cutting; metaphorically (majāz), it extends to "traversing" or "piercing" through a land or matter.
- Root: م-ع-ر (m-ʿ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes change or alteration of state, particularly of the face (tamaʿʿara), i.e., the countenance becoming altered or distressed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance: a visible change in facial expression reflecting inner emotional or spiritual disturbance, often due to compassion or concern.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical change in appearance; metaphorical: the manifestation of inner states upon the exterior.
- Root: ك-ف-ل (k-f-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Kifl denotes a portion, share, or double portion; also a guarantor (kafīl).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In eschatological context, kifl signifies a full or multiplied share of recompense, whether of reward or burden.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a share; metaphorical: the full measure of responsibility transferred to the originator of an act.
- Root: د-ل-ل (d-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Dalāla means indication, guidance, or pointing the way; also evidence (dalīl).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, dalāla is the act of directing toward truth or good, entailing a share in the resultant reward.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: pointing; metaphorical: intellectual or moral guidance that leads another to action.
- Root: ج-ه-ز (j-h-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Tajhīz means equipping, preparing, or furnishing for a journey or expedition.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In martial context, tajhīz ghāzin is the provision of means for one who fights in God's path, equated with the act of fighting itself.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: outfitting; metaphorical: the moral equivalence of enabling versus performing.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When a noun follows another without a conjunction to clarify it, as in "كأنه مذهبة" where the simile clause clarifies the state of the Prophet's face; also the rule of Ḥāl (Circumstantial Accusative) for "متقلدي السيوف" (being girt with swords) as a circumstantial qualifier of the arriving people.
chapters.translation:
Know, may Allah guide you, that the scholars of hadith have compiled chapters on the virtues of establishing good practices and the perils of introducing evil ones. I say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was seated when a group of people came to him — naked, wearing striped woolen cloaks (numur) or ʿabāʾ garments pierced through their heads, with swords hung from their necks. Most of them were from Muḍar — nay, all of them were from Muḍar. The face of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, changed (tamaʿʿara) when he saw their destitution. He entered his house, then came out, and commanded Bilāl to give the call to prayer (adhān) and the commencement call (iqāmah). He prayed, then delivered a sermon, saying: {«يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة»} — "O mankind, fear your Lord who created you from a single soul" — to the end of the verse: {«إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا»} — "Indeed, Allah is ever over you a Watcher" [al-Nisāʾ 4:1]. And the other verse at the end of Sūrat al-Ḥashr: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله ولتنظر نفس ما قدمت لغد»} — "O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow" [al-Ḥashr 59:18]. Then he said: "Let a man give charity from his dinar, from his dirham, from his garment, from a ṣāʿ of his wheat, from a ṣāʿ of his dates" — until he said — "even if it be half a date." Then a man from the Anṣār came with a purse that his hand could scarcely carry — nay, it had become unable to carry it. Then the people followed in succession until I saw two mounds (kawmayn) of food and clothing, until I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, radiant (yatalallaʾu) as if it were gilded (mudhhabah). Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever establishes (sanna) in Islam a good practice (sunnah ḥasanah) shall have its reward and the reward of those who act upon it after him, without diminishing anything from their rewards. And whoever establishes in Islam an evil practice (sunnah sayyiʾah) shall bear its sin and the sin of those who act upon it after him, without diminishing anything from their sins." Narrated by Muslim.

I say, regarding the narrator's words: "مجتابي النمار" (mujtābī al-numur) — the letter is jīm, and after the alif is a single bāʾ. Al-numur is the plural of nimrah, which is a striped woolen cloak. The meaning of "mujtābīhā" is: wearing them, having pierced them through their heads. And "al-jawb" is cutting; from it is the saying of the Exalted: {«وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد»} — "And Thamūd, who carved the rock in the valley" [al-Fajr 89:9], meaning they hewed and cut it. His saying "tamaʿʿara" is with the unpointed ʿayn, meaning: his face changed. His saying "رأيت كومين" (I saw two mounds) — with fatḥah on the kāf and ḍammah on it (both readings valid) — meaning two heaps. His saying "كأنه مذهبة" (as if gilded) is with the dotted dhāl, fatḥah on the hāʾ and the bāʾ — so stated by Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ and others. Some scholars erred in transcription, saying "مدهنة" (mudhhanah) with an unpointed dāl, ḍammah on the hāʾ, and nūn — thus did al-Ḥumaydī record it. The correct and well-known reading is the first. The intended meaning, on both readings, is clarity and luminosity.

[172] — On the authority of Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "No soul is killed unjustly except that the first son of Adam bears a portion (kifl) of its blood, because he was the first to establish the practice of killing." Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

Section 20 — On Guiding to Good and Calling to Guidance or Misguidance

Allah the Exalted said: {«وادع إلى ربك»} — "And call to your Lord" [al-Qaṣaṣ 28:87]. And the Exalted said: {«ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة»} — "Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition" [al-Naḥl 16:125]. And the Exalted said: {«وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى»} — "And cooperate in righteousness and piety" [al-Māʾidah 5:2]. And the Exalted said: {«ولتكن منكم أمة يدعون إلى الخير»} — "And let there be from you a nation calling to good" [Āl ʿImrān 3:104].

[173] — On the authority of Abū Masʿūd ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī al-Badrī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever guides to good (dalla ʿalā khayr) shall have the like of the reward of the one who acts upon it." Narrated by Muslim.

[174] — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever calls to guidance (daʿā ilā hudā) shall have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without that diminishing anything from their rewards. And whoever calls to misguidance (daʿā ilā ḍalālah) shall bear sin like the sins of those who follow him, without that diminishing anything from their sins." Narrated by Muslim.

[175] — On the authority of Abū al-ʿAbbās Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī, may Allah be pleased with him: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said on the Day of Khaybar: "I shall surely give the banner tomorrow to a man through whose hands Allah will grant victory — one who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love." The people spent the night discussing (yadūkūna) among themselves as to which of them would be given it. When morning came, they went to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, each hoping to be given it. He said: "Where is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib?" It was said: O Messenger of Allah, he is suffering from an ailment in his eyes. He said: "Send for him." So he was brought, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, spat in his eyes and supplicated for him, and he was cured as if no pain had ever touched him. Then he gave him the banner. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of Allah, shall I fight them until they become like us? He said: "Proceed at your ease (ʿalā rislika) until you descend in their courtyard, then call them to Islam, and inform them of what is obligatory upon them of the rights of Allah the Exalted therein. For by Allah, if Allah guides through you a single man, that is better for you than red camels (ḥumr al-naʿam)." Agreed upon.

I say: His saying "يدوكون" (yadūkūna) means: they were plunging into discussion and conversing. His saying "رسلك" (ruslika) — with kasrah on the rāʾ and with fatḥah on it, both are two valid dialects, and the kasrah is more eloquent.

[176] — On the authority of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: A young man from Aslam said: O Messenger of Allah, I wish to go on a military expedition (ghazw), but I have nothing with which to equip myself. He said: "Go to so-and-so, for he had prepared himself (tajahhaza) but then fell ill." So he went to him and said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, conveys his greeting of peace to you, and says: Give me what you have prepared for the expedition. He said: O so-and-so (addressing his wife), give him what I have prepared, and do not withhold anything from it. For by Allah, if you withhold anything from it, you will not be blessed in it. Narrated by Muslim.

Section 21 — On Cooperation in Righteousness and Piety

Allah the Exalted said: {«وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى»} — "And cooperate in righteousness and piety" [al-Māʾidah 5:2]. And the Exalted said: {«والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وتواصوا بالحق وتواصوا بالصبر»} — "By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience" [al-ʿAṣr 103:1-3]. Imām al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, said words to the effect: Most people — or the majority of them — are heedless of reflecting upon this sūrah.

[177] — On the authority of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever equips a fighter (j ahhaza ghāziyan) in the path of Allah has indeed fought (ghazā). And whoever looks after the family of a fighter in his absence with goodness has indeed fought." Agreed upon.

[178] — On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, dispatched an expedition (baʿtha) to Banū Liḥyān from Hudhayl, and said: "Let one of every two men go forth, and the reward shall be shared between them." Narrated by Muslim.

[179] — On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, met a caravan at al-Rawḥāʾ and said: "Who are the people?" They said: Muslims. Then they said: Who are you? He said: "The Messenger of Allah." A woman raised a child to him and said: Is there a pilgrimage (ḥajj) for this one? He said: "Yes, and for you is a reward." Narrated by Muslim.

chapters.title_en: Section 25 — On Sincerity (al-Naṣīḥah) and Enjoining Right & Forbidding Wrong (al-Amr bi-l-Maʿrūf wa al-Nahy ʿan al-Munkar)
chapters.arabic_text:
| 180 - 
# وعن أبي موسى الأشعري - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

أنه قال: «الخازن المسلم الأمين الذي ينفذ ما أمر به فيعطيه كاملا موفرا

طيبة به نفسه فيدفعه إلى الذي أمر له به، أحد المتصدقين». متفق عليه. (1)
# وفي رواية: «الذي يعطي ما أمر به» وضبطوا «المتصدقين» بفتح القاف مع كسر

النون على التثنية، وعكسه على الجمع وكلاهما صحيح.

$ 22 - باب في النصيحة
# قال تعالى: {إنما المؤمنون إخوة} [الحجرات: 10]، وقال تعالى: إخبارا عن

نوح - صلى الله عليه وسلم: {وأنصح لكم} [الأعراف: 62]، وعن هود - صلى الله

عليه وسلم: {وأنا لكم ناصح أمين} [الأعراف: 68].
# 
# وأما الأحاديث:

| 181 - 
# فالأول: عن أبي رقية تميم بن أوس الداري - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - قال: «الدين النصيحة» قلنا: لمن؟ قال: «لله ولكتابه

ولرسوله ولأئمة المسلمين وعامتهم (1)». رواه مسلم. (2)

| 182 - 
# الثاني: عن جرير بن عبد الله - رضي الله عنه - قال: بايعت رسول الله -

صلى الله عليه وسلم - على إقام الصلاة، وإيتاء الزكاة، والنصح لكل مسلم.

متفق عليه. (1)

| 183 - 
# الثالث: عن أنس - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«لا يؤمن أحدكم حتى يحب لأخيه ما يحب لنفسه» (1) متفق عليه. (2)

$ 23 - باب في الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر
# قال الله تعالى: {ولتكن منكم أمة يدعون إلى الخير ويأمرون بالمعروف

وينهون عن المنكر وأولئك هم المفلحون} [آل عمران: 104]، وقال تعالى: {كنتم

خير أمة أخرجت للناس تأمرون بالمعروف وتنهون  عن المنكر} [آل عمران: 110]،

وقال تعالى: {خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين} [الأعراف: 199]،

وقال تعالى: {والمؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أولياء بعض يأمرون بالمعروف وينهون

عن المنكر} [التوبة:71]، وقال تعالى: {لعن الذين كفروا من بني إسرائيل على

لسان داود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون كانوا لا يتناهون عن

منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون} [المائدة: 78]، وقال تعالى: {وقل الحق من

ربكم فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر} [الكهف:29]، وقال تعالى: {فاصدع بما

تؤمر} [الحجر:94]، وقال تعالى: {فأنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء وأخذنا الذين

ظلموا بعذاب بئيس بما كانوا يفسقون} [الأعراف: 165] والآيات في الباب كثيرة

معلومة.
# 
# (1) - وأما الأحاديث:

| 184 - 
# فالأول: عن أبي سعيد الخدري - رضي الله عنه - قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - يقول: «من رأى منكم منكرا فليغيره بيده، فإن لم يستطع

فبلسانه، فإن لم يستطع فبقلبه، وذلك أضعف (1) الإيمان». رواه مسلم. (2)

| 185 - 
# الثاني: عن ابن مسعود - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم

- قال: «ما من نبي بعثه الله

| [ص: 83]
# في أمة قبلي إلا كان له من أمته حواريون (1) وأصحاب يأخذون بسنته ويقتدون

بأمره، ثم إنها تخلف من بعدهم خلوف (2) يقولون ما لا يفعلون، ويفعلون ما لا

يؤمرون، فمن جاهدهم بيده فهو مؤمن، ومن جاهدهم بقلبه فهو مؤمن، ومن جاهدهم

بلسانه فهو مؤمن، وليس وراء ذلك من الإيمان حبة خردل». رواه مسلم. (3)

| 186 - 
# الثالث: عن أبي الوليد عبادة بن الصامت - رضي الله عنه - قال: بايعنا

رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - على السمع والطاعة في العسر واليسر،

والمنشط والمكره، وعلى أثرة علينا، وعلى أن لا ننازع الأمر أهله إلا أن

تروا كفرا بواحا عندكم من الله تعالى فيه برهان، وعلى أن نقول بالحق أينما

كنا، لا نخاف في الله لومة لائم. متفق عليه. (1)
# «المنشط والمكره» بفتح ميميهما: أي في السهل والصعب. و «الأثرة»:

الاختصاص بالمشترك وقد سبق بيانها. «بواحا» بفتح الباء الموحدة بعدها واو

ثم ألف ثم حاء مهملة: أي ظاهرا لا  يحتمل تأويلا.

| 187 - 
# الرابع: عن النعمان بن بشير رضي الله عنهما، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - قال: «مثل القائم في حدود الله والواقع فيها، كمثل قوم استهموا على

سفينة فصار بعضهم أعلاها وبعضهم أسفلها، وكان الذين في أسفلها إذا استقوا

من الماء مروا على من فوقهم، فقالوا: لو أنا خرقنا في نصيبنا خرقا ولم نؤذ

من فوقنا، فإن تركوهم وما أرادوا هلكوا جميعا، وإن أخذوا على أيديهم نجوا

ونجوا جميعا». رواه البخاري. (1)
# «القائم في حدود الله تعالى» معناه: المنكر لها، القائم في دفعها

وإزالتها، والمراد بالحدود: ما نهى الله عنه. «استهموا»: اقترعوا.

| 188 - 
# الخامس: عن أم المؤمنين أم سلمة هند بنت أبي أمية حذيفة رضي الله عنها،

عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال: «إنه يستعمل عليكم أمراء فتعرفون

وتنكرون، فمن كره فقد برئ، ومن أنكر فقد سلم، ولكن من رضي وتابع» قالوا: يا

رسول الله، ألا نقاتلهم؟ قال: «لا، ما أقاموا فيكم الصلاة». رواه مسلم. (1)

| [ص: 84]
# معناه: من كره بقلبه ولم يستطع إنكارا بيد ولا لسان فقد برىء من الإثم،

وأدى وظيفته، ومن أنكر بحسب طاقته فقد سلم من هذه المعصية ومن رضي بفعلهم

وتابعهم فهو العاصي.

| 189 - 
# السادس: عن أم المؤمنين أم الحكم زينب بنت جحش رضي الله عنها: أن النبي -

صلى الله عليه وسلم - دخل عليها فزعا، يقول: «لا إله إلا الله، ويل للعرب

من شر قد اقترب، فتح اليوم من ردم يأجوج ومأجوج مثل هذه»، وحلق بأصبعيه

الإبهام والتي تليها، فقلت: يا رسول الله، أنهلك وفينا الصالحون؟ قال:

«نعم، إذا كثر الخبث (1)». متفق عليه. (2)

| 190 - 
# السابع: عن أبي سعيد الخدري - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ص-ح (n-ṣ-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of pure, unadulterated sincerity; the root denotes the craftsman's precise stitching (khiyāṭah) that renders a garment whole and sound — hence, counsel that seeks the genuine welfare of the other.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, naṣīḥah is the sincere, wholehearted pursuit of the well-being of the one advised — for God, His Book, His Messenger, and the Muslim community — entailing both inward intention (niyyah) and outward action.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is the integrity of the thing itself; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies it to speech and conduct that are free from deceit and corruption.
- Sībawayh Rule: Predicate-Nominative Construction (al-Mubtadaʾ wa al-Khabar) — In «الدين النصيحة», the definite noun (al-dīn) is the subject and the definite noun (al-naṣīḥah) is the predicate, yielding a restrictive equation: the entirety of the religion is sincerity.

- Root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes knowledge and recognition; al-maʿrūf is that which is well-known and universally acknowledged as good by sound human nature (fiṭrah) and revealed law.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, al-maʿrūf is the divinely sanctioned good that the intellect and revelation concur upon; al-munkar is its opposite — that which is repudiated by both.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "known/recognized"; metaphorical sense in the imperative «مر بالمعروف» is "command that which is established as virtuous in the Law."
- Sībawayh Rule: Command Construction (Ṣīghat al-Amr) — «ولتكن منكم أمة» employs the lām of command (lām al-amr) with the jussive, indicating obligation upon a sufficient portion of the community (farḍ kifāyah).
chapters.translation:
**180** — And from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: «The trustworthy Muslim treasurer who executes what he is commanded, giving it in full and in abundance, with his soul content therein, delivering it to the one for whom it was commanded — he is one of the givers of charity (al-mutaṣaddiqīn).» Agreed upon. (1)

In another narration: «The one who gives what he is commanded» — and they (the scholars) have recorded «al-mutaṣaddiqīn» with the fatḥah on the qāf and the kasrah on the nūn, indicating the dual form (al-mutaṣaddiqayn), and its opposite (i.e., the plural form) — and both are correct.

**Section 22 — On Sincerity (al-Naṣīḥah)**

God, Exalted is He, said: {«إنما المؤمنون إخوة»} [al-Ḥujurāt: 10] — "The believers are but brothers." And God, Exalted is He, said, informing of Noah, peace be upon him: {«وأنصح لكم»} [al-Aʿrāf: 62] — "And I am sincere to you." And of Hūd, peace be upon him: {«وأنا لكم ناصح أمين»} [al-Aʿrāf: 68] — "And I am to you a sincere, trustworthy advisor."

As for the ḥadīths:

**181** — The first: from Abū Ruqayyah Tamīm ibn Aws al-Dārī, may God be pleased with him: that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «The religion is sincerity (al-naṣīḥah).» We said: "To whom?" He said: «To God, to His Book, to His Messenger, to the leaders of the Muslims, and to their common folk.» (1) Narrated by Muslim. (2)

**182** — The second: from Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, may God be pleased with him, who said: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, upon establishing the prayer, giving the zakāh, and sincerity to every Muslim. Agreed upon. (1)

**183** — The third: from Anas, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: «None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.» (1) Agreed upon. (2)

**Section 23 — On Enjoining Right and Forbidding Wrong**

God, Exalted is He, said: {«ولتكن منكم أمة يدعون إلى الخير ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر وأولئك هم المفلحون»} [Āl ʿImrān: 104] — "And let there be from among you a nation calling to goodness, enjoining right and forbidding wrong — and it is they who are the successful." And He, Exalted is He, said: {«كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس تأمرون بالمعروف وتنهون عن المنكر»} [Āl ʿImrān: 110] — "You are the best nation brought forth for mankind, enjoining right and forbidding wrong." And He, Exalted is He, said: {«خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين»} [al-Aʿrāf: 199] — "Take the forgiveness, command the good, and turn away from the ignorant." And He, Exalted is He, said: {«والمؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أولياء بعض يأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر»} [al-Tawbah: 71] — "And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another; they enjoin right and forbid wrong." And He, Exalted is He, said: {«لعن الذين كفروا من بني إسرائيل على لسان داود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون»} [al-Māʾidah: 78] — "Cursed were those who disbelieved from the Children of Israel upon the tongue of David and Jesus son of Mary — that was because they disobeyed and were transgressing. They would not forbid one another from the wrong they committed — evil indeed was what they used to do." And He, Exalted is He, said: {«وقل الحق من ربكم فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر»} [al-Kahf: 29] — "And say: The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve." And He, Exalted is He, said: {«فاصدع بما تؤمر»} [al-Ḥijr: 94] — "So proclaim openly what you are commanded." And He, Exalted is He, said: {«فأنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء وأخذنا الذين ظلموا بعذاب بئيس بما كانوا يفسقون»} [al-Aʿrāf: 165] — "So We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who wronged with a grievous punishment, because they were defiantly disobedient." And the verses on this subject are many and well-known.

(1) — As for the ḥadīths:

**184** — The first: from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say: «Whoever among you sees a wrong (munkar), let him change it with his hand; if he is unable, then with his tongue; if he is unable, then with his heart — and that is the weakest of faith.» Narrated by Muslim. (2)

**185** — The second: from Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him: that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: «There was no prophet whom God sent to a nation before me but that he had from his nation disciples (ḥawāriyyūn) (1) and companions who adhered to his Sunnah and followed his command. Then after them came successors (khalūf) (2) who say what they do not do, and do what they are not commanded. Whoever strives against them with his hand is a believer; whoever strives against them with his heart is a believer; whoever strives against them with his tongue is a believer — and beyond that there is not even a mustard seed of faith.» Narrated by Muslim. (3)

**186** — The third: from Abū al-Walīd ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, may God be pleased with him, who said: We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, upon hearing and obedience in hardship and ease, in enthusiasm and reluctance (al-munshaṭ wa al-makrah), and upon not contending for authority with its rightful people — unless you see clear disbelief (kufran bawāḥan) regarding which you have from God, Exalted is He, a proof — and upon speaking the truth wherever we may be, not fearing in God the blame of any blamer. Agreed upon. (1)

«Al-munshaṭ wa al-makrah» — with the fatḥah on both their mīms — meaning: in ease and in difficulty. And «al-atharah»: the exclusive appropriation of what is shared — and its explanation has preceded. «Bawāḥan» — with the fatḥah on the bāʾ, followed by a wāw, then an alif, then an unpointed ḥāʾ — meaning: manifest, admitting no interpretation.

**187** — The fourth: from al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, may God be pleased with both of them, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: «The parable of the one who upholds the limits (ḥudūd) of God and the one who falls into them is like a people who cast lots for a ship — some of them became its upper deck and some its lower deck. Those in the lower deck, when they needed water, had to pass by those above them, so they said: "If we were to bore a hole in our own portion, we would not harm those above us." If they leave them to what they intend, they all perish; and if they seize their hands, they are all saved — and all are saved.» Narrated by al-Bukhārī. (1)

«The one who upholds the limits of God, Exalted is He» — its meaning: the one who rejects them (the violations), standing firm in repelling and removing them. And the intended meaning of «the limits» is: what God has forbidden. «Istahamū»: they cast lots.

**188** — The fifth: from the Mother of the Believers, Umm Salamah Hind bint Abī Umayyah Ḥudhayfah, may God be pleased with her, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: «Rulers will be appointed over you — you will recognize (some of their deeds) and disapprove (of others). Whoever disapproves (with his heart) has absolved himself; whoever rejects (with his tongue or hand) has been saved; but whoever is pleased and follows — (he is the sinner).» They said: "O Messenger of God, shall we not fight them?" He said: «No, as long as they establish the prayer among you.» Narrated by Muslim. (1)

Its meaning: whoever disapproves with his heart, and is unable to reject with hand or tongue, has absolved himself of sin and fulfilled his duty; and whoever rejects according to his capacity has been saved from this disobedience; and whoever is pleased with their deeds and follows them — he is the sinner.

**189** — The sixth: from the Mother of the Believers, Umm al-Ḥakam Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, may God be pleased with her: that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered upon her in a state of alarm, saying: «There is no god but God. Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near! Today a gap has been opened in the dam of Gog and Magog (Yaʾjūj wa Maʾjūj) like this» — and he made a circle with his two fingers, the thumb and the one next to it. I said: "O Messenger of God, shall we perish while there are righteous people among us?" He said: «Yes, when wickedness (al-khubth) (1) becomes abundant.» Agreed upon. (2)

**190** — The seventh: from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him...

chapters.title_en: Section 26 — The Obligation of Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
وسلم - قال: «إياكم والجلوس في الطرقات!» فقالوا: يا رسول الله، ما لنا من

مجالسنا بد، نتحدث فيها. فقال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «فإذا أبيتم

إلا المجلس، فأعطوا الطريق حقه». قالوا: وما حق الطريق يا رسول الله؟ قال:

«غض البصر، وكف الأذى، ورد السلام، والأمر  بالمعروف، والنهي عن المنكر».

متفق عليه. (1)

| 191 - 
# الثامن: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم

- رأى خاتما من ذهب في يد رجل فنزعه فطرحه، وقال: «يعمد أحدكم إلى جمرة من

نار فيجعلها في يده!».‍‍‍‍‍‍ فقيل للرجل بعدما ذهب رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم: خذ خاتمك انتفع به. قال: لا والله لا آخذه أبدا وقد طرحه رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم. رواه مسلم. (1)

| 192 - 
# التاسع: عن أبي سعيد الحسن البصري: أن عائذ بن عمرو - رضي الله عنه - دخل

على عبيد الله بن زياد، فقال: أي بني، إني سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - يقول: «إن شر الرعاء الحطمة (1)» فإياك أن تكون منهم، فقال له: اجلس

فإنما أنت من نخالة أصحاب محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال: وهل كانت لهم

نخالة إنما كانت النخالة بعدهم وفي غيرهم. رواه مسلم. (2)

| 193 - 
# العاشر: عن حذيفة - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«والذي نفسي بيده، لتأمرن بالمعروف، ولتنهون عن المنكر أو ليوشكن الله أن

يبعث عليكم عقابا منه
# ثم تدعونه فلا يستجاب لكم». رواه الترمذي، (1) وقال: «حديث حسن».

| 194 - 
# الحادي عشر: عن أبي سعيد الخدري - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - قال: «أفضل الجهاد كلمة عدل عند سلطان جائر». رواه أبو داود

والترمذي، وقال: «حديث حسن». (1)

| 195 - 
# الثاني عشر: عن أبي عبد الله طارق بن شهاب البجلي الأحمسي - رضي الله

عنه: أن رجلا سأل النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وقد وضع رجله في الغرز: أي

الجهاد أفضل؟ قال: «كلمة حق عند سلطان جائر». رواه النسائي بإسناد صحيح.

(1)
# «الغرز» بغين معجمة مفتوحة ثم راء ساكنة ثم زاي: وهو ركاب كور الجمل إذا

كان من جلد أو خشب وقيل: لا يختص بجلد وخشب.

| 196 - 
# الثالث عشر: عن ابن مسعود - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم: «إن أول ما دخل النقص على بني إسرائيل أنه كان الرجل  يلقى

الرجل، فيقول: يا هذا، اتق الله ودع ما تصنع فإنه لا يحل لك، ثم يلقاه من

الغد وهو على حاله، فلا يمنعه ذلك أن يكون أكيله وشريبه وقعيده، فلما فعلوا

ذلك ضرب الله قلوب بعضهم ببعض» ثم قال: {لعن الذين كفروا من بني إسرائيل

على لسان داود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون كانوا لا يتناهون

عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون ترى كثيرا منهم يتولون الذين كفروا

لبئس ما قدمت لهم أنفسهم} - إلى قوله - {فاسقون} [المائدة: 78 - 81] ثم

قال: «كلا، والله لتأمرن بالمعروف، ولتنهون عن المنكر، ولتأخذن على يد

الظالم، ولتأطرنه على الحق أطرا، ولتقصرنه على الحق قصرا، أو ليضربن الله

بقلوب بعضكم على بعض، ثم ليلعننكم كما لعنهم». رواه أبو داود والترمذي،

وقال: «حديث حسن». (1)

| [ص: 86]
# هذا لفظ أبي داود، ولفظ الترمذي، قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«لما وقعت بنو إسرائيل في المعاصي نهتهم علماؤهم فلم ينتهوا، فجالسوهم في

مجالسهم، وواكلوهم وشاربوهم، فضرب الله قلوب بعضهم ببعض، ولعنهم على لسان

داود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون» فجلس رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - وكان متكئا، فقال: «لا، والذي نفسي بيده حتى تأطروهم على

الحق أطرا».
# قوله: «تأطروهم»: أي تعطفوهم. «ولتقصرنه»: أي لتحبسنه.

| 197 - 
# الرابع عشر: عن أبي بكر الصديق - رضي الله عنه - قال: يا أيها الناس،

إنكم لتقرؤون هذه الآية: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا عليكم أنفسكم لا يضركم من ضل

إذا اهتديتم} [المائدة: 105] وإني سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

يقول: «إن الناس إذا رأوا الظالم فلم يأخذوا على يديه أوشك أن يعمهم الله

بعقاب منه». رواه أبو داود والترمذي والنسائي بأسانيد صحيحة. (1)

$ 24 - باب تغليظ عقوبة من أمر بمعروف أو نهى عن منكر وخالف قوله فعله
# قال الله تعالى: {أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم وأنتم تتلون الكتاب

أفلا تعقلون} [البقرة: 44]، وقال تعالى: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما

لا تفعلون كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا  ما لا تفعلون} [الصف: 2 - 3]، وقال

تعالى إخبارا عن شعيب - صلى الله عليه وسلم: {وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما

أنهاكم عنه} [هود:88].
#

| 198 - 
# وعن أبي زيد أسامة بن حارثة رضي الله عنهما، قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - يقول: «يؤتى بالرجل يوم القيامة فيلقى في النار، فتندلق

أقتاب بطنه فيدور بها كما يدور الحمار في الرحى، فيجتمع إليه أهل النار،

فيقولون: يا فلان، ما لك؟ ألم تك تأمر بالمعروف وتنهى عن المنكر؟ فيقول:

بلى، كنت آمر بالمعروف ولا آتيه، وأنهى عن المنكر وآتيه». متفق عليه. (1)
# قوله: «تندلق» هو بالدال المهملة، ومعناه تخرج. و «الأقتاب»: الأمعاء،

واحدها قتب.

$ 25 - باب الأمر بأداء الأمانة
# قال الله تعالى: {إن الله يأمركم أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها} [النساء:

58]، وقال تعالى: {إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السماوات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن

يحملنها وأشفقن منها وحملها الإنسان إنه كان ظلوما جهولا} [الأحزاب: 72].
#

| 199 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-م-ر (ʿamara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To command, order, or enjoin; building up and cultivating (as in ʿimārah, flourishing of the land).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Al-maʿrūf (the good) is that which is recognized and approved by sound intellect and divine law; al-munkar (the evil) is that which is rejected and disapproved.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is commanding; metaphorical extension covers the moral imperative of societal rectification.
- Root: ن-ه-ي (nahā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To forbid, prohibit, restrain from.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Prohibition of evil (nahy ʿan al-munkar) is the counterpart to commanding good; both are collective obligations (furūḍ kifāyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal prohibition; rhetorically used for deterrence and correction.
- Root: ج-ل-س (jalasa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To sit, to remain seated; majlis (sitting place).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal contexts, refers to gatherings where social interaction occurs, carrying ethical responsibilities.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sitting; metaphorically denotes social fellowship and its attendant duties.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Condition and Exception (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The phrase «فإذا أبيتم إلا المجلس» employs the conditional particle idhā followed by an exceptive construction (illā al-majlis), governing the apodosis that follows, indicating a concession with imposed conditions.
chapters.translation:
I say — and success is from Allah:

**Hadith 190:** The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Beware of sitting in the roadways!» They said: O Messenger of Allah, we have no alternative but to sit in our gatherings to converse therein. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «If you insist on sitting, then give the road its due right.» They asked: And what is the due right of the road, O Messenger of Allah? He said: «Lowering the gaze, refraining from harm, returning the greeting of peace, commanding the good, and forbidding the evil.» [Agreed upon by al-Bukhārī and Muslim]

**Hadith 191:** The eighth: On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both): That the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) saw a gold ring on the hand of a man, so he removed it and cast it away, saying: «Would one of you deliberately take a burning ember of fire and place it in his hand!» After the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) had departed, it was said to the man: Take your ring and benefit from it. He said: No, by Allah, I will never take it, for the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) cast it away. [Narrated by Muslim]

**Hadith 192:** The ninth: On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī: That ʿĀʾidh ibn ʿAmr (may Allah be pleased with him) entered upon ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyād and said: O my son, I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: «Indeed, the worst of shepherds are those who crush (al-ḥuṭamah)» — so beware of being among them. ʿUbayd Allāh said to him: Sit down, for you are but of the chaff (nukhālah) of the companions of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him). He replied: Was there ever chaff among them? Indeed, the chaff came after them and among others. [Narrated by Muslim]

**Hadith 193:** The tenth: On the authority of Ḥudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «By Him in Whose hand is my soul, you must command the good and forbid the evil, or else Allah will soon send upon you a punishment from Him, and then you will supplicate to Him and your supplication will not be answered.» [Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, who said: A ḥasan (good) hadith]

**Hadith 194:** The eleventh: On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «The most excellent form of jihad is a word of justice spoken before a tyrannical ruler.» [Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, who said: A ḥasan hadith]

**Hadith 195:** The twelfth: On the authority of Abū ʿAbd Allāh Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb al-Bajalī al-Aḥmasī (may Allah be pleased with him): That a man asked the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) — while he had placed his foot in the stirrup (al-gharz) —: Which jihad is most excellent? He said: «A word of truth before a tyrannical ruler.» [Narrated by al-Nasāʾī with a sound chain of transmission]

The commentator (al-Nawawī) says: «Al-gharz» — with an unpointed ghayn (gh), then a silent rāʾ, then a zāy — is the stirrup of the camel's saddle (kawr) when it is made of leather or wood; and it is said that it is not restricted to leather and wood.

**Hadith 196:** The thirteenth: On the authority of Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Indeed, the first deficiency that entered upon the Children of Israel was that a man would meet another man and say: O this one, fear Allah and abandon what you are doing, for it is not lawful for you. Then he would meet him the next day while he was still in the same state, and that would not prevent him from being his companion in eating, drinking, and sitting. When they did that, Allah struck the hearts of some of them against others.» Then he said: {«Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and of Jesus, son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressing. They did not forbid one another from the evil they committed. Wretched indeed was what they used to do. You see many of them taking the disbelievers as allies. Wretched indeed is what their souls have sent forth for them»} — up to His saying — {«and defiantly disobedient»} [al-Māʾidah 5:78–81]. Then he said: «No, by Allah, you must command the good and forbid the evil, and you must seize the hand of the wrongdoer, and you must bend him toward the truth with force, and you must restrain him to the truth with constraint — or else Allah will strike the hearts of some of you against others, and then He will curse you as He cursed them.» [Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, who said: A ḥasan hadith]

This is the wording of Abū Dāwūd. The wording of al-Tirmidhī is: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «When the Children of Israel fell into sins, their scholars forbade them, but they did not desist. So they sat with them in their gatherings, and ate with them, and drank with them. Thus Allah struck the hearts of some of them against others, and cursed them by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressing.» Then the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) sat up — and he had been reclining — and said: «No, by Him in Whose hand is my soul, until you bend them toward the truth with force.»

The commentator (al-Nawawī) says: His saying «taʾṭirūhum» (you bend them) means: you incline them. And «l-taqṣirannahu» (you restrain him) means: you confine him.

**Hadith 197:** The fourteenth: On the authority of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: O people, you recite this verse: {«O you who have believed, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves. Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided»} [al-Māʾidah 5:105]. And indeed I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: «Indeed, when people see a wrongdoer and do not seize his hand [to stop him], Allah is about to encompass them all with a punishment from Him.» [Narrated by Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Nasāʾī with sound chains of transmission]

---

**Section 24 — The Severity of Punishment for One Who Commands Good or Forbids Evil but Contradicts His Words with His Deeds**

Allah the Exalted said: {«Do you command people to righteousness while you forget yourselves, while you recite the Book? Do you not then reason?»} [al-Baqarah 2:44]. And He the Exalted said: {«O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Greatly hateful in the sight of Allah is that you say what you do not do»} [al-Ṣaff 61:2–3]. And He the Exalted said, informing about Shuʿayb (peace be upon him): {«And I do not intend to differ from you in that which I have forbidden you»} [Hūd 11:88].

**Hadith 198:** On the authority of Abū Zayd Usāmah ibn Ḥārithah (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: «A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and cast into the Fire. His intestines (aqtāb) will spill out (tandaliq), and he will circle around with them just as the donkey circles around the millstone. The people of the Fire will gather around him and say: O so-and-so, what is the matter with you? Did you not use to command the good and forbid the evil? He will say: Yes, I used to command the good but not practice it, and I used to forbid the evil and practice it.» [Agreed upon by al-Bukhārī and Muslim]
