I say: The first [interpretation] is that it softens [the hearts]. And it was said: its meaning is that it makes each yearn for the other through embellishment and enticement. And it was said: it makes each resemble the other.

| 668 -
# On the authority of Abū Hunaydah Wāʾil ibn Ḥujr — may God be pleased with him — who said: Salamah ibn Yazīd al-Juʿfī asked the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — and said: O Prophet of God, have you considered if there arise over us rulers who demand from us their right and withhold from us our right, what do you command us? So he turned away from him, then he asked him again, and the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: «Hear and obey, for upon them is what they have been burdened with, and upon you is what you have been burdened with.» Narrated by Muslim. (1)

| 669 -
# On the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd — may God be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: «There will be after me preferential treatment (atharah) and matters you will disapprove of!» They said: O Messenger of God, what do you command whoever among us reaches that time? He said: «You fulfill the right that is upon you, and you ask God for what is yours.» Agreed upon. (2)

| 670 -
# On the authority of Abū Hurayrah — may God be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: «Whoever obeys me has obeyed God, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed God. Whoever obeys the ruler has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys the ruler has disobeyed me.» Agreed upon. (1)

| 671 -
# On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās — may God be pleased with them both — that the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: «Whoever dislikes something from his ruler, let him be patient, for whoever departs from the authority by a handspan dies a death of ignorance (jāhiliyyah).» Agreed upon. (1)

| 672 -
# On the authority of Abū Bakrah — may God be pleased with him — who said: I heard the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — say: «Whoever dishonors the ruler, God dishonors him.» Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, (1) who said: «A good (ḥasan) hadith.»
# In this chapter there are many hadiths in the authentic collections. Some have already preceded in previous chapters.

$ 81 — Chapter on the Prohibition of Seeking Authority and Choosing to Abandon Positions of Governance When It Is Not Obligatory Upon One or When There Is No Need for It
# God the Exalted has said: {That is the abode of the Hereafter — We assign it to those who do not desire exaltation upon the earth nor corruption. And the outcome is for the God-fearing} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 83].
#

| 673 -
# On the authority of Abū Saʿīd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samurah — may God be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said to me: «O ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samurah, do not ask for authority; for if you are given it without asking, you will be aided upon it, and if you are given it upon asking, you will be entrusted to it. And if you swear an oath and see something better than it, then do that which is better and expiate for your oath.» Agreed upon. (1)

| 674 -
# On the authority of Abū Dharr — may God be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: «O Abū Dharr, I see that you are weak, and I love for you what I love for myself. Do not take command over two, and do not manage the wealth of an orphan.» Narrated by Muslim. (1)

| 675 -
# On his authority, he said: I said: O Messenger of God, will you not appoint me? So he struck my shoulder with his hand, then said: «O Abū Dharr, you are weak, and it is a trust (amānah), and it will be on the Day of Resurrection a disgrace and regret — except for one who takes it with its due right and fulfills what is upon him in it.» Narrated by Muslim. (1)

| 676 -
# On the authority of Abū Hurayrah — may God be pleased with him — that the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: «You will be eager for authority, and it will be a regret on the Day of Resurrection.» Narrated by al-Bukhārī. (1)

$ 82 — Chapter on Urging the Ruler, the Judge, and Others Among Those in Positions of Authority to Take a Righteous Advisor, and Warning Them Against Evil Companions and Accepting from Them
# God the Exalted has said: {Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing} [al-Zukhruf: 67].
#

| 677 -
# On the authority of Abū Saʿīd and Abū Hurayrah — may God be pleased with them both — that the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: «God has not sent any prophet, nor appointed any successor (khalīfah), except that he had two advisors: an advisor that commands him to good and urges him upon it, and an advisor that commands him to evil and urges him upon it. And the protected one is he whom God protects.» Narrated by al-Bukhārī. (1)

| 678 -
# On the authority of ʿĀʾishah — may God be pleased with her — who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: «When God desires good for a ruler, He grants him a truthful advisor (wazīr ṣidq): if he forgets, he reminds him; and if he remembers, he aids him. And when He desires other than that for him, He grants him an evil advisor: if he forgets, he does not remind him; and if he remembers, he does not aid him.» Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1) with a sound chain upon the condition of Muslim.

$ 83 — Chapter on the Prohibition of Appointing to Authority, Judgeship, and Other Positions of Governance Whoever Asks for It or Is Eager for It, Thus Exposing Himself

| 679 -
# On the authority of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī — may God be pleased with him — who said: I entered upon the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — along with two men from my paternal cousins. One of them said: O Messenger of God, appoint us over some of what God — Mighty and Majestic — has entrusted to you. And the other said the like of that. So he said: «By God, we do not appoint to this work anyone who asks for it, nor anyone who is eager for it.» Agreed upon. (1)

| (1) — Book of Etiquette (Kitāb al-Adab)

$ 84 — Chapter on Modesty (al-Ḥayāʾ), Its Virtue, and the Urging to Adopt It as a Character Trait

| 680 -
# On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar — may God be pleased with them both — that the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — passed by a man from the Anṣār who was admonishing his brother about modesty. So the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: «Leave him, for modesty is from faith (īmān).» Agreed upon. (1)

| 681 -
# On the authority of ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn — may God be pleased with them both — who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: «Modesty does not bring anything but good.» Agreed upon. (1)
# In a narration of Muslim: «Modesty is all good» — or he said: «Modesty is entirely good.»

| 682 -
# On the authority of Abū Hurayrah — may God be pleased with him — that the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: «Faith has seventy-some or sixty-some branches: the most excellent of them is the saying: there is no god but God (lā ilāha illā Allāh), and the lowest of them is removing harm from the path, and modesty is a branch of faith.» Agreed upon. (1)
# «Al-biḍʿ» — with kasrah of the bāʾ, and it is permissible to open it — it is from three to ten.
# And «al-shuʿbah»: the part and the trait. And «al-imāṭah»: the removal. And «al-adhā»: that which harms, such as a stone, a thorn, mud, ash, filth, and the like.

| 683 -
# On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī — may God be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — was more intense in modesty than a virgin in her seclusion, and when he saw something he disliked, we recognized it in his face. Agreed upon. (1)

| [p. 220]
# The scholars said: The reality of modesty (ḥayāʾ) is a disposition (khuluq) that impels one to abandon the reprehensible and prevents one from falling short in

chapters.title_en: Section 70: The Right of the One Who Has a Right; Chapter 85: Guarding Secrets; Chapter 86: Fulfilling Covenants and Keeping Promises; Chapter 87: Persevering in Customary Good Deeds
chapters.arabic_text:
حق ذي الحق. وروينا عن أبي القاسم الجنيد رحمه الله، قال: الحياء: رؤية

الآلاء - أي النعم - ورؤية التقصير، فيتولد بينهما حالة تسمى حياء (2).

والله أعلم.

$ 85 - باب حفظ السر
# قال الله تعالى: {وأوفوا بالعهد إن العهد كان مسؤولا} [الإسراء: 34].

| 684 - 
# وعن أبي سعيد الخدري - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم: «إن من أشر الناس عند الله منزلة يوم القيامة الرجل يفضي إلى

المرأة وتفضي إليه، ثم ينشر سرها». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 685 - 
# وعن عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما: أن عمر - رضي الله عنه - حين تأيمت

بنته حفصة، قال: لقيت عثمان بن عفان - رضي الله عنه - فعرضت عليه حفصة،

فقلت: إن شئت أنكحتك حفصة بنت عمر؟ قال: سأنظر في أمري. فلبثت ليالي ثم

لقيني، فقال: قد بدا لي أن لا أتزوج يومي هذا. فلقيت أبا بكر - رضي الله

عنه - فقلت: إن شئت أنكحتك حفصة بنت عمر، فصمت أبو بكر - رضي الله عنه -

فلم يرجع إلي شيئا! فكنت عليه أوجد مني على عثمان، فلبث ليالي ثم خطبها

النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فأنكحتها إياه. فلقيني أبو بكر، فقال: لعلك

وجدت علي حين عرضت علي حفصة فلم أرجع إليك شيئا؟ فقلت: نعم، قال: فإنه لم

يمنعني أن أرجع إليك فيما عرضت علي إلا أني كنت علمت أن النبي - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - ذكرها، فلم أكن لأفشي سر رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ولو

تركها النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لقبلتها. رواه البخاري. (1)
# «تأيمت» أي: صارت بلا زوج، وكان زوجها توفي - رضي الله عنه. «وجدت»:

غضبت.

| 686 - 
# وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت: كن أزواج النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

عنده، فأقبلت فاطمة رضي الله عنها تمشي، ما تخطئ مشيتها من مشية رسول الله

- صلى الله عليه وسلم - شيئا، فلما رآها رحب بها، وقال:

| [ص: 221]
# «مرحبا بابنتي»، ثم  أجلسها عن يمينه أو عن شماله، ثم سارها فبكت بكاء

شديدا، فلما رأى جزعها، سارها الثانية فضحكت، فقلت لها: خصك رسول الله -

صلى الله عليه وسلم - من بين نسائه بالسرار، ثم أنت تبكين! فلما قام رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - سألتها: ما قال لك رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم -؟ قالت: ما كنت لأفشي على رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - سره،

فلما توفي رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قلت: عزمت عليك بما لي عليك من

الحق، لما حدثتني ما قال لك رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم؟ فقالت: أما

الآن فنعم، أما حين سارني في المرة الأولى فأخبرني أن جبريل كان يعارضه

القرآن في كل سنة مرة أو مرتين، وأنه عارضه الآن مرتين، وإني لا أرى الأجل

إلا قد اقترب، فاتقي الله واصبري، فإنه نعم السلف أنا لك، فبكيت بكائي الذي

رأيت، فلما رأى جزعي سارني الثانية، فقال: «يا فاطمة، أما ترضين أن تكوني

سيدة نساء المؤمنين، أو سيدة نساء هذه الأمة؟» فضحكت ضحكي الذي رأيت. متفق

عليه، وهذا لفظ مسلم. (1)

| 687 - 
# وعن ثابت، عن أنس - رضي الله عنه - قال: أتى علي رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - وأنا ألعب مع الغلمان، فسلم علينا، فبعثني إلى حاجة، فأبطأت

على أمي. فلما جئت، قالت: ما حبسك؟ فقلت: بعثني رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - لحاجة، قالت: ما حاجته؟ قلت: إنها سر. قالت: لا تخبرن بسر رسول الله

- صلى الله عليه وسلم - أحدا، قال أنس: والله لو حدثت به أحدا لحدثتك به يا

ثابت. رواه مسلم وروى البخاري بعضه مختصرا. (1)

$ 86 - باب الوفاء بالعهد وإنجاز الوعد
# قال الله تعالى: {وأوفوا بالعهد إن العهد كان مسئولا} [الإسراء: 34]،

وقال تعالى: {وأوفوا بعهد الله إذا عاهدتم} [النحل: 91]، وقال تعالى: {يا

أيها الذين آمنوا أوفوا بالعقود} [المائدة: 1]، وقال تعالى: {يا أيها الذين

آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون}

[الصف: 2 - 3].
#

| 688 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة  - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«آية المنافق ثلاث: إذا حدث كذب، وإذا وعد أخلف، وإذا اؤتمن خان». متفق

عليه. (1)
# زاد في رواية لمسلم: «وإن صام وصلى وزعم أنه مسلم».

| 689 - 
# وعن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما: أن رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - قال: «أربع من كن فيه كان منافقا خالصا، ومن كانت فيه خصلة

منهن كانت فيه خصلة من النفاق حتى يدعها: إذا اؤتمن خان، وإذا حدث كذب،

وإذا عاهد غدر، وإذا خاصم فجر». متفق عليه. (1)

| 690 - 
# وعن جابر - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال لي النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لو

قد جاء مال البحرين أعطيتك هكذا وهكذا وهكذا» فلم يجئ مال البحرين حتى قبض

النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فلما جاء مال البحرين أمر أبو بكر - رضي الله

عنه - فنادى: من كان له عند رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عدة أو دين

فليأتنا، فأتيته وقلت له: إن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال لي كذا

وكذا، فحثى لي حثية فعددتها، فإذا هي خمسمئة، فقال لي: خذ مثليها. متفق

عليه. (1)

$ 87 - باب المحافظة على ما اعتاده من الخير
# قال الله تعالى: {إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم}

[الرعد: 11]، وقال تعالى: {ولا تكونوا كالتي نقضت غزلها من بعد قوة أنكاثا}

[النحل: 92].
# و «الأنكاث»: جمع نكث، وهو الغزل المنقوض.
# وقال تعالى: {ولا يكونوا كالذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبل فطال عليهم الأمد

فقست قلوبهم} [الحديد: 16]، وقال تعالى: {فما رعوها حق رعايتها} [الحديد:

27].
#

| 691 - 
# وعن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما، قال: قال لي رسول الله -
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of life (ḥayāh) and its derivative states; al-ḥayāʾ (shyness/modesty) as a life-giving moral trait.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ḥayāʾ is a moral faculty restraining the soul from base acts, rooted in awareness of divine oversight.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is life; metaphorical (majāz) sense is the "life" of the heart through virtuous shame.
- Root: س-ر-ر (s-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of concealment and the inner self (sirr); the secret as that which is hidden.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sirr denotes what is concealed in the heart; revealing it (ifshāʾ) is a breach of trust (amānah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is hidden speech; metaphorical is the inner conscience, and "whispering" (sirār) as intimate counsel.
- Root: ع-ه-د (ʿ-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of a pledge, covenant, or entrusted obligation (ʿahd).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿAhd is a binding agreement with God or man; fulfilling it (īfāʾ) is a mark of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is a contract; metaphorical is the moral duty of promise-keeping (waʿd).
- Root: ن-ق-ض (n-q-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of unravelling, breaking, or reversing a bond.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Naqḍ signifies violating a covenant; an-nakth is the unspun thread, a metaphor for fickleness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is physical unravelling; metaphorical is spiritual regression from steadfastness.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — For phrases like "الآلاء - أي النعم", the explicative appositive clarifies the preceding term; also, conditional clauses (in ḥadīth 688) follow the rule of jumlat al-sharṭ with apodosis marked by fa-.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the right of the one who has a right (over you) is to honour it. We have narrated from Abū al-Qāsim al-Junayd (may God have mercy on him) that he said: "Al-ḥayāʾ (modesty) is the perception of divine favours (ālāʾ) — that is, blessings (niʿam) — and the perception of one's own shortcoming (taqṣīr); thus, between the two, a state is generated which is called modesty (ḥayāʾ)." And God knows best.

Chapter 85 — On Guarding Secrets

God the Exalted has said: {«وأوفوا بالعهد إن العهد كان مسؤولا»} [Al-Isrāʾ: 34] — "And fulfil the covenant; indeed, the covenant will be asked about."

684. On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Verily, among the most wicked of people in rank before God on the Day of Resurrection is a man who consorts with his wife, and she consorts with him, then he spreads her secret.» Narrated by Muslim.

685. On the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar (may God be pleased with them both): When his daughter Ḥafṣah became a widow (taʾayyamat), ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) said: I met ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān (may God be pleased with him) and offered Ḥafṣah to him, saying: "If you wish, I shall marry you to Ḥafṣah bint ʿUmar." He said: "I shall consider my affair." I waited several nights, then he met me and said: "It has become apparent to me that I shall not marry at this time." Then I met Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) and said: "If you wish, I shall marry you to Ḥafṣah bint ʿUmar." Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) remained silent and did not return any answer to me! I was more displeased (awjad) with him than I had been with ʿUthmān. I waited several nights, then the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) proposed to her, and I married her to him. Then Abū Bakr met me and said: "Perhaps you were displeased with me when I offered Ḥafṣah and I did not return any answer to you?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Nothing prevented me from answering you regarding what you offered except that I knew that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) had mentioned her, and I would not divulge the secret of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). Had the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) left her, I would have accepted her." Narrated by al-Bukhārī.
[The commentator says:] "Taʾayyamat" means: she became without a husband, for her husband had died (may God be pleased with him). "Wajidta" means: you became angry.

686. On the authority of ʿĀʾishah (may God be pleased with her), who said: The wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) were with him, then Fāṭimah (may God be pleased with her) approached walking — her gait did not differ in any way from the gait of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). When he saw her, he welcomed her and said: «Welcome, my daughter», then he seated her on his right or on his left, then he whispered to her (sārarahā), and she wept intensely. When he saw her distress, he whispered to her a second time, and she laughed. I said to her: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) singled you out among his wives for this private counsel, yet you weep!" When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) stood up, I asked her: "What did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say to you?" She said: "I would never divulge the secret of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him)." When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) passed away, I said: "I adjure you by the right I have upon you, that you tell me what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to you." She said: "As for now, yes. When he whispered to me the first time, he informed me that Gabriel (Jibrīl) used to review the Qurʾān with him once or twice every year, and that he had reviewed it with him now twice, and that I do not see but that the term (of my life) has drawn near. So fear God and be patient, for indeed I am an excellent predecessor (salaf) for you." So I wept that weeping which you saw. When he saw my distress, he whispered to me a second time and said: «O Fāṭimah, are you not pleased to be the mistress of the women of the believers, or the mistress of the women of this nation?» So I laughed that laughter which you saw. Agreed upon (by al-Bukhārī and Muslim), and this is the wording of Muslim.

687. On the authority of Thābit, from Anas (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) came upon me while I was playing with the boys, and he greeted us with salām. Then he sent me on an errand, and I was delayed in returning to my mother. When I came, she said: "What detained you?" I said: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sent me on an errand." She said: "What was his errand?" I said: "It is a secret." She said: "Do not tell anyone the secret of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him)." Anas said: "By God, had I told it to anyone, I would have told you, O Thābit." Narrated by Muslim, and al-Bukhārī narrated part of it in abbreviated form.

Chapter 86 — On Fulfilling the Covenant and Keeping Promises

God the Exalted has said: {«وأوفوا بالعهد إن العهد كان مسئولا»} [Al-Isrāʾ: 34] — "And fulfil the covenant; indeed, the covenant will be asked about." And the Exalted said: {«وأوفوا بعهد الله إذا عاهدتم»} [Al-Naḥl: 91] — "And fulfil the covenant of God when you have covenanted." And the Exalted said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا أوفوا بالعقود»} [Al-Māʾidah: 1] — "O you who believe, fulfil the contracts." And the Exalted said: {«يا أيها الذين آمنوا لم تقولون ما لا تفعلون كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون»} [Al-Ṣaff: 2–3] — "O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? Greatly hateful is it in the sight of God that you say what you do not do."

688. On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him): The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «The sign of the hypocrite (munāfiq) is three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks (his promise); and when he is entrusted, he betrays.» Agreed upon. In a narration of Muslim, there is an addition: «Even if he fasts and prays and claims that he is a Muslim.»

689. On the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may God be pleased with them both): The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Four traits, whoever possesses them is a pure hypocrite, and whoever possesses one of them possesses a trait of hypocrisy until he abandons it: when he is entrusted, he betrays; when he speaks, he lies; when he covenants, he acts treacherously; and when he quarrels, he behaves obscenely.» Agreed upon.

690. On the authority of Jābir (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to me: «If the wealth of Bahrain comes, I shall give you such-and-such, such-and-such, and such-and-such.» But the wealth of Bahrain did not come until the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) passed away. When the wealth of Bahrain came, Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) ordered a crier to announce: "Whoever has a promise or a debt owed by the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), let him come to us." So I came to him and said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to me such-and-such." He scooped out a handful for me, and I counted it — it was five hundred. Then he said to me: "Take twice that as well." Agreed upon.

Chapter 87 — On Persevering in What One Has Customarily Done of Good

God the Exalted has said: {«إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم»} [Al-Raʿd: 11] — "Indeed, God does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves." And the Exalted said: {«ولا تكونوا كالتي نقضت غزلها من بعد قوة أنكاثا»} [Al-Naḥl: 92] — "And do not be like her who unravels her spun thread after its strength, into broken strands." And "al-ankāth" is the plural of nikth, which is the unravelled thread. And the Exalted said: {«ولا يكونوا كالذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبل فطال عليهم الأمد فقست قلوبهم»} [Al-Ḥadīd: 16] — "And do not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and a long period passed over them, so their hearts hardened." And the Exalted said: {«فما رعوها حق رعايتها»} [Al-Ḥadīd: 27] — "But they did not observe it with due observance."

691. On the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may God be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to me: ...

chapters.title_en: Section 71 — The Book of Miscellaneous Admonitions and Etiquettes (Continued)
chapters.arabic_text:
صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يا عبد الله، لا تكن مثل فلان، كان يقوم الليل فترك

قيام الليل». متفق عليه. (1)

$ 88 - باب استحباب طيب الكلام وطلاقة الوجه عند اللقاء
# قال الله تعالى: {واخفض جناحك للمؤمنين} [الحجر: 88]، وقال تعالى: {ولو

كنت فظا غليظ القلب لانفضوا من حولك} [آل عمران: 159].
#

| 692 - 
# وعن  عدي بن حاتم - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «اتقوا النار ولو بشق تمرة، فمن لم يجد فبكلمة طيبة». متفق عليه. (1)

| 693 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«والكلمة الطيبة صدقة». متفق عليه، (1) وهو بعض حديث تقدم بطوله.

| 694 - 
# وعن أبي ذر - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال لي رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «لا تحقرن من المعروف شيئا، ولو أن تلقى أخاك بوجه طلق». رواه مسلم

(1).

$ 89 - باب استحباب بيان الكلام وإيضاحه للمخاطب وتكريره ليفهم إذا لم يفهم إلا بذلك

| 695 - 
# عن أنس - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان إذا تكلم

بكلمة أعادها ثلاثا حتى تفهم عنه، وإذا أتى على قوم فسلم عليهم سلم عليهم

ثلاثا. رواه البخاري. (1)

| 696 - 
# وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت: كان كلام رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم

- كلاما فصلا يفهمه كل من يسمعه. رواه أبو داود. (1)

$ 90 - باب إصغاء الجليس لحديث جليسه الذي ليس بحرام واستنصات العالم والواعظ حاضري مجلسه

| 697 - 
# عن جرير بن عبد الله - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال لي رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - في حجة الوداع: «استنصت الناس» ثم قال: «لا ترجعوا بعدي كفارا

يضرب بعضكم رقاب بعض». متفق عليه. (1)

$ 91 - باب الوعظ والاقتصاد فيه
# قال الله تعالى: {ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة} [النحل:

125].
#

| 698 - 
# وعن أبي وائل شقيق بن سلمة، قال: كان ابن مسعود - رضي الله عنه - يذكرنا

في كل خميس، فقال له رجل: يا أبا عبد الرحمن، لوددت أنك ذكرتنا كل يوم،

فقال: أما إنه يمنعني من ذلك أني أكره أن أملكم، وإني أتخولكم بالموعظة،

كما كان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يتخولنا بها مخافة السآمة علينا.

متفق عليه. (1)
# «يتخولنا»: يتعهدنا.

| 699 - 
# وعن أبي اليقظان عمار بن ياسر رضي الله عنهما، قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - يقول: «إن طول صلاة الرجل، وقصر خطبته، مئنة  من فقهه،

فأطيلوا الصلاة وأقصروا الخطبة». رواه مسلم. (1)
# «مئنة» بميم مفتوحة ثم همزة مكسورة ثم نون مشددة، أي: علامة دالة على

فقهه.

| 700 - 
# وعن معاوية بن الحكم السلمي - رضي الله عنه - قال: بينا أنا أصلي مع رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إذ عطس رجل من القوم، فقلت: يرحمك الله،

فرماني القوم بأبصارهم! فقلت: واثكل أمياه، ما شأنكم تنظرون إلي؟! فجعلوا

يضربون بأيديهم على أفخاذهم! فلما رأيتهم يصمتونني لكني سكت، فلما صلى رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فبأبي هو وأمي، ما رأيت معلما قبله ولا بعده

أحسن تعليما منه، فوالله ما كهرني، ولا ضربني، ولا شتمني. قال: «إن هذه

الصلاة لا يصلح فيها شيء من كلام الناس، إنما هي التسبيح والتكبير، وقراءة

القرآن»، أو كما قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم. قلت: يا رسول الله،

إني حديث عهد بجاهلية، وقد جاء الله بالإسلام، وإن منا رجالا يأتون الكهان؟

قال: «فلا تأتهم» قلت: ومنا رجال يتطيرون؟ قال: «ذاك شيء يجدونه في صدورهم

فلا يصدنهم». رواه مسلم. (1)
# «الثكل» بضم الثاء المثلثة: المصيبة والفجيعة. «ما كهرني» أي: ما نهرني.

| 701 - 
# وعن العرباض بن سارية - رضي الله عنه - قال: وعظنا رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - موعظة وجلت منها القلوب، وذرفت منها العيون ... وذكر الحديث

وقد سبق بكماله في باب الأمر بالمحافظة على السنة، وذكرنا أن الترمذي، قال:

«إنه حديث حسن صحيح». (1)

$ 92 - باب الوقار والسكينة
# قال الله تعالى: {وعباد الرحمان الذين يمشون على الأرض هونا وإذا خاطبهم

الجاهلون قالوا سلاما} [الفرقان: 63].
#

| 702 - 
# وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت: ما رأيت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم

- مستجمعا قط ضاحكا حتى ترى منه لهواته، إنما كان يتبسم. متفق عليه. (1)
# «اللهوات» جمع لهاة: وهي اللحمة التي في أقصى سقف الفم.

$ 93 - باب الندب إلى إتيان الصلاة والعلم ونحوهما من العبادات بالسكينة والوقار
# قال الله تعالى: {ومن يعظم شعائر الله فإنها من تقوى القلوب} [الحج: 32].
#

| 703 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: سمعت  رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - يقول: «إذا أقيمت الصلاة، فلا تأتوها وأنتم تسعون، وأتوها وأنتم

تمشون، وعليكم السكينة، فما أدركتم فصلوا، وما فاتكم فأتموا». متفق عليه.

(1)
# زاد مسلم في رواية له: «فإن أحدكم إذا كان يعمد إلى الصلاة فهو في صلاة».

| 704 - 
# وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أنه دفع مع النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

يوم عرفة فسمع النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وراءه زجرا شديدا وضربا وصوتا

للإبل، فأشار بسوطه إليهم، وقال: «يا أيها الناس، عليكم بالسكينة، فإن البر

ليس بالإيضاع». رواه البخاري، وروى مسلم بعضه. (1)
# «البر»: الطاعة. و «الإيضاع» بضاد معجمة قبلها ياء وهمزة مكسورة، وهو:

الإسراع.

$ 94 - باب إكرام الضيف

فقالوا سلاما قال سلام قوم منكرون فراغ إلى أهله فجاء بعجل سمين فقربه

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of obedience, compliance, and voluntary submission.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, denotes voluntary acts of worship (ṭāʿah) as opposed to obligatory duties (farīḍah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of following; metaphorically, the soul's compliance with divine command.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (Jumla Sharṭiyya) — The protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) structure governs the legal implications of the statements.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: «O ʿAbd Allah, do not be like so-and-so; he used to stand in night prayer, then he abandoned standing in night prayer.» Agreed upon (by al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

**Chapter 88 — The Recommendation of Pleasant Speech and a Cheerful Countenance Upon Meeting**

Allah the Exalted said: {«And lower your wing to the believers»} [Al-Ḥijr: 88]. And He the Exalted said: {«And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from about you»} [Āl ʿImrān: 159].

**692.** On the authority of ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Guard yourselves against the Fire, even with half a date; and whoever does not find [that], then [let him give] a kind word.» Agreed upon.

**693.** On the authority of Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — that the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «And the kind word is a charity.» Agreed upon. This is part of a ḥadīth that has preceded in full.

**694.** On the authority of Abū Dharr — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said to me: «Do not belittle any act of goodness, even that you meet your brother with a cheerful face.» Narrated by Muslim.

**Chapter 89 — The Recommendation of Clarifying Speech and Making It Clear to the Addressee, and Repeating It So That He Understands If He Does Not Understand Otherwise**

**695.** On the authority of Anas — may Allah be pleased with him — that the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — when he spoke a word, he would repeat it three times until it was understood from him; and when he came upon a people and greeted them, he would greet them three times. Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

**696.** On the authority of ʿĀʾishah — may Allah be pleased with her — who said: The speech of the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — was clear speech that everyone who heard it understood. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd.

**Chapter 90 — The Attentiveness of a Companion to the Speech of His Companion That Is Not Unlawful, and the Scholar and Preacher Asking Those Present in Their Assembly to Listen Attentively**

**697.** On the authority of Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said to me during the Farewell Pilgrimage: «Ask the people to listen attentively.» Then he said: «Do not revert after me to disbelievers, striking the necks of one another.» Agreed upon.

**Chapter 91 — Admonition and Moderation in It**

Allah the Exalted said: {«Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition»} [Al-Naḥl: 125].

**698.** On the authority of Abū Wāʾil Shaqīq ibn Salamah, who said: Ibn Masʿūd — may Allah be pleased with him — used to remind us every Thursday. A man said to him: O Abā ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, I wish that you would remind us every day. He said: As for that, what prevents me from it is that I dislike to weary you, and I choose the right time for admonition with you, just as the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — used to choose the right time for us with it, fearing weariness upon us. Agreed upon. «Yatakhawwalunā» means: he would attend to us at intervals.

**699.** On the authority of Abū al-Yaqẓān ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir — may Allah be pleased with them both — who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — say: «Indeed, the length of a man's prayer and the shortness of his sermon are a sign of his understanding (fiqh); so lengthen the prayer and shorten the sermon.» Narrated by Muslim. «Maʾinnah» — with an open mīm, then a kasrah on the hamzah, then a shaddah on the nūn — means: a sign indicating his understanding.

**700.** On the authority of Muʿāwiyah ibn al-Ḥakam al-Sulamī — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: While I was praying with the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — a man from the people sneezed, and I said: May Allah have mercy on you. The people glared at me with their eyes! So I said: Woe to my mother, what is the matter with you that you look at me?! They began striking their hands upon their thighs! When I saw them silencing me, I fell silent. When the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — finished the prayer — may my father and mother be his ransom — I have never seen a teacher before him nor after him who taught better than he did. By Allah, he did not rebuke me, nor strike me, nor revile me. He said: «Indeed, this prayer does not admit anything of the speech of people; it is only glorification (tasbīḥ), magnification (takbīr), and recitation of the Qurʾān» — or as the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said. I said: O Messenger of Allah, I am recently emerged from ignorance (jāhiliyyah), and Allah has brought Islam; and among us there are men who go to soothsayers? He said: «Then do not go to them.» I said: And among us there are men who practice augury (taṭayyur)? He said: «That is something they find in their breasts; let it not turn them away.» Narrated by Muslim. «Al-Thakal» — with a ḍammah on the thāʾ — means: calamity and affliction. «Mā kaharanī» means: he did not rebuke me harshly.

**701.** On the authority of al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — admonished us with an admonition from which hearts trembled and from which eyes shed tears... and he mentioned the ḥadīth, which has already preceded in full in the chapter on the command to adhere to the Sunnah; and we mentioned that al-Tirmidhī said: «It is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth.»

**Chapter 92 — Dignity and Tranquility**

Allah the Exalted said: {«And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth gently, and when the ignorant address them, they say words of peace»} [Al-Furqān: 63].

**702.** On the authority of ʿĀʾishah — may Allah be pleased with her — who said: I never saw the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — laughing fully so that his uvula (lahawāt) could be seen; he only used to smile. Agreed upon. «Al-Lahawāt» is the plural of lahāh, which is the piece of flesh at the far end of the roof of the mouth.

**Chapter 93 — The Recommendation to Come to Prayer, Knowledge, and Similar Acts of Worship with Tranquility and Dignity**

Allah the Exalted said: {«And whoever venerates the sacred rites of Allah, indeed that is from the piety of hearts»} [Al-Ḥajj: 32].

**703.** On the authority of Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — say: «When the prayer is established, do not come to it rushing; come to it walking, and upon you be tranquility. What you catch up with, pray; and what you miss, complete.» Agreed upon. Muslim added in one of his narrations: «For indeed, when one of you intends the prayer, he is in a state of prayer.»

**704.** On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās — may Allah be pleased with them both — that he departed with the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — on the Day of ʿArafah, and he heard behind him severe shouting, striking, and the sound of camels. So he gestured to them with his whip and said: «O people, upon you be tranquility, for indeed righteousness is not in haste.» Narrated by al-Bukhārī, and Muslim narrated part of it. «Al-Birr» means: obedience. And «al-īḍāʿ» — with a ḍād (pointed) preceded by a yāʾ and a kasrah on the hamzah — means: haste.

**Chapter 94 — Honoring the Guest**

Allah the Exalted said: {«Has the story of the honored guests of Abraham reached you? When they entered upon him and said: Peace. He said: Peace, a people unknown. Then he went quietly to his family and brought a fat calf. And he placed it before them, saying: Will you not eat?»} [Al-Dhāriyāt: 24–27]. And He the Exalted said: {«And his people came to him»}
