- Root: ع و ذ (ʿ-w-dh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Seeking refuge, protection, and clinging to a sanctuary
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of entreating divine protection against evil, both corporeal and spiritual
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in the sense of defensive sheltering; metaphorical when applied to the soul's recourse to God
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The explanatory conjunction linking parallel divine attributes without altering the syntactic case
chapters.translation:
**1014** — On the authority of ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir, may God be pleased with him: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «Have you not seen the verses revealed this night, the like of which have never been seen? {Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the Dawn} and {Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of Mankind}». Narrated by Muslim.

**1015** — On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to seek refuge from the jinn and from the evil eye of man, until the two refuge-seeking chapters (al-Muʿawwidhatān) were revealed. When they were revealed, he adhered to them and abandoned all else. Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A good (ḥasan) hadith."

**1016** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «There is a chapter of the Qur'an of thirty verses which interceded for a man until he was forgiven — it is: {Blessed is He in Whose Hand is the Sovereignty}». Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A good (ḥasan) hadith." In the narration of Abū Dāwūd: «It will intercede».

**1017** — On the authority of Abū Masʿūd al-Badrī, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: «Whoever recites the two verses at the end of Sūrat al-Baqarah in a night, they will suffice him». Agreed upon. It was said: They sufficed him against the disliked things of that night; and it was said: They sufficed him from the night prayer.

**1018** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «Do not make your houses graves; indeed, the devil flees from a house in which Sūrat al-Baqarah is recited». Narrated by Muslim.

**1019** — On the authority of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «O Abā al-Mundhir, do you know which verse of the Book of God is greatest with you?» I said: {God — there is no deity but Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting}. He struck my chest and said: «May knowledge be delightful to you, O Abā al-Mundhir». Narrated by Muslim.

**1020** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entrusted me with guarding the zakāh of Ramadan. A visitor came to me and began scooping up from the food. I seized him and said: I shall surely take you to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: I am in need, and I have dependents, and I am in severe want. So I released him. When morning came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «O Abā Hurayrah, what did your captive do last night?» I said: O Messenger of God, he complained of need and dependents, so I had mercy on him and set him free. He said: «Indeed, he lied to you, and he will return». So I knew he would return, because of the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I lay in wait for him, and he came scooping up from the food. I said: I shall surely take you to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Leave me, for I am in need, and I have dependents — I shall not return. So I had mercy on him and set him free. When morning came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: «O Abā Hurayrah, what did your captive do last night?» I said: O Messenger of God, he complained of need and dependents, so I had mercy on him and set him free. He said: «Indeed, he lied to you, and he will return». So I lay in wait for him a third time, and he came scooping up from the food. I seized him and said: I shall surely take you to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace — and this is the third time, while you claim you will not return! He said: Leave me, for I shall teach you words by which God will benefit you. I said: What are they? He said: When you go to your bed, recite the Āyat al-Kursī, for there will not cease to be over you a protector from God, and no devil will approach you until morning. So I set him free. When morning came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: «What did your captive do last night?» I said: O Messenger of God, he claimed he would teach me words by which God would benefit me, so I set him free. He said: «What are they?» I said: He told me: When you go to your bed, recite the Āyat al-Kursī from its beginning until you complete the verse: {God — there is no deity but Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting}. And he said to me: There will not cease to be over you a protector from God, and no devil will approach you until morning. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «Indeed, he spoke the truth to you, though he is a liar. Do you know whom you have been addressing for three nights, O Abā Hurayrah?» I said: No. He said: «That was a devil». Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

**1021** — On the authority of Abū al-Dardāʾ, may God be pleased with him: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «Whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Sūrat al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjāl». In another narration: «From the end of Sūrat al-Kahf». Both narrated by Muslim.

**1022** — On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both: While Gabriel, peace be upon him, was sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he heard a creaking sound from above him. He raised his head and said: This is a gate of heaven opened today, which has never been opened before except today. An angel descended from it, and he said: This is an angel who has descended to the earth, who has never descended before except today. He gave the greeting and said: Rejoice in two lights given to you, which no prophet before you was given: the Opening of the Book (Fātiḥat al-Kitāb) and the closing verses of Sūrat al-Baqarah. You will not recite a single letter of them except that you will be given it. Narrated by Muslim. «Al-Naqīḍ» means: the sound.

**§ 184 — Chapter on the Recommendation of Gathering for Recitation**

**1023** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «No people gather in a house of the houses of God, reciting the Book of God and studying it among themselves, except that tranquility descends upon them, mercy envelops them, the angels surround them, and God mentions them among those with Him». Narrated by Muslim.

**§ 185 — Chapter on the Virtue of Ablution**

God the Exalted has said: {O you who believe, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces} up to His saying: {God does not intend to place upon you any hardship, but He intends to purify you and to complete His favor upon you, that you may be grateful} [al-Māʾidah: 6].

**1024** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: «Indeed, my community will be called on the Day of Resurrection with radiant foreheads (ghurr) and bright limbs (muḥajjalīn) from the traces of ablution. So whoever among you is able to lengthen his radiance, let him do so». Agreed upon.

**1025** — On his authority, he said: I heard my intimate friend, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: «The adornment of the believer reaches where the ablution reaches». Narrated by Muslim.

**1026** — On the authority of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «Whoever performs ablution and perfects the ablution, his sins come forth from his body until they come out from beneath his fingernails». Narrated by Muslim.

**1027** — On his authority, he said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution like this ablution of mine.

chapters.title_en: Section 94 — The Virtue of Ablution (Wuḍūʾ) and the Call to Prayer (Adhān)
chapters.arabic_text:
ثم
# قال: «من توضأ هكذا، غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه، وكانت صلاته ومشيه إلى

المسجد نافلة». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1028 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«إذا توضأ العبد المسلم - أو المؤمن - فغسل وجهه، خرج من وجهه كل خطيئة نظر

إليها بعينيه مع الماء، أو مع آخر قطر الماء، فإذا غسل يديه، خرج من يديه

كل خطيئة كان بطشتها يداه مع الماء، أو مع آخر قطر الماء، فإذا غسل رجليه،

خرجت كل خطيئة مشتها رجلاه مع الماء، أو  مع آخر قطر الماء، حتى يخرج نقيا

من الذنوب». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1029 - 
# وعنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أتى المقبرة، فقال: «السلام

عليكم دار قوم مؤمنين، وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون، وددت أنا قد رأينا

إخواننا» قالوا: أولسنا إخوانك يا رسول الله؟ قال: «أنتم أصحابي، وإخواننا

الذين لم يأتوا بعد» قالوا: كيف تعرف من لم يأت بعد من أمتك يا رسول الله؟

فقال: «أرأيت لو أن رجلا له خيل غر محجلة بين ظهري خيل دهم (1) بهم (2)،

ألا يعرف خيله؟» قالوا: بلى يا رسول الله، قال: «فإنهم يأتون غرا محجلين من

الوضوء، وأنا فرطهم على الحوض». رواه مسلم. (3)

| 1030 - 
# وعنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «ألا أدلكم على ما يمحو

الله به الخطايا، ويرفع به الدرجات؟» قالوا: بلى يا رسول الله، قال: «إسباغ

الوضوء على المكاره، وكثرة الخطا إلى المساجد، وانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة؛

فذلكم الرباط؛ فذلكم الرباط». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1031 - 
# وعن أبي مالك الأشعري - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم: «الطهور شطر الإيمان». رواه مسلم. (1)
# وقد سبق بطوله في باب الصبر، وفي الباب حديث عمرو بن عبسة - رضي الله عنه

- السابق (2) في آخر باب الرجاء، وهو حديث عظيم؛ مشتمل على جمل من الخيرات.

| 1032 - 
# وعن عمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

قال: «ما منكم من أحد يتوضأ فيبلغ - أو فيسبغ - الوضوء، ثم يقول: أشهد أن

لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله؛ إلا فتحت له

أبواب الجنة الثمانية يدخل من أيها شاء». رواه مسلم. (1)
# وزاد الترمذي: «اللهم اجعلني من التوابين، واجعلني من المتطهرين».

$ 186 - باب فضل الأذان

| 1033 - 
# عن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«لو يعلم الناس ما في النداء والصف الأول، ثم لم يجدوا إلا أن يستهموا عليه

لاستهموا عليه، ولو يعلمون ما في التهجير لاستبقوا إليه، ولو  يعلمون ما في

العتمة (1) والصبح لأتوهما ولو حبوا». متفق عليه. (2)
# «الاستهام»: الاقتراع، و «التهجير»: التبكير إلى الصلاة.

| 1034 - 
# وعن معاوية - رضي الله عنه - قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

يقول: «المؤذنون أطول الناس أعناقا يوم القيامة». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1035 - 
# وعن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمان بن أبي صعصعة: أن أبا سعيد الخدري - رضي

الله عنه - قال له: «إني أراك تحب الغنم والبادية فإذا كنت في غنمك - أو

باديتك - فأذنت للصلاة، فارفع صوتك بالنداء، فإنه لا يسمع مدى صوت المؤذن

جن، ولا إنس، ولا شيء، إلا شهد له يوم القيامة» قال أبو سعيد: سمعته من

رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم. رواه البخاري. (1)

| 1036 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «إذا نودي بالصلاة، أدبر الشيطان، وله ضراط حتى لا يسمع التأذين،

فإذا قضي النداء أقبل، حتى إذا ثوب للصلاة أدبر، حتى إذا قضي التثويب أقبل،

حتى يخطر بين المرء ونفسه، يقول: اذكر كذا واذكر كذا - لما لم يذكر من قبل

- حتى يظل الرجل ما يدري كم صلى». متفق عليه. (1)
# «التثويب»: الإقامة.

| 1037 - 
# وعن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما: أنه سمع رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - يقول: «إذا سمعتم النداء فقولوا مثل ما يقول، ثم صلوا

علي؛ فإنه من صلى علي صلاة صلى الله عليه بها عشرا، ثم سلوا الله لي

الوسيلة؛ فإنها منزلة في الجنة لا تنبغي إلا لعبد من عباد الله وأرجو أن

أكون أنا هو، فمن سأل لي الوسيلة حلت له الشفاعة». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1038 - 
# وعن أبي سعيد الخدري - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم

- قال: «إذا سمعتم النداء، فقولوا كما يقول المؤذن». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1039 - 
# وعن جابر - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «من

قال حين يسمع النداء: اللهم رب هذه الدعوة التامة، والصلاة القائمة، آت

محمدا الوسيلة، والفضيلة، وابعثه مقاما محمودا الذي وعدته،  حلت له شفاعتي

يوم القيامة». رواه البخاري. (1)

| 1040 - 
# وعن سعد بن أبي وقاص - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

أنه قال: «من قال حين يسمع المؤذن: أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك

له، وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله، رضيت بالله ربا، وبمحمد رسولا، وبالإسلام دينا،

غفر له ذنبه». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1041 - 
# وعن أنس - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«الدعاء لا يرد بين الأذان والإقامة». رواه أبو داود والترمذي، (1) وقال:

«حديث حسن».

$ 187 - باب فضل الصلوات
# قال الله تعالى: {إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر} [العنكبوت: 45].
#

| 1042 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - يقول: «أرأيتم لو أن نهرا بباب أحدكم يغتسل منه كل يوم خمس مرات، هل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Purity, cleanliness; removal of filth (najāsah) and impurity (khabath).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual purification (ṭahārah) as a spiritual cleansing from sins, not merely physical — a prerequisite for valid prayer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical washing; metaphorical (majāz) for the expiation of sins, as water is the vehicle of divine forgiveness.
- Root: ن-د-و (n-d-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To call out, proclaim aloud; the act of summoning (nidāʾ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The adhān as a public declaration of divine unity (tawḥīd) and the summons to communal worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the vocal call; metaphorical for the spiritual summons to salvation.
- Root: غ-س-ل (gh-s-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Washing, cleansing by water; thorough ablution.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The physical act symbolizing the effacement of sin (takfīr al-khaṭāyā).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the limbs; metaphorical for the soul's purification.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (Jumlat al-Sharṭ) — The protasis (idhā) introduces a condition whose apodosis (jawāb) follows with a result, often marked by fa- or a nominal sentence, as in «إذا توضأ... خرج» (When he performs ablution... there emerges).
chapters.translation:
Then the author (Imam al-Nawawi) said:

**1028.** On the authority of Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — that the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «When the Muslim servant — or the believer — performs ablution and washes his face, every sin he looked upon with his eyes exits from his face with the water, or with the last drop of water. When he washes his hands, every sin his hands grasped exits from his hands with the water, or with the last drop of water. When he washes his feet, every sin his feet walked toward exits with the water, or with the last drop of water, until he emerges pure of sins.» Narrated by Muslim.

**1029.** On his authority (Abū Hurayrah): That the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — came to the cemetery and said: «Peace be upon you, O abode of believing people. Indeed, we, Allah willing, shall join you. I wish we had seen our brothers.» They said: "Are we not your brothers, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: «You are my companions, and our brothers are those who have not yet come.» They said: "How will you recognize those of your community who have not yet come, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: «Consider: if a man had horses with white blazes and white-stockinged legs among dark black horses, would he not recognize his own horses?» They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: «Indeed, they will come with white blazes and white-stockinged legs from the traces of ablution, and I will precede them to the Basin (al-Ḥawḍ).» Narrated by Muslim.

**1030.** On his authority: That the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Shall I not guide you to that by which Allah erases sins and elevates ranks?» They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: «Perfecting the ablution despite hardships, taking many steps to the mosques, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer — that is the ribāṭ (the fortress-like vigilance); that is the ribāṭ.» Narrated by Muslim.

**1031.** On the authority of Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Purification (al-ṭuhūr) is half of faith.» Narrated by Muslim. This has already been mentioned in full in the Chapter on Patience (Ṣabr), and in that chapter is the hadith of ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah — may Allah be pleased with him — previously cited at the end of the Chapter on Hope (Rajāʾ); it is a momentous hadith, encompassing numerous virtues.

**1032.** On the authority of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — may Allah be pleased with him — from the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — who said: «There is none among you who performs ablution, perfecting it — or completing it — then says: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger," except that the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him, and he enters through whichever he wishes.» Narrated by Muslim. Al-Tirmidhī added: «O Allah, make me among the oft-repentant, and make me among those who purify themselves.»

**§ 186 — Chapter on the Virtue of the Call to Prayer (Adhān)**

**1033.** On the authority of Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him: That the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «If people knew what is in the call (to prayer) and the first row, and found no way but to cast lots for it, they would cast lots. If they knew what is in arriving early (al-tahjīr), they would race to it. If they knew what is in the ʿAtamah (night prayer) and the Dawn prayer, they would come to them even if crawling.» Agreed upon (by al-Bukhārī and Muslim). «Al-istihām» means casting lots, and «al-tahjīr» means hastening early to the prayer.

**1034.** On the authority of Muʿāwiyah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — say: «The muʾadhdhins (callers to prayer) will have the longest necks on the Day of Resurrection.» Narrated by Muslim.

**1035.** On the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ṣaʿṣaʿah: That Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī — may Allah be pleased with him — said to him: «I see that you love sheep and the desert. When you are among your sheep — or in your desert — and you give the call to prayer, raise your voice with the call, for no jinn, human, or anything within the range of the muʾadhdhin's voice will hear it except that it will bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection.» Abū Saʿīd said: I heard this from the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

**1036.** On the authority of Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «When the call to prayer is made, Satan turns away in flight, passing wind so as not to hear the adhān. When the call is finished, he returns. When the iqāmah (second call) is made, he turns away again. When it is finished, he returns and whispers between a man and his own self, saying: "Remember such-and-such, remember such-and-such" — of what he had not remembered — until the man remains not knowing how much he has prayed.» Agreed upon. «Al-tathwīb» means the iqāmah.

**1037.** On the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ — may Allah be pleased with them both: That he heard the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — say: «When you hear the call, say what he says, then send blessings upon me; for whoever sends one blessing upon me, Allah sends ten blessings upon him. Then ask Allah for al-wasīlah for me; for it is a station in Paradise befitting none but one of Allah's servants, and I hope that I am that one. Whoever asks for al-wasīlah for me, my intercession becomes permissible for him.» Narrated by Muslim.

**1038.** On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī — may Allah be pleased with him: That the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «When you hear the call, say as the muʾadhdhin says.» Agreed upon.

**1039.** On the authority of Jābir — may Allah be pleased with him: That the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «Whoever says upon hearing the call: "O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, grant Muḥammad the wasīlah and the excellence, and raise him to the praiseworthy station (maqām maḥmūd) which You have promised him," my intercession becomes permissible for him on the Day of Resurrection.» Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

**1040.** On the authority of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ — may Allah be pleased with him — from the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — that he said: «Whoever says upon hearing the muʾadhdhin: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. I am content with Allah as Lord, with Muḥammad as Messenger, and with Islam as religion," his sin is forgiven.» Narrated by Muslim.

**1041.** On the authority of Anas — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: «The supplication is not rejected between the adhān and the iqāmah.» Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A good (ḥasan) hadith."

**§ 187 — Chapter on the Virtue of the Prayers**

Allah the Exalted says: {«Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing»} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 45].

**1042.** On the authority of Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — say: «Consider: if a river flowed at the door of one of you, and he bathed in it five times every day, would...»

chapters.title_en: Section 95 — The Virtue of the Five Prayers, Friday to Friday, and the Prayer of Fajr and ʿAṣr

يبقى من درنه (1)
# شيء؟» قالوا: لا يبقى من درنه شيء، قال: «فذلك مثل الصلوات الخمس يمحو

الله بهن الخطايا». متفق عليه. (2)

| 1043 - 
# وعن جابر - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«مثل الصلوات الخمس كمثل نهر جار غمر على باب أحدكم يغتسل منه كل يوم خمس

مرات». رواه مسلم. (1)
# «الغمر» بفتح الغين المعجمة: الكثير.

| 1044 - 
# وعن ابن مسعود - رضي الله عنه: أن رجلا أصاب من امرأة قبلة، فأتى النبي -

صلى الله عليه وسلم - فأخبره فأنزل الله تعالى: {أقم الصلاة طرفي النهار

وزلفا من الليل، إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات} [هود: 114] فقال الرجل ألي هذا؟

قال: «لجميع أمتي كلهم». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1045 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«الصلوات الخمس، والجمعة إلى الجمعة، كفارة لما بينهن، ما لم تغش الكبائر».

رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1046 - 
# وعن عثمان بن عفان - رضي الله عنه - قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - يقول: «ما من امرئ مسلم تحضره صلاة مكتوبة فيحسن وضوءها؛ وخشوعها،

وركوعها، إلا كانت كفارة لما قبلها من الذنوب ما لم تؤت كبيرة، وذلك الدهر

كله». رواه  مسلم. (1)

$ 188 - باب فضل صلاة الصبح والعصر

| 1047 - 
# عن أبي موسى - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«من صلى البردين دخل الجنة». متفق عليه. (1)
# «البردان»: الصبح والعصر.

| 1048 - 
# وعن أبي زهير عمارة بن رؤيبة - رضي الله عنه - قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - يقول: «لن يلج النار أحد صلى قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها»

يعني: الفجر والعصر. رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1049 - 
# وعن جندب بن سفيان - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «من صلى الصبح فهو في ذمة الله، فانظر يا ابن آدم، لا يطلبنك الله من

ذمته بشيء». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1050 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة بالليل، وملائكة بالنهار، ويجتمعون في صلاة

الصبح وصلاة العصر، ثم يعرج الذين باتوا فيكم، فيسألهم الله - وهو أعلم بهم

- كيف تركتم عبادي؟ فيقولون: تركناهم وهم يصلون، وأتيناهم وهم يصلون». متفق

عليه. (1)

| 1051 - 
# وعن جرير بن عبد الله البجلي - رضي الله عنه - قال: كنا عند النبي - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - فنظر إلى القمر ليلة البدر، فقال: «إنكم سترون ربكم كما

ترون هذا القمر، لا تضامون في رؤيته، فإن استطعتم أن لا تغلبوا على صلاة

قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها، فافعلوا». متفق عليه. (1)
# وفي رواية: «فنظر إلى القمر ليلة أربع عشرة».

| 1052 - 
# وعن بريدة - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«من ترك صلاة العصر فقد حبط عمله». رواه البخاري. (1)

$ 189 - باب فضل المشي إلى المساجد

| 1053 - 
# عن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «من

غدا إلى المسجد أو راح، أعد الله له في الجنة نزلا كلما غدا أو راح». متفق

عليه. (1)

| 1054 - 
# وعنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «من تطهر في بيته، ثم مضى

إلى بيت من بيوت الله، ليقضي فريضة من فرائض الله، كانت خطواته، إحداها تحط

خطيئة، والأخرى  ترفع درجة». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1055 - 
# وعن أبي بن كعب - رضي الله عنه - قال: كان رجل من الأنصار لا أعلم أحدا

أبعد من المسجد منه، وكانت لا تخطئه صلاة، فقيل له: لو اشتريت حمارا لتركبه

في الظلماء وفي الرمضاء (1)، قال: ما يسرني أن منزلي إلى جنب المسجد، إني

أريد أن يكتب لي ممشاي إلى المسجد، ورجوعي إذا رجعت إلى أهلي. فقال رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «قد جمع الله لك ذلك كله». رواه مسلم. (2)

| 1056 - 
# وعن جابر - رضي الله عنه - قال: خلت البقاع حول المسجد، فأراد بنو سلمة

أن ينتقلوا قرب المسجد، فبلغ ذلك النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال لهم:

«بلغني أنكم تريدون أن تنتقلوا قرب المسجد؟» قالوا: نعم، يا رسول الله، قد

أردنا ذلك. فقال: «بني سلمة دياركم تكتب آثاركم، دياركم تكتب آثاركم (1)»

فقالوا: ما يسرنا أنا كنا تحولنا. رواه مسلم، وروى البخاري معناه من رواية

أنس. (2)

| 1057 - 
# وعن أبي موسى - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«إن أعظم الناس أجرا في الصلاة أبعدهم إليها ممشى، فأبعدهم، والذي ينتظر

الصلاة حتى يصليها مع الإمام أعظم أجرا من الذي يصليها ثم ينام». متفق

عليه. (1)

| 1058 - 
# وعن بريدة - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «بشروا

المشائين في الظلم إلى المساجد بالنور التام يوم القيامة». رواه أبو داود

والترمذي. (1)

| 1059 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«ألا أدلكم على ما يمحو الله به الخطايا، ويرفع به الدرجات؟» قالوا: بلى يا

رسول الله؟ قال: «إسباغ الوضوء على المكاره، وكثرة الخطا إلى المساجد،

وانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة، فذلكم الرباط، فذلكم الرباط». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1060 - 
# وعن أبي سعيد الخدري - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

قال: «إذا رأيتم الرجل يعتاد المساجد فاشهدوا له بالإيمان، قال الله - عز

وجل: {إنما يعمر مساجد الله من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر} الآية». رواه

الترمذي، وقال: «حديث حسن». (1)

$ 190  - باب فضل انتظار الصلاة

| 1061 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-س-ل (gh-s-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Washing, cleansing by water; removal of physical impurity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual purification (ghusl) as a metaphor for spiritual expiation of sins.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal washing (ḥaqīqah) vs. metaphorical cleansing of sins (majāz).
- Root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Covering, veiling; expiation (kaffārah) as covering over sins.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Atonement that conceals the effect of minor sins.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal covering vs. theological covering of transgressions.
- Root: ح-ب-ط (ḥ-b-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To become void, nullified; a deed rendered fruitless.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Annulment of good works due to grave sin.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal falling to the ground vs. metaphorical loss of reward.
- Root: ع-م-ر (ʿ-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To inhabit, cultivate, frequent a place.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual flourishing of mosques through worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal building vs. metaphorical inhabitation by devotion.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The protasis (e.g., 'whoever prays') establishes a universal condition, with the apodosis as its necessary consequence, requiring precise particle selection (man, mā) for generality.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The five prayers, and Friday to Friday, are an expiation (kaffārah) for what is between them, so long as one avoids the grave sins (kabā'ir)."

From Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do you not see that if a river flowed at the door of one of you, and he bathed in it five times daily, would any of his filth remain?" They said: "No filth would remain." He said: "Such is the likeness of the five prayers — Allah erases by them the transgressions (khaṭāyā)." Agreed upon.

From Jābir (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The likeness of the five prayers is that of a flowing, abundant river (ghamar) at the door of one of you, in which he bathes five times every day." Narrated by Muslim. The word 'ghamar' (with a fatḥah on the ghayn) means: abundant.

From Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him): A man kissed a woman, then came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and informed him. So Allah the Exalted revealed: {«أقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل، إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات»} [Hūd: 114] — "Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds." The man said: "Is this for me alone?" He said: "For all of my nation, all of them." Agreed upon.

From Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The five prayers, and Friday to Friday, are an expiation (kaffārah) for what is between them, so long as one does not commit the grave sins (kabā'ir)." Narrated by Muslim.

From ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān (may Allah be pleased with him): I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "No Muslim man to whom an obligatory prayer (ṣalāh maktūbah) comes, and he perfects its ablution (wuḍū'), its humility (khushūʿ), and its bowing (rukūʿ), except that it becomes an expiation (kaffārah) for the sins preceding it, so long as he does not commit a grave sin (kabīrah) — and that applies for all time." Narrated by Muslim.

Section 188 — The Virtue of the Fajr and ʿAṣr Prayers

From Abū Mūsā (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever prays the two cool prayers (al-bardayn) will enter Paradise." Agreed upon. The two cool prayers (al-bardān) are: Fajr and ʿAṣr.

From Abū Zuhayr ʿUmārah ibn Ru'aybah (may Allah be pleased with him): I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "No one will enter the Fire who prayed before the rising of the sun and before its setting" — meaning: Fajr and ʿAṣr. Narrated by Muslim.

From Jundub ibn Sufyān (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever prays the Fajr prayer is under the protection (dhimmah) of Allah. So beware, O son of Adam, lest Allah seek you out for something regarding His protection." Narrated by Muslim.

From Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Angels of the night and angels of the day take turns among you, and they gather at the Fajr prayer and the ʿAṣr prayer. Then those who had spent the night among you ascend, and Allah — Who knows them best — asks them: 'How did you leave My servants?' They say: 'We left them praying, and we came to them praying.'" Agreed upon.

From Jarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Bajalī (may Allah be pleased with him): We were with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon (badr), and said: "You will surely see your Lord as you see this moon — you will not be wronged (lā tuḍāmmūn) in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome regarding the prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so." Agreed upon. In another narration: "He looked at the moon on the night of the fourteenth."

From Buraydah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever abandons the ʿAṣr prayer, his deeds have been rendered void (ḥabiṭa ʿamaluhu)." Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

Section 189 — The Virtue of Walking to the Mosques

From Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever goes forth to the mosque in the morning or returns in the evening, Allah has prepared for him a hospitality (nuzul) in Paradise every time he goes forth or returns." Agreed upon.

From him (Abū Hurayrah): The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever purifies himself in his house, then proceeds to one of the houses of Allah to fulfill an obligation (farīḍah) from the obligations of Allah, then his steps — one of them erases a sin (khaṭī'ah), and the other raises a degree (darajah)." Narrated by Muslim.

From Ubayy ibn Kaʿb (may Allah be pleased with him): There was a man of the Anṣār — I know of no one whose house was farther from the mosque than his — and no prayer ever escaped him. It was said to him: "Why not buy a donkey to ride in the darkness and in the scorching heat (al-ramḍā')?" He said: "I would not be pleased that my house were adjacent to the mosque. I want my walking to the mosque and my return to my family to be recorded for me." So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Allah has gathered all of that for you." Narrated by Muslim.

From Jābir (may Allah be pleased with him): The lands around the mosque became vacant, and the Banū Salamah wanted to move closer to the mosque. This reached the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and he said to them: "It has reached me that you intend to move closer to the mosque?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, we have intended that." He said: "O Banū Salamah, keep your dwellings, for your footsteps are recorded — keep your dwellings, for your footsteps are recorded." They said: "We would not be pleased that we had moved." Narrated by Muslim, and al-Bukhārī narrated its meaning from Anas.

From Abū Mūsā (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The greatest of people in reward for the prayer is the one who walks the farthest to it, and the farthest. And the one who waits for the prayer until he prays it with the Imām has a greater reward than the one who prays it and then sleeps." Agreed upon.

From Buraydah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Give glad tidings to those who walk in the darkness to the mosques of complete light (nūr tāmm) on the Day of Resurrection." Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī.

From Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Shall I not guide you to that by which Allah erases sins (khaṭāyā) and raises degrees (darajāt)?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Perfecting the ablution (isbāgh al-wuḍū') despite hardships (makārih), and taking many steps to the mosques, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer — that is the ribāṭ (fortification), that is the ribāṭ." Narrated by Muslim.

From Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "If you see a man frequenting the mosques, then bear witness for him of faith (īmān). Allah the Exalted said: {«إنما يعمر مساجد الله من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر»} — 'Indeed, the mosques of Allah are only inhabited by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day' — the verse." Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A ḥasan ḥadīth."

Section 190 — The Virtue of Waiting for the Prayer

From Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said:
