chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ج-ل (ʿ-j-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Swiftness, haste, alacrity in commencing an action; the opposite of delay (taʾkhīr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the divine attribution, it denotes God's preference for the servant's eager compliance with the revealed command, not an anthropomorphic urgency.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in human action; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to God, signifying approval and reward.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) — The protasis (idhā) governs the apodosis (fa-qad afṭara), establishing a causal-legal nexus.
chapters.translation:
**1235** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «God, Mighty and Majestic, said: The most beloved of My servants to Me are those who hasten most to break the fast.» Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A ḥasan (good) ḥadīth."

**1236** — On the authority of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «When the night approaches from this direction, and the day departs from this direction, and the sun has set, then the fasting person has broken his fast.» Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

**1237** — On the authority of Abū Ibrāhīm ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā (may God be pleased with them both), who said: We traveled with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) while he was fasting. When the sun set, he said to one of the people: «O so-and-so, dismount and mix for us (ajdih).» He said: O Messenger of God, if only you would wait until evening? He said: «Dismount and mix for us (ajdih).» He said: But daylight remains upon you. He said: «Dismount and mix for us (ajdih).» He said: So he dismounted and mixed for them, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) drank. Then he said: «When you see the night approaching from this direction, then the fasting person has broken his fast» — and he pointed with his hand toward the east. Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

His saying «ajdih» — with jīm, then dāl, then ḥāʾ, both unpointed — means: mix the sawīq (barley porridge) with water.

**1238** — On the authority of Salmān ibn ʿĀmir al-Ḍabbī, the Companion (may God be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: «When one of you breaks his fast, let him break it with dates; if he finds none, then let him break it with water, for it is purifying.» Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ (good and sound) ḥadīth."

**1239** — On the authority of Anas (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to break his fast before praying with fresh dates; if fresh dates were not available, then with dried dates; if dried dates were not available, he would take a few sips of water. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A ḥasan (good) ḥadīth."

**§ 223 — Chapter on the Command for the Fasting Person to Guard His Tongue and Limbs from Transgressions, Obscenity, and the Like**

**1240** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «When it is the day of fasting for one of you, let him not utter obscenity (yarfuth) nor raise his voice in clamor (yaṣkhab). If anyone reviles him or fights him, let him say: I am fasting.» Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

**1241** — On his authority (Abū Hurayrah), who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Whoever does not abandon false speech (qawl al-zūr) and acting upon it, then God has no need for him to abandon his food and drink.» Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

**§ 224 — Chapter on Various Matters Pertaining to Fasting**

**1242** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: «If one of you forgets and eats or drinks, let him complete his fast, for it is only God who has fed him and given him to drink.» Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

**1243** — On the authority of Laqīṭ ibn Ṣabirah (may God be pleased with him), who said: I said: O Messenger of God, inform me about the ablution (wuḍūʾ). He said: «Perform the ablution thoroughly, and run water between the fingers, and exaggerate in snuffing water into the nose (istinshāq), unless you are fasting.» Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ (good and sound) ḥadīth."

**1244** — On the authority of ʿĀʾishah (may God be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) would be overtaken by dawn while in a state of major impurity (junub) from his family, then he would bathe and fast. Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

**1245** — On the authority of ʿĀʾishah and Umm Salamah (may God be pleased with them both), who both said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) would wake at dawn in a state of major impurity (junub) not from a wet dream, then he would fast. Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

**§ 225 — Chapter on the Virtue of Fasting in Muḥarram, Shaʿbān, and the Sacred Months**

**1246** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «The most excellent fast after Ramaḍān is the month of God, al-Muḥarram; and the most excellent prayer after the obligatory prayer is the night prayer.» Narrated by Muslim.

**1247** — On the authority of ʿĀʾishah (may God be pleased with her), who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) did not fast in any month more than in Shaʿbān, for he used to fast all of Shaʿbān. In another narration: He used to fast Shaʿbān except for a little. Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

**1248** — On the authority of Mujībah al-Bāhilīyah, from her father or her uncle: that he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), then departed, then came to him after a year — and his condition and appearance had changed — and said: O Messenger of God, do you not recognize me? He said: «And who are you?» He said: I am the Bāhilī who came to you last year. He said: «What has changed you, for you were of handsome appearance!» He said: I have not eaten any food since I left you except at night. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «You have tormented yourself!» Then he said: «Fast the month of patience (ṣabr), and one day from every month.» He said: Increase me, for I have strength. He said: «Fast two days.» He said: Increase me. He said: «Fast three days.» He said: Increase me. He said: «Fast from the sacred months and refrain; fast from the sacred months and refrain; fast from the sacred months and refrain» — and he gestured with his three fingers, clasping them together, then releasing them. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd. And «the month of patience (ṣabr)» is Ramaḍān.

**§ 226 — Chapter on the Virtue of Fasting and Other Deeds in the First Ten Days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah**

**1249** — On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to God than these days» — meaning the ten days (of Dhū al-Ḥijjah). They said: O Messenger of God, not even striving in the path of God (jihād)? He said: «Not even striving in the path of God, except a man who goes out with his life and his wealth, and returns not with any of that.» Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

**§ 227 — Chapter on the Virtue of Fasting the Day of ʿArafah, ʿĀshūrāʾ, and Tāsūʿāʾ**

**1250** — On the authority of Abū Qatādah (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked about fasting the Day of ʿArafah, and he said: «It expiates the past year and the coming year.» Narrated by Muslim.

**1251** — On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both): that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) fasted the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ and commanded fasting it. Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

**1252** — On the authority of Abū Qatādah (may God be pleased with him): that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked about fasting the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, and he said: «It expiates the past year.» Narrated by Muslim.

**1253** — On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «If I remain alive until the next year, I will surely fast the ninth (Tāsūʿāʾ).» Narrated by Muslim.

**§ 228 — Chapter on the Recommendation of Fasting Six Days of Shawwāl**

**1254** — On the authority of Abū Ayyūb (may God be pleased with him): that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said:
