1614 — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, who said: «Avoid the seven destructive sins!» They said: O Messenger of God, what are they? He said: «Associating partners with God (shirk), sorcery, killing a soul that God has forbidden except by right, consuming usury (ribā), consuming the wealth of the orphan, turning one's back on the day of advance (battle), and slandering chaste, believing, heedless women.» Agreed upon. «Destructive sins» (al-mūbiqāt) means: the things that cause perdition.

Section 287 — Chapter on the Aggravated Prohibition of Usury (Ribā)

God Almighty said: {«Those who consume usury will not stand except as one stands whom Satan has struck with madness by touch. That is because they said: Trade is like usury. But God has permitted trade and forbidden usury. So whoever receives an admonition from his Lord and desists—his past is forgiven, and his affair rests with God. And whoever returns—those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein eternally. God destroys usury and increases charity»} — up to His saying, exalted: {«O you who believe, fear God and abandon what remains of usury»} [Al-Baqarah: 275–278]. As for the hadiths, they are numerous in the authentic collections and well-known; among them is the hadith of Abū Hurayrah mentioned in the preceding chapter.

1615 — On the authority of Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, cursed the consumer of usury and its payer. Narrated by Muslim. Al-Tirmidhī and others added: and its two witnesses and its scribe.

Section 288 — Chapter on the Prohibition of Ostentation (Riyāʾ)

God Almighty said: {«And they were not commanded except to worship God, being sincere to Him in religion, as monotheists»} [Al-Bayyinah: 5], and He, exalted, said: {«Do not nullify your charities by reminders of favor and injury, like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people»} [Al-Baqarah: 264], and He, exalted, said: {«They show off to people and do not remember God except a little»} [Al-Nisāʾ: 142].

1616 — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, say: «God Almighty said: I am the most self-sufficient of partners from partnership. Whoever performs a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his partnership.» Narrated by Muslim.

1617 — On his authority, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, say: «The first of people to be judged on the Day of Resurrection is a man who was martyred. He is brought forth, and God makes known to him His blessings, and he recognizes them. He says: What did you do with them? He says: I fought for You until I was martyred. He says: You have lied! Rather, you fought so that it would be said: Brave! And it was said. Then he is commanded, and he is dragged on his face until he is cast into the Fire. And a man who learned knowledge and taught it, and recited the Qurʾān. He is brought forth, and God makes known to him His blessings, and he recognizes them. He says: What did you do with them? He says: I learned knowledge and taught it, and I recited the Qurʾān for You. He says: You have lied! Rather, you learned so that it would be said: Scholar! And you recited the Qurʾān so that it would be said: Reciter! And it was said. Then he is commanded, and he is dragged on his face until he is cast into the Fire. And a man whom God had made wealthy and given from all kinds of wealth. He is brought forth, and God makes known to him His blessings, and he recognizes them. He says: What did you do with them? He says: I left no path that You love that wealth be spent on, except I spent on it for You. He says: You have lied! Rather, you did it so that it would be said: Generous! And it was said. Then he is commanded, and he is dragged on his face until he is cast into the Fire.» Narrated by Muslim. «Brave» (jarīʾ) — with a fatḥah on the jīm, kasrah on the rāʾ, and madd — means: courageous and skillful.

1618 — On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them both: that some people said to him: We enter upon our rulers and say to them the opposite of what we say when we leave them. Ibn ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them both, said: We used to count this as hypocrisy (nifāq) in the time of the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him. Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

1619 — On the authority of Jundub ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sufyān, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, said: «Whoever seeks to be heard, God will make him heard; and whoever shows off, God will expose him.» Agreed upon. Muslim also narrated it from the transmission of Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both. «Seeks to be heard» (sammaʿa) — with a shaddah on the mīm — its meaning is: he displays his deed to people out of ostentation. «God will make him heard» means: He will expose him on the Day of Resurrection. And the meaning of «whoever shows off» (rāʾā) is: whoever displays righteous deeds to people to be magnified in their eyes. «God will expose him» means: He will reveal his inner secret before the heads of creation.

chapters.arabic_text:
| 1620 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «من تعلم علما مما يبتغى به وجه الله - عز وجل - لا يتعلمه إلا ليصيب

به عرضا من الدنيا، لم يجد عرف الجنة يوم القيامة». يعني: ريحها. رواه أبو

داود بإسناد صحيح والأحاديث في الباب كثيرة مشهورة. (1)

$ 289 - باب ما يتوهم أنه رياء وليس هو رياء

| 1621 - 
# وعن أبي ذر - رضي الله عنه - قال: قيل لرسول الله - صلى الله عليه  وسلم:

أرأيت الرجل الذي يعمل العمل من الخير، ويحمده الناس عليه؟ قال: «تلك عاجل

بشرى المؤمن» (1). رواه مسلم. (2)

$ 290 - باب تحريم النظر إلى المرأة الأجنبية والأمرد الحسن لغير حاجة شرعية
# قال الله تعالى: {قل للمؤمنين يغضوا من أبصارهم} [النور: 30]، وقال

تعالى: {إن السمع والبصر والفؤاد كل أولئك كان عنه مسئولا} [الإسراء: 36]،

وقال تعالى: {يعلم خائنة الأعين وما تخفي الصدور} [غافر: 19]، وقال تعالى:

{إن ربك لبالمرصاد} [الفجر: 14].
#

| 1622 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«كتب على ابن آدم نصيبه من الزنا مدرك ذلك لا محالة: العينان زناهما النظر،

والأذنان زناهما الاستماع، واللسان زناه الكلام، واليد زناها البطش، والرجل

زناها الخطا، والقلب يهوى ويتمنى، ويصدق ذلك الفرج أو يكذبه». متفق عليه.

(1) هذا لفظ مسلم، ورواية البخاري مختصرة.

| 1623 - 
# وعن أبي سعيد الخدري - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

قال: «إياكم والجلوس في الطرقات!» قالوا: يا رسول الله، ما لنا من مجالسنا

بد، نتحدث فيها. فقال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «فإذا أبيتم إلا

المجلس، فأعطوا الطريق حقه» قالوا: وما حق الطريق يا رسول الله؟ قال: «غض

البصر، وكف الأذى، ورد السلام، والأمر بالمعروف، والنهي عن المنكر» (1)

متفق عليه. (2)

| 1624 - 
# وعن أبي طلحة زيد بن سهل - رضي الله عنه - قال: كنا قعودا بالأفنية (1)

نتحدث فيها فجاء رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقام علينا، فقال: «ما

لكم ولمجالس الصعدات؟ اجتنبوا مجالس الصعدات». فقلنا: إنما قعدنا لغير ما

بأس، قعدنا نتذاكر، ونتحدث. قال: «إما لا فأدوا حقها: غض البصر، ورد

السلام، وحسن الكلام». رواه مسلم. (2)
# «الصعدات» بضم الصاد والعين: أي الطرقات.

| 1625 - 
# وعن جرير - رضي الله عنه - قال: سألت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

عن نظر الفجأة فقال: «اصرف بصرك». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1626 - 
# وعن أم سلمة رضي الله عنها، قالت: كنت عند رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - وعنده ميمونة، فأقبل ابن أم مكتوم، وذلك بعد أن أمرنا بالحجاب فقال

النبي - صلى  الله عليه وسلم: «احتجبا منه» فقلنا:

| [ص: 457]
# يا رسول الله، أليس هو أعمى! لا يبصرنا، ولا يعرفنا؟ فقال النبي - صلى

الله عليه وسلم: «أفعمياوان أنتما ألستما تبصرانه!؟». رواه أبو داود

والترمذي، (1) وقال: «حديث حسن صحيح».

| 1627 - 
# وعن أبي سعيد - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«لا ينظر الرجل إلى عورة الرجل، ولا المرأة إلى عورة المرأة، ولا يفضي

الرجل إلى الرجل في ثوب واحد (1)، ولا تفضي المرأة إلى المرأة في الثوب

الواحد». رواه مسلم. (2)

$ 291 - باب تحريم الخلوة بالأجنبية
# قال الله تعالى: {وإذا سألتموهن متاعا فاسألوهن من وراء حجاب} [الأحزاب:

53].
#

| 1628 - 
# وعن عقبة بن عامر - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

قال: «إياكم والدخول على النساء!» فقال رجل من الأنصار: أفرأيت الحمو؟ قال:

«الحمو الموت!». متفق عليه. (1)
# «الحمو»: قريب الزوج كأخيه، وابن أخيه، وابن عمه.

| 1629 - 
# وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«لا يخلون أحدكم بامرأة إلا مع ذي محرم». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1630 - 
# وعن بريدة - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«حرمة نساء المجاهدين على القاعدين كحرمة أمهاتهم، ما من رجل من القاعدين

يخلف رجلا من المجاهدين في أهله، فيخونه فيهم إلا وقف له يوم القيامة،

فيأخذ من حسناته ما شاء حتى يرضى» ثم التفت إلينا رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - فقال: «ما ظنكم؟». رواه مسلم. (1)

$ 292 - باب تحريم تشبه الرجال بالنساء وتشبه النساء بالرجال في لباس وحركة وغير ذلك

| 1631 - 
# عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، قال: لعن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

المخنثين من الرجال، والمترجلات من النساء.
# وفي رواية: لعن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - المتشبهين من الرجال

بالنساء، والمتشبهات من النساء بالرجال. رواه البخاري. (1)

| 1632 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: لعن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم

- الرجل يلبس لبسة المرأة، والمرأة تلبس لبسة الرجل. رواه أبو داود بإسناد

صحيح. (1)

| 1633 - 
# وعنه، قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «صنفان من أهل النار لم

أرهما: قوم معهم سياط كأذناب البقر يضربون بها الناس، ونساء كاسيات عاريات

مميلات مائلات، رؤوسهن كأسنمة البخت المائلة لا يدخلن الجنة، ولا يجدن

ريحها، وإن ريحها ليوجد من مسيرة كذا وكذا». (1). رواه مسلم. (2)
# معنى «كاسيات» أي: من نعمة الله «عاريات» من شكرها. وقيل معناه: تستر بعض

بدنها، وتكشف بعضه إظهارا لجمالها ونحوه. وقيل: تلبس ثوبا رقيقا يصف لون

| [ص: 459]
# بدنها. ومعنى «مائلات»، قيل: عن طاعة الله وما يلزمهن حفظه «مميلات» أي:

يعلمن غيرهن فعلهن المذموم. وقيل: مائلات يمشين متبخترات، مميلات لأكتافهن،

- Root: غ-ض-ي (ghaḍa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To lower, to cast down, to restrain (the gaze); core sense of constricting and withholding.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic usage, "ghaḍḍ al-baṣar" denotes the moral discipline of averting the gaze from what is unlawful—a command of the heart enacted by the limb.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in reference to the physical eye; metaphorical (majāz) in extending to the ear, tongue, hand, and foot as "organs of sight" in moral accountability.
- Root: ز-ن-ي (zanā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Fornication, adultery; root sense of deviation from the natural and lawful course.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Prophet's expansion of "zinā" to the limbs is a theological metaphor (majāz) for the soul's inclination toward transgression, actualized by each member.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Here, "zinā" is transferred (manqūl) from the specific act to its preparatory and ancillary sins—a rhetorical trope of synecdoche.
- Root: خ-ل-و (khalā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be alone, to be empty; seclusion of two persons in a private space.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological discourse, "khalwah" is the unlawful privacy between a man and an unrelated woman, a state inviting temptation (fitnah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal spatial solitude; metaphorical for the heart's seclusion with desire.
- Root: ح-م-و (ḥamū)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A husband's male relative (brother, nephew, cousin); root sense of closeness and in-law affinity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Prophet's equation of "al-ḥamū" with death (al-mawt) is a hyperbolic metaphor (mubālaghah) for the extreme danger of seclusion with such relatives, as the social familiarity masks the risk.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): "Death" here is metaphorical for the spiritual ruin and scandal that ensue, not literal mortality.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Conditional Prohibition (al-nahy al-muʿallaq bi-sharṭ) — In "If you insist on sitting, then give the road its right," the imperative (amr) following the conditional (sharṭ) is obligatory upon the stated condition, parsed as a jumlah shartiyyah with the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) carrying the binding command.
chapters.translation:
**1620** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Whoever acquires knowledge of that by which the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is sought, yet does not learn it except to obtain thereby a portion of the worldly goods, he shall not find the fragrance of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection» — meaning, its scent. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd with a sound chain of transmission, and the hadiths on this matter are numerous and well-known.

**Section 289** — Chapter on What Is Suspected to Be Ostentation (Riyāʾ) but Is Not Ostentation

**1621** — On the authority of Abū Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him): "Have you considered a man who performs a deed of goodness, and the people praise him for it?" He said: «That is the immediate glad tiding for the believer». Narrated by Muslim.

**Section 290** — Chapter on the Prohibition of Looking at an Unrelated Woman and a Handsome Beardless Youth Without a Legitimate Need

Allah the Exalted has said: {«Say to the believing men to lower their gaze»} [Al-Nūr: 30], and He the Exalted said: {«Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of these shall be questioned about»} [Al-Isrāʾ: 36], and He the Exalted said: {«He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal»} [Ghāfir: 19], and He the Exalted said: {«Indeed, your Lord is surely ever watchful»} [Al-Fajr: 14].

**1622** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «It has been decreed upon the son of Adam his share of fornication, which he will inevitably attain: the two eyes — their fornication is the look; the two ears — their fornication is the listening; the tongue — its fornication is the speech; the hand — its fornication is the grasp; the foot — its fornication is the step; and the heart yearns and desires, and the private parts either confirm that or deny it». Agreed upon. This is the wording of Muslim, and the narration of Al-Bukhārī is abridged.

**1623** — On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: «Beware of sitting in the roadways!» They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have no alternative to our sitting places, where we converse." So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «If you insist on the sitting, then give the road its right». They said: "And what is the right of the road, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: «Lowering the gaze, refraining from harm, returning the greeting of peace, commanding what is right, and forbidding what is wrong». Agreed upon.

**1624** — On the authority of Abū Ṭalḥah Zayd ibn Sahl (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: We were sitting in the courtyards conversing, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) came and stood over us, and said: «What is the matter with you and the gatherings of the open spaces? Avoid the gatherings of the open spaces!» So we said: "We only sat for no wrong purpose; we sat to remember and to converse." He said: «If not, then fulfill their right: lowering the gaze, returning the greeting of peace, and speaking well». Narrated by Muslim. "Al-Ṣaʿadāt" — with ḍammah on the ṣād and the ʿayn — meaning: the roadways.

**1625** — On the authority of Jarīr (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) about the sudden glance, and he said: «Turn away your gaze». Narrated by Muslim.

**1626** — On the authority of Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: I was with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), and Maymūnah was with him, when Ibn Umm Maktūm came — and that was after we had been commanded to observe the veil — so the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Veil yourselves from him». So we said: "O Messenger of Allah, is he not blind? He cannot see us, nor can he recognize us?" So the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Are you two blind? Do you not see him!?» Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and Al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A good and sound hadith."

**1627** — On the authority of Abū Saʿīd (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Let not a man look at the private parts of a man, nor a woman at the private parts of a woman; and let not a man lie with a man under one garment, nor a woman lie with a woman under one garment». Narrated by Muslim.

**Section 291** — Chapter on the Prohibition of Seclusion with an Unrelated Woman

Allah the Exalted has said: {«And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a curtain»} [Al-Aḥzāb: 53].

**1628** — On the authority of ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Beware of entering upon women!» So a man from the Anṣār said: "Have you considered the ḥamū?" He said: «The ḥamū is death!» Agreed upon. "Al-Ḥamū": the husband's close relative, such as his brother, his brother's son, and his paternal cousin.

**1629** — On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Let not any one of you seclude himself with a woman except with a close male relative (maḥram)». Agreed upon.

**1630** — On the authority of Buraydah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «The sanctity of the wives of the mujāhidīn (those who strive in Allah's cause) with respect to those who stay behind is like the sanctity of their own mothers. There is no man among those who stay behind who is entrusted with the family of a mujāhid and then betrays him in them, except that he shall be made to stand before him on the Day of Resurrection, and he shall take from his good deeds whatever he wishes until he is satisfied». Then the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) turned to us and said: «What do you think?» Narrated by Muslim.

**Section 292** — Chapter on the Prohibition of Men Imitating Women and Women Imitating Men in Dress, Movement, and Otherwise

**1631** — On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) cursed the effeminate men among men, and the masculine women among women. In another narration: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) cursed the men who imitate women, and the women who imitate men. Narrated by Al-Bukhārī.

**1632** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) cursed the man who wears the garment of a woman, and the woman who wears the garment of a man. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd with a sound chain of transmission.

**1633** — On his authority, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Two categories of the people of the Fire I have not yet seen: a people with whips like the tails of cattle, with which they strike the people; and women who are clothed yet naked, swaying and inclining, their heads like the humps of the Bactrian camels, leaning to one side — they shall not enter Paradise, nor shall they find its fragrance, though its fragrance is indeed found from the distance of such-and-such a journey». Narrated by Muslim. The meaning of "clothed yet naked" (kāsiyāt ʿāriyāt): clothed with the blessings of Allah, yet naked of gratitude for them. And it is said: its meaning is that she covers part of her body and uncovers part of it, displaying her beauty and the like. And it is said: she wears a thin garment that describes the color of her body. And the meaning of "inclining" (māʾilāt): it is said, away from obedience to Allah and what they are obligated to preserve; and "swaying" (mumīlāt): that is, they teach others their blameworthy conduct. And it is said: inclining — they walk with a swaggering gait, swaying their shoulders.

chapters.title_en: Section 136 — Prohibition of Imitating Satan and the Unbelievers; and Related Adornment Rulings
chapters.arabic_text:
وقيل: مائلات يمتشطن المشطة الميلاء: وهي مشطة البغايا، و «مميلات» يمشطن

غيرهن تلك المشطة.
# «رؤوسهن كأسنمة البخت» أي: يكبرنها ويعظمنها بلف عمامة أو عصابة أو

نحوها.

$ 293 - باب النهي عن التشبه بالشيطان والكفار

| 1634 - 
# عن جابر - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا

تأكلوا بالشمال، فإن الشيطان يأكل ويشرب بالشمال». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1635 - 
# وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«لا يأكلن أحدكم (1) بشماله، ولا يشربن بها، فإن الشيطان يأكل بشماله ويشرب

بها». رواه مسلم. (2)

| 1636 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«إن اليهود والنصارى لا يصبغون، فخالفوهم». متفق عليه. (1)
# المراد: خضاب شعر اللحية والرأس الأبيض بصفرة أو حمرة؛ وأما السواد،

فمنهي عنه كما سنذكره في الباب بعده، إن شاء الله تعالى.

$ 294 - باب نهي الرجل والمرأة عن خضاب شعرهما بسواد

| 1637 - 
# عن جابر - رضي الله عنه - قال: أتي بأبي قحافة والد أبي بكر الصديق رضي

الله عنهما، يوم فتح مكة ورأسه ولحيته كالثغامة (1) بياضا. فقال رسول الله

- صلى الله عليه وسلم: «غيروا هذا واجتنبوا السواد». رواه مسلم. (2)

$ 295 - باب النهي عن القزع وهو حلق بعض الرأس دون بعض (1)، وإباحة حلقه كله للرجل دون المرأة

| 1638 - 
# عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، قال:  نهى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

عن القزع. متفق عليه. (2)

| 1639 - 
# وعنه، قال: رأى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - صبيا قد حلق بعض شعر

رأسه وترك بعضه، فنهاهم عن ذلك، وقال: «احلقوه كله، أو اتركوه كله». رواه

أبو داود بإسناد صحيح على شرط البخاري ومسلم. (1)

| 1640 - 
# وعن عبد الله بن جعفر رضي الله عنهما: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

أمهل آل جعفر ثلاثا، ثم أتاهم، فقال: «لا تبكوا على أخي بعد اليوم» ثم قال:

«ادعوا لي بني أخي» فجيء بنا كأننا أفرخ فقال: «ادعوا لي الحلاق» فأمره،

فحلق رؤوسنا. رواه أبو داود بإسناد صحيح على شرط البخاري ومسلم. (1)

| 1641 - 
# وعن علي - رضي الله عنه - قال: نهى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن

تحلق المرأة رأسها. رواه النسائي. (1)

$ 296 - باب تحريم وصل الشعر والوشم (1) والوشر وهو تحديد الأسنان
# قال تعالى: {إن يدعون من دونه إلا إناثا وإن يدعون إلا شيطانا مريدا لعنه

الله وقال لأتخذن من عبادك نصيبا مفروضا ولأضلنهم ولأمنينهم ولآمرنهم

فليبتكن آذان الأنعام ولآمرنهم فليغيرن خلق الله} [النساء: 117 - 119].

| 1642 - 
# وعن أسماء رضي الله عنها: أن امرأة سألت النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

فقالت: يا رسول الله إن ابنتي أصابتها الحصبة (1)، فتمرق شعرها، وإني

زوجتها، أفأصل فيه؟ فقال: «لعن الله الواصلة والموصولة». متفق عليه. (2)
# وفي رواية: «الواصلة، والمستوصلة».
# قولها: «فتمرق» هو بالراء ومعناه: انتثر وسقط. «والواصلة»: التي تصل

شعرها، أو شعر غيرها بشعر آخر. «والموصولة»: التي يوصل شعرها.
# «والمستوصلة»: التي تسأل من يفعل لها ذلك.
# وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها نحوه. متفق عليه.

| 1643 - 
# وعن حميد بن عبد الرحمان: أنه سمع معاوية - رضي الله عنه - عام حج على

المنبر وتناول قصة من شعر كانت في يد حرسي فقال: يا أهل المدينة أين

علماؤكم؟! سمعت النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ينهى عن مثل هذه، ويقول:

«إنما هلكت بنوإسرائيل حين اتخذها نساؤهم». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1644 - 
# وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه  وسلم - لعن

الواصلة والمستوصلة، والواشمة والمستوشمة. متفق عليه. (1)

| 1645 - 
# وعن ابن مسعود - رضي الله عنه - قال: لعن الله الواشمات والمستوشمات

والمتنمصات، والمتفلجات للحسن، المغيرات خلق الله، فقالت له امرأة في ذلك

| [ص: 462]
# فقال: وما لي لا ألعن من لعنه رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وهو في

كتاب الله؟ قال الله تعالى: {وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نهاكم عنه

فانتهوا} [سورة الحشر: 7]. متفق عليه. (1)
# «المتفلجة» هي: التي تبرد من أسنانها ليتباعد بعضها عن بعض قليلا،

وتحسنها وهو الوشر. «والنامصة»: التي تأخذ من شعر حاجب غيرها، وترققه ليصير

حسنا. «والمتنمصة»: التي تأمر من يفعل بها ذلك.

$ 297 - باب النهي عن نتف الشيب من اللحية والرأس وغيرهما، وعن نتف الأمرد شعر لحيته عند أول طلوعه

| 1646 - 
# عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - قال: «لا تنتفوا الشيب؛ فإنه نور المسلم يوم القيامة» حديث

حسن، رواه أبو داود، والترمذي، والنسائي بأسانيد حسنة، قال الترمذي: «هو

حديث حسن» (1).

| 1647 - 
# وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من

عمل عملا ليس عليه أمرنا فهو رد». رواه مسلم. (1)

$ 298 - باب كراهة الاستنجاء (1) باليمين ومس الفرج باليمين من غير عذر

| 1648 - 
# وعن أبي قتادة - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«إذا بال أحدكم، فلا يأخذن ذكره بيمينه، ولا يستنج بيمينه، ولا يتنفس في

الإناء». متفق عليه. (2)
# وفي الباب أحاديث كثيرة صحيحة.

$ 299 - باب كراهة المشي في نعل واحدة أو خف واحد لغير عذر وكراهة لبس النعل والخف قائما لغير عذر

| 1649 - 
# عن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:
chapters.anchors:
- Root: م-ي-ل (m-y-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Inclination, deviation from the straight path; a leaning of the head or body in pride or coquetry.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Moral and spiritual deviation — the inner disposition of the heart inclining toward vanity and seduction.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical leaning; metaphorical (majāz) = the gait and bearing of women who sway seductively to attract men.
- Sībawayh Rule: Naʿt Sababī (Attributive Adjective with Pronominal Reference) — the active participle «مائلات» governs a following prepositional phrase «بما» that is semantically linked to the head noun, requiring careful resolution of the pronominal reference.
chapters.translation:
Know that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said concerning women who are «مائلات مميلات» — that is, those who incline (māʾilāt) from obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and who cause others to incline (mumīlāt) from the path of truth by their seductive bearing. It is also said: they are those who incline in their gait, swaying coquettishly, and who teach others to do likewise. And it is said: «مائلات» are those who comb their hair with the "inclined combing" (al-mashṭah al-maylāʾ) — which is the combing of prostitutes (al-baghāyā) — and «مميلات» are those who comb others' hair with that same style of combing.

His saying, peace be upon him: «رؤوسهن كأسنمة البخت» — "their heads are like the humps of Bactrian camels" — means: they enlarge and magnify their heads by wrapping a turban, a headband, or something similar upon them, so that their heads appear elevated and humped like the humps of that breed of camel.

---

**Section 293 — Prohibition of Imitating Satan and the Unbelievers**

**Hadith 1634:** On the authority of Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: «Do not eat with your left hand, for verily Satan eats and drinks with his left hand.» Narrated by Muslim.

**Hadith 1635:** On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: «Let none of you eat with his left hand, nor drink with it, for verily Satan eats with his left hand and drinks with it.» Narrated by Muslim.

**Hadith 1636:** On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: «Verily the Jews and the Christians do not dye [their grey hair], so differ from them.» Agreed upon (by al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

The intended meaning [of dyeing] is the dyeing of the white hair of the beard and head with yellow or red [coloring]. As for black [dye], it is prohibited, as we shall mention in the following section, Allah Most High willing.

---

**Section 294 — Prohibition of a Man and a Woman Dyeing Their Hair Black**

**Hadith 1637:** On the authority of Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Abū Quḥāfah, the father of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with them both, was brought on the day of the Conquest of Mecca, and his head and beard were as white as the thughāmah plant (a white-flowered herb). The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: «Change this [whiteness], and avoid black.» Narrated by Muslim.

---

**Section 295 — Prohibition of al-Qazaʿ (i.e., Shaving Part of the Head and Leaving Part), and the Permissibility of Shaving the Entire Head for a Man, but Not for a Woman**

**Hadith 1638:** On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade al-qazaʿ. Agreed upon.

**Hadith 1639:** On the same authority, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw a boy whose head had been partially shaved and partially left, and he forbade them from doing that, saying: «Shave it all, or leave it all.» Narrated by Abū Dāwūd with a sound chain (isnād) upon the condition of al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

**Hadith 1640:** On the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar, may Allah be pleased with them both: That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave the family of Jaʿfar a respite of three days [for mourning], then came to them and said: «Do not weep for my brother after this day.» Then he said: «Call to me the sons of my brother.» So we were brought to him as if we were chicks (afrākh). He said: «Call the barber to me.» Then he commanded him, and he shaved our heads. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd with a sound chain upon the condition of al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

**Hadith 1641:** On the authority of ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade that a woman shave her head. Narrated by al-Nasāʾī.

---

**Section 296 — Prohibition of Extending Hair (waṣl), Tattooing (washm), and Filing the Teeth (washr, i.e., Sharpening/Spacing the Teeth)**

Allah Most High said: {«إن يدعون من دونه إلا إناثا وإن يدعون إلا شيطانا مريدا لعنه الله وقال لأتخذن من عبادك نصيبا مفروضا ولأضلنهم ولأمنينهم ولآمرنهم فليبتكن آذان الأنعام ولآمرنهم فليغيرن خلق الله»} — "They invoke not besides Him but female [deities], and they invoke not but a rebellious Satan, whom Allah has cursed. For he said: 'I will surely take from among Your servants a portion ordained. And I will surely mislead them, and I will surely arouse in them [sinful] desires, and I will surely command them so they will slit the ears of cattle, and I will surely command them so they will change the creation of Allah.'" [Al-Nisāʾ: 117–119].

**Hadith 1642:** On the authority of Asmāʾ, may Allah be pleased with her: That a woman asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying: O Messenger of Allah, my daughter was afflicted with measles (al-ḥaṣbah), and her hair fell out (tamarraqa). I have married her [now], so may I extend [her hair with additions]? He said: «Allah has cursed the woman who extends hair (al-wāṣilah) and the woman whose hair is extended (al-mawṣūlah).» Agreed upon.

In another narration: «al-wāṣilah and al-mustawṣilah» (the one who asks for hair extension).

Her saying «فتمرق» (fa-tamarraqa) is with the letter rāʾ, and its meaning is: it scattered and fell out. «Al-wāṣilah» is the woman who joins her own hair, or the hair of another, with additional hair. «Al-mawṣūlah» is the woman whose hair is joined [by another]. «Al-mustawṣilah» is the woman who asks someone to do that for her.

And on the authority of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, something similar [is narrated]. Agreed upon.

**Hadith 1643:** On the authority of Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: That he heard Muʿāwiyah, may Allah be pleased with him, in the year of the Hajj, upon the pulpit — and he took a lock of hair that was in the hand of a guard — saying: O people of Medina! Where are your scholars?! I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbidding something like this, saying: «Verily the Children of Israel were destroyed when their women took to this [practice].» Agreed upon.

**Hadith 1644:** On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, cursed the woman who extends hair (al-wāṣilah) and the one who asks for extension (al-mustawṣilah), and the woman who tattoos (al-wāshimah) and the one who asks for tattooing (al-mustawshimah). Agreed upon.

**Hadith 1645:** On the authority of Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Allah has cursed the women who tattoo (al-wāshimāt) and those who ask for tattooing (al-mustawshimāt), and those who pluck facial hair (al-mutanammiṣāt), and those who file their teeth for beauty (al-mutafallijāt), [thereby] changing the creation of Allah. A woman said to him concerning that [i.e., questioning his severity] — [and he replied]: And why should I not curse those whom the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, cursed, while it is in the Book of Allah? Allah Most High said: {«وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا»} — "And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it." [Sūrat al-Ḥashr: 7]. Agreed upon.

«Al-mutafallijah» is the woman who files her teeth so that they become slightly spaced apart from one another, beautifying them — and this is al-washr. «Al-nāmiṣah» is the woman who plucks the hair of another's eyebrow and thins it so that it becomes beautiful. «Al-mutanammiṣah» is the woman who asks someone to do that to her.

---

**Section 297 — Prohibition of Plucking Grey Hair from the Beard, Head, and Elsewhere; and Prohibition of a Beardless Youth Plucking His Beard Hair When It First Begins to Appear**

**Hadith 1646:** On the authority of ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: «Do not pluck out grey hair, for verily it is the light (nūr) of the Muslim on the Day of Resurrection.» A ḥasan (good) hadith, narrated by Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Nasāʾī with sound chains. Al-Tirmidhī said: "It is a ḥasan hadith."

**Hadith 1647:** On the authority of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: «Whoever performs a deed that is not in accordance with our affair [i.e., our Sunnah], it is rejected.» Narrated by Muslim.

---

**Section 298 — Dislike (Karāhah) of Cleaning Oneself After Relieving Oneself (al-istinjāʾ) with the Right Hand, and Touching the Genitals with the Right Hand Without a Valid Excuse**

**Hadith 1648:** On the authority of Abū Qatādah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: «When one of you urinates, let him not take his penis with his right hand, nor clean himself with his right hand, nor breathe into the vessel [while drinking].» Agreed upon.

And in this section there are many authentic hadiths.

---

**Section 299 — Dislike of Walking in a Single Sandal or a Single Sock Without a Valid Excuse; and Dislike of Putting on Sandals or Socks While Standing Without a Valid Excuse**

**Hadith 1649:** On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: [The hadith continues in the following section of the text.]

«لا يمش أحدكم في نعل واحدة، لينعلهما جميعا، أو ليخلعهما جميعا».
# وفي رواية: «أو ليحفهما جميعا». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1650 - 
# وعنه، قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يقول: «إذا انقطع شسع

(1) نعل أحدكم، فلا يمش في الأخرى حتى يصلحها». رواه مسلم.  (2)

| 1651 - 
# وعن جابر - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - نهى أن

ينتعل الرجل قائما. رواه أبو داود بإسناد حسن. (1)

$ 300 - باب النهي عن ترك النار في البيت عند النوم ونحوه سواء كانت في سراج أو غيره

| 1652 - 
# عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «لا

تتركوا
# النار في بيوتكم حين تنامون». (1) متفق عليه. (2)

| 1653 - 
# وعن أبي موسى الأشعري - رضي الله عنه - قال: احترق بيت بالمدينة على أهله

من الليل، فلما حدث رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بشأنهم، قال: «إن هذه

النار عدو لكم، فإذا نمتم، فأطفئوها» متفق عليه. (1)

| 1654 - 
# وعن جابر - رضي الله عنه - عن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«غطوا الإناء، وأوكئوا السقاء، وأغلقوا الأبواب، وأطفئوا السراج، فإن

الشيطان لا يحل سقاء، ولا يفتح

| [ص: 464]

# بابا، ولا يكشف إناء. فإن لم يجد أحدكم إلا أن يعرض على إنائه عودا،

ويذكر اسم الله، فليفعل، فإن الفويسقة تضرم على أهل البيت بيتهم». رواه

مسلم. (1)
# «الفويسقة»: الفأرة، «وتضرم»: تحرق.

$ 301 - باب النهي عن التكلف، وهو فعل وقول ما لا مصلحة فيه بمشقة
# قال الله تعالى: {قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر وما أنا من المتكلفين} [ص:

86].
#

| 1655 - 
# وعن عمر - رضي الله عنه - قال: نهينا عن التكلف. رواه البخاري. (1)

| 1656 - 
# وعن مسروق، قال: دخلنا على عبد الله بن مسعود - رضي الله عنه - فقال: يا

أيها الناس، من علم شيئا فليقل به، ومن لم يعلم، فليقل: الله أعلم، فإن من

العلم أن يقول لما لا يعلم: الله أعلم. قال الله تعالى لنبيه - صلى الله

عليه وسلم: {قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر وما أنا من المتكلفين}. [ص: 86].

رواه البخاري. (1)

$ 302 - باب تحريم النياحة على الميت ولطم الخد وشق الجيب ونتف الشعر وحلقه والدعاء بالويل والثبور

| 1657 - 
# عن عمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«الميت يعذب في قبره بما نيح عليه».
# وفي رواية: «ما نيح  عليه». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1658 - 
# وعن ابن مسعود - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «ليس منا من ضرب الخدود، وشق الجيوب، ودعا بدعوى الجاهلية». متفق

عليه. (1)

| 1659 - 
# وعن أبي بردة، قال: وجع أبو موسى، فغشي عليه، ورأسه في حجر امرأة

| [ص: 465]
# من أهله، فأقبلت تصيح برنة (1) فلم يستطع أن يرد عليها شيئا، فلما أفاق

قال: أنا بريء ممن برىء منه رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إن رسول الله

- صلى الله عليه وسلم - بريء من الصالقة، والحالقة، والشاقة. متفق عليه.

(2)
# «الصالقة»: التي ترفع صوتها بالنياحة والندب. «والحالقة»: التي تحلق

رأسها عند المصيبة. «والشاقة»: التي تشق ثوبها.

| 1660 - 
# وعن المغيرة بن شعبة - رضي الله عنه - قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - يقول: «من نيح عليه، فإنه يعذب بما نيح عليه يوم القيامة».

متفق عليه. (1)

| 1661 - 
# وعن أم عطية نسيبة - بضم النون وفتحها - رضي الله عنها، قالت: أخذ علينا

رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عند البيعة أن لا ننوح. متفق عليه. (1)

| 1662 - 
# وعن النعمان بن بشير رضي الله عنهما، قال: أغمي على عبد الله بن رواحة -

رضي الله عنه - فجعلت أخته تبكي، وتقول: واجبلاه، واكذا، واكذا: تعدد عليه.

فقال حين أفاق: ما قلت شيئا إلا قيل لي أنت كذلك؟!. رواه البخاري. (1)

| 1663 - 
# وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، قال: اشتكى سعد بن عبادة - رضي الله عنه -

شكوى، فأتاه رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يعوده مع عبد الرحمان بن

عوف، وسعد بن أبي وقاص، وعبد الله بن مسعود - رضي الله عنهم. فلما دخل

عليه، وجده في غشية (1) فقال: «أقضى؟» قالوا: لا يا رسول الله، فبكى رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فلما رأى القوم بكاء النبي - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - بكوا، قال: «ألا تسمعون؟ إن الله

| [ص: 466]
# لا يعذب بدمع العين، ولا بحزن القلب، ولكن يعذب بهذا - وأشار إلى لسانه -

أو يرحم». متفق عليه. (2)

| 1664 - 
# وعن أبي مالك الأشعري - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول  الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم: «النائحة إذا لم تتب قبل موتها تقام يوم القيامة وعليها سربال

(1) من قطران، ودرع (2) من جرب». رواه مسلم. (3)

| 1665 - 
# وعن أسيد بن أبي أسيد التابعي، عن امرأة من المبايعات، قالت: كان فيما

أخذ علينا رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في المعروف الذي أخذ علينا أن

لا نعصيه فيه: أن لا نخمش وجها، ولا ندعو ويلا، ولا نشق جيبا، وأن لا ننشر

شعرا. رواه أبو داود بإسناد حسن. (1)

| 1666 - 
# وعن أبي موسى - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«ما من ميت يموت فيقوم باكيهم فيقول: واجبلاه (1)، واسيداه، أو نحو ذلك إلا

وكل به ملكان يلهزانه: أهكذا كنت؟». رواه الترمذي، (2) وقال: «حديث حسن».
# «اللهز»: الدفع بجمع اليد في الصدر.

| 1667 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «اثنتان في الناس هما بهم كفر: الطعن في النسب، والنياحة على الميت».

(1) رواه مسلم. (2)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ع-ل (n-ʿ-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The sandal or shoe; the act of wearing footwear; also the sole of the foot.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical covering of the foot; in prophetic injunctions, it signifies complete bodily preparation and symmetry in ritual and daily acts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — wearing sandals; metaphorical (majāz) — completeness of one's state; walking in one sandal is a mark of imbalance and deviation from the prophetic norm.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Construction (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The imperative "لينعلهما جميعا، أو ليخلعهما جميعا" (let him wear both or take off both) functions as the apodosis of an implied conditional, demanding a binary resolution to avoid ambiguity.

- Root: ن-ا-ر (n-ā-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Fire; the elemental flame; also punishment and hellfire.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradats): In sacred law, fire is a created utility but also a source of destruction; the command to extinguish it at night reflects the principle of preventing harm (darʾ al-mafāsid).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the physical flame; metaphorical — the enmity of fire as a "foe" (ʿadūw) personified, indicating its potential to destroy.
- Sībawayh Rule: Prohibition Construction (Ṣīghat al-Nahy) — "لا تتركوا النار" (Do not leave the fire) is a direct negative imperative, indicating categorical prohibition (taḥrīm) in this context.

- Root: ك-ل-ف (k-l-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To burden, to impose hardship; also to be enamored or preoccupied.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Takalluf is self-imposed affectation — undertaking speech or action that exceeds one's capacity or lacks genuine benefit, often for show.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — burdening oneself; metaphorical — pretentiousness in religion, condemned as a departure from prophetic simplicity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Masdar Construction — "التكلف" (affectation) as a verbal noun denotes the act itself, and its prohibition is absolute unless tied to a genuine religious or worldly benefit.

- Root: ن-و-ح (n-w-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Lamentation, wailing; the raising of the voice in mourning with enumeration of the deceased's virtues.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A pre-Islamic practice of excessive grief expression; in Islamic law, it is a major sin (kabīrah) because it implies discontent with divine decree.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — audible wailing; metaphorical — the inner rebellion against God's will, which the shariah uproots.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf (Coordination) — In "الصالقة، والحالقة، والشاقة" (the shrieker, the shaver, the tearer), the conjunction links three participial nouns, each denoting a distinct prohibited act, unified under the same legal ruling.
chapters.translation:
**Section 137 — Prohibition of Walking in One Sandal, Leaving Fire Burning at Night, Affectation (Takalluf), and Lamentation (Niyāḥah) over the Dead**

**Chapter on the Prohibition of Walking in One Sandal**

| 1649 — 
From Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «لا يمش أحدكم في نعل واحدة، لينعلهما جميعا، أو ليخلعهما جميعا» — "Let none of you walk in a single sandal; let him wear both of them, or take off both of them."
And in another narration: «أو ليحفهما جميعا» — "or let him remove both of them." Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

| 1650 — 
And from him (Abū Hurayrah), he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: «إذا انقطع شسع نعل أحدكم، فلا يمش في الأخرى حتى يصلحها» — "When the strap of one of your sandals breaks, let him not walk in the other until he repairs it." Narrated by Muslim.

| 1651 — 
And from Jābir (may Allah be pleased with him): That the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade a man from putting on his sandal while standing. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd with a good (ḥasan) chain of transmission.

**Chapter 300 — Prohibition of Leaving Fire in the House at Sleep Time and the Like, Whether in a Lamp or Otherwise**

| 1652 — 
From Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), he said: «لا تتركوا النار في بيوتكم حين تنامون» — "Do not leave the fire in your houses when you sleep." Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

| 1653 — 
And from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: A house in Madīnah burned down over its inhabitants at night. When the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) was informed of their matter, he said: «إن هذه النار عدو لكم، فإذا نمتم، فأطفئوها» — "Indeed, this fire is an enemy to you. So when you sleep, extinguish it." Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

| 1654 — 
And from Jābir (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), he said: «غطوا الإناء، وأوكئوا السقاء، وأغلقوا الأبواب، وأطفئوا السراج، فإن الشيطان لا يحل سقاء، ولا يفتح بابا، ولا يكشف إناء. فإن لم يجد أحدكم إلا أن يعرض على إنائه عودا، ويذكر اسم الله، فليفعل، فإن الفويسقة تضرم على أهل البيت بيتهم» — "Cover the vessel, tie the waterskin, close the doors, and extinguish the lamp, for the devil does not untie a waterskin, nor open a door, nor uncover a vessel. If one of you finds nothing but to place a stick across his vessel and mention the name of Allah, let him do so, for the little wicked creature (al-fuwaysiqah) sets fire to the house of its inhabitants." Narrated by Muslim.
The commentator states: «الفويسقة» is the mouse, and «تضرم» means it burns (sets ablaze).

**Chapter 301 — Prohibition of Affectation (Takalluf), Which Is Doing or Saying What Has No Benefit with Hardship**

Allah the Exalted says: {قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر وما أنا من المتكلفين} [Ṣād: 86] — "Say: I do not ask you for it any payment, and I am not of the affecters (al-mutakallifīn)."

| 1655 — 
And from ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: We were forbidden from affectation (takalluf). Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

| 1656 — 
And from Masrūq, he said: We entered upon ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said: O people, whoever knows something, let him speak it; and whoever does not know, let him say: Allah knows best. For indeed, part of knowledge is to say for what one does not know: Allah knows best. Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): {قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر وما أنا من المتكلفين} [Ṣād: 86]. Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

**Chapter 302 — Prohibition of Lamentation (Niyāḥah) over the Dead, Striking the Cheeks, Tearing the Garment Collar, Pulling Out or Shaving the Hair, and Calling with Woe and Destruction**

| 1657 — 
From ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «الميت يعذب في قبره بما نيح عليه» — "The deceased is punished in his grave because of the lamentation made over him."
And in another narration: «ما نيح عليه» — "for what was lamented over him." Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

| 1658 — 
And from Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «ليس منا من ضرب الخدود، وشق الجيوب، ودعا بدعوى الجاهلية» — "He is not of us who strikes the cheeks, tears the collars, and calls with the call of the pre-Islamic era (Jāhiliyyah)." Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

| 1659 — 
And from Abū Burdah, he said: Abū Mūsā fell ill and fainted, with his head in the lap of a woman from his family. She began to shriek with a wailing cry (rinnah), and he could not respond to her at all. When he regained consciousness, he said: I am free of him whom the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) declared himself free of. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) declared himself free of the shrieker (al-ṣāliqah), the shaver (al-ḥāliqah), and the tearer (al-shāqqah). Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).
The commentator states: «الصالقة» is the one who raises her voice in lamentation and wailing; «الحالقة» is the one who shaves her head at a calamity; «الشاقة» is the one who tears her garment.

| 1660 — 
And from al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: «من نيح عليه، فإنه يعذب بما نيح عليه يوم القيامة» — "Whoever is lamented over, he will be punished for what was lamented over him on the Day of Resurrection." Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

| 1661 — 
And from Umm ʿAṭiyyah Nusaybah (with ḍammah on the nūn and its fatḥah) (may Allah be pleased with her), she said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) took from us at the pledge of allegiance (al-bayʿah) that we would not lament (lā nanūḥ). Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

| 1662 — 
And from al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr (may Allah be pleased with them both), he said: ʿAbdullāh ibn Rawāḥah (may Allah be pleased with him) fell unconscious, and his sister began to weep, saying: "O my mountain! O such-and-such! O such-and-such!" — enumerating his virtues. When he regained consciousness, he said: I did not say anything except it was said to me: "Are you like that?!" Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

| 1663 — 
And from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), he said: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah (may Allah be pleased with him) fell ill with an illness, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) came to visit him along with ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, and ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with them all). When he entered upon him, he found him in a swoon (ghashyah). He said: «أقضى؟» — "Has he passed away?" They said: No, O Messenger of Allah. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) wept. When the people saw the weeping of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), they wept. He said: «ألا تسمعون؟ إن الله لا يعذب بدمع العين، ولا بحزن القلب، ولكن يعذب بهذا - وأشار إلى لسانه - أو يرحم» — "Do you not hear? Indeed, Allah does not punish for the tear of the eye, nor for the grief of the heart, but He punishes for this — and he pointed to his tongue — or He shows mercy." Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

| 1664 — 
And from Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «النائحة إذا لم تتب قبل موتها تقام يوم القيامة وعليها سربال من قطران، ودرع من جرب» — "The lamenter (al-nāʾiḥah), if she does not repent before her death, will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection wearing a garment (sirbāl) of tar (qaṭrān) and a coat of mail (dirʿ) of scabies (jarab)." Narrated by Muslim.

| 1665 — 
And from Usayd ibn Abī Usayd, the Tābiʿī, from a woman among those who gave the pledge of allegiance, she said: Among what the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) took from us in the good (al-maʿrūf) that he took from us — that we would not disobey him in it — was that we would not scratch our faces, nor call for woe (wayl), nor tear our collars, nor spread (dishevel) our hair. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd with a good (ḥasan) chain of transmission.

| 1666 — 
And from Abū Mūsā (may Allah be pleased with him): That the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «ما من ميت يموت فيقوم باكيهم فيقول: واجبلاه، واسيداه، أو نحو ذلك إلا وكل به ملكان يلهزانه: أهكذا كنت؟» — "There is no deceased person who dies, and their wailer stands and says: 'O my mountain! O my master!' or the like, except that two angels are appointed over him, poking him (yalahizānahu): 'Was this how you were?'" Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A good (ḥasan) hadith."
The commentator states: «اللهز» (al-lahz) is the pushing with the fist against the chest.

| 1667 — 
And from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «اثنتان في الناس هما بهم كفر: الطعن في النسب، والنياحة على الميت» — "Two matters among the people are disbelief (kufr) in them: slandering lineage (al-ṭaʿn fī al-nasab) and lamentation over the dead (al-niyāḥah ʿalā al-mayyit)." Narrated by Muslim.

chapters.title_en: Section 138 — Prohibition of Consulting Soothsayers, Astrologers, Diviners, and the Prohibition of Superstitious Omens (Ṭiyarah); The Prohibition of Depicting Living Beings
chapters.arabic_text:
$ 303 - باب النهي عن إتيان الكهان والمنجمين والعراف وأصحاب الرمل والطوارق بالحصى وبالشعير ونحو ذلك

| 1668 - 
# عن عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت: سأل رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

أناس عن الكهان، فقال: «ليسوا بشيء» فقالوا: يا رسول الله إنهم يحدثونا

أحيانا بشيء، فيكون حقا؟ فقال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «تلك الكلمة

من الحق يخطفها الجني فيقرها في أذن وليه، فيخلطون معها مائة كذبة». متفق

عليه. (1)
# وفي رواية للبخاري عن عائشة رضي الله عنها: أنها سمعت رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - يقول: «إن الملائكة تنزل في العنان - وهو السحاب - فتذكر

الأمر قضي في السماء، فيسترق الشيطان السمع، فيسمعه، فيوحيه إلى الكهان،

فيكذبون معها مائة كذبة من عند أنفسهم».
# قوله: «فيقرها» هو بفتح الياء وضم القاف والراء، أي: يلقيها،
# «والعنان» بفتح العين.

| 1669 - 
# وعن صفية بنت أبي عبيد، عن بعض أزواج النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ورضي

الله عنها، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «من أتى عرافا (1) فسأله

عن  شيء فصدقه، لم تقبل له صلاة أربعين يوما». رواه مسلم. (2)

| 1670 - 
# وعن قبيصة بن المخارق - رضي الله عنه - قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - يقول: «العيافة، والطيرة، والطرق، من الجبت». رواه أبو داود

بإسناد حسن. (1)
# وقال: «الطرق» هو الزجر: أي زجر الطير وهو أن يتيمن أو يتشاءم بطيرانه،

فإن طار إلى جهة اليمين، تيمن، وإن طار إلى جهة اليسار، تشاءم. قال أبو

داود: «والعيافة»: الخط.
# قال الجوهري في الصحاح (2): الجبت كلمة تقع على الصنم والكاهن والساحر

ونحو ذلك.

| 1671 - 
# وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«من اقتبس علما من النجوم (1)، اقتبس شعبة من السحر زاد ما زاد». رواه أبو

داود بإسناد صحيح. (2)

| 1672 - 
# وعن معاوية بن الحكم - رضي الله عنه - قال: قلت: يا رسول الله إني حديث

عهد بالجاهلية، وقد جاء الله تعالى بالإسلام، وإن منا رجالا يأتون الكهان؟

قال: «فلا تأتهم» قلت: ومنا رجال يتطيرون؟ قال: «ذلك شيء يجدونه في صدورهم،

فلا يصدهم» قلت: ومنا رجال يخطون؟ قال: «كان نبي من الأنبياء يخط، فمن وافق

خطه، فذاك». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1673 - 
# وعن أبي مسعود البدري - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم

- نهى عن ثمن الكلب (1)، ومهر البغي (2)، وحلوان الكاهن (3). متفق عليه.

(4)

$ 304 - باب النهي عن التطير
# فيه الأحاديث السابقة في الباب قبله (1).

| 1674 - 
# وعن أنس - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا

عدوى ولا طيرة، ويعجبني الفأل» قالوا: وما الفأل؟ قال: «كلمة طيبة». متفق

عليه. (1)

| 1675 - 
# وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«لا عدوى ولا طيرة. وإن كان الشؤم في شيء ففي الدار، والمرأة، والفرس (1)».

متفق عليه. (2)

| 1676 - 
# وعن بريدة - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان لا

يتطير. رواه أبو داود بإسناد صحيح. (1)

| 1677 - 
# وعن عروة بن عامر - رضي الله عنه - قال: ذكرت الطيرة عند رسول الله - صلى

الله  عليه وسلم - فقال: «أحسنها الفأل. ولا ترد مسلما فإذا رأى أحدكم ما

يكره، فليقل:

| [ص: 454]
# اللهم لا يأتي بالحسنات إلا أنت، ولا يدفع السيئات إلا أنت، ولا حول ولا

قوة إلا بك» حديث صحيح رواه أبو داود بإسناد صحيح. (1)

$ 305 - باب تحريم تصوير الحيوان في بساط أو حجر أو ثوب أو درهم أو مخدة أو دينار أو وسادة وغير ذلك وتحريم اتخاذ الصور في حائط وسقف وستر وعمامة وثوب ونحوها
# والأمر بإتلاف الصورة (1)

| 1678 - 
# عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«إن الذين يصنعون هذه الصور يعذبون يوم القيامة، يقال لهم: أحيوا ما

خلقتم». متفق عليه. (2)

| 1679 - 
# وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت: قدم رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من

سفر، وقد سترت سهوة لي بقرام فيه تماثيل، فلما رآه رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - تلون وجهه، وقال: «يا عائشة، أشد الناس عذابا عند الله يوم

القيامة الذين يضاهون بخلق الله!» قالت: فقطعناه فجعلنا منه وسادة أو

وسادتين. متفق عليه. (1)
# «القرام» بكسر القاف هو: الستر. «والسهوة» بفتح السين المهملة، وهي:

الصفة تكون بين يدي البيت، وقيل: هي الطاق النافذ في الحائط.

| 1680 - 
# وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم

- يقول: «كل مصور في النار، يجعل له بكل صورة صورها نفس فيعذبه في جهنم».

قال ابن عباس: فإن كنت لا بد فاعلا، فاصنع الشجر وما لا روح فيه. متفق

عليه. (1)

| 1681 - 
# وعنه، قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يقول: «من صور صورة في

الدنيا، كلف أن ينفخ فيها الروح يوم القيامة وليس بنافخ». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1682 - 
# وعن ابن مسعود - رضي الله عنه - قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - يقول: «إن أشد الناس عذابا يوم القيامة المصورون». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1683 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - يقول: «قال الله تعالى: ومن أظلم ممن ذهب  يخلق كخلقي؟ فليخلقوا ذرة

أو ليخلقوا حبة، أو ليخلقوا شعيرة». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1684 - 
# وعن أبي طلحة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«لا تدخل الملائكة بيتا فيه كلب ولا صورة». متفق عليه. (1)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ه-ن (K-H-N)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: One who claims knowledge of the unseen (ghayb) through jinn or satanic agency; the professional soothsayer (kāhin).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The kāhin is one who asserts foreknowledge of events, a practice rooted in jāhiliyyah and antithetical to prophetic revelation (waḥy).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for the soothsayer; metaphorically extended to astrologers (munajjimūn) and diviners (ʿarrāfūn) who share the same epistemic claim.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The phrase «من أتى عرافا...» employs the conditional particle 'man' governing a protasis and apodosis, indicating a universal legal ruling contingent upon the act.

- Root: ط-ي-ر (T-Y-R)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is 'bird' or 'flight'; from it derives ṭiyarah (omen-taking) via the practice of observing bird flight for augury.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ṭiyarah is a jāhili practice of seeking omens; Islam nullifies its validity, affirming tawakkul (reliance on God) instead.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: bird flight; metaphorical (majāz): the superstitious inference of good or ill fortune from such flight, condemned as a form of shirk.
- Sībawayh Rule: Negation of Genus (Lā li-nafy al-jins) — «لا عدوى ولا طيرة» negates the entire category of contagion and omen-taking as operative realities, a definitive grammatical nullification.

- Root: ص-و-ر (S-W-R)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To form, shape, or fashion; the act of giving form (taṣwīr) to something.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, taṣwīr is exclusively God's prerogative as al-Muṣawwir (The Fashioner); human imitation of this act constitutes a challenge to divine sovereignty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: shaping an image; metaphorical: the audacious attempt to rival God's creative act, hence the severe eschatological threat.
- Sībawayh Rule: Command Form (Ṣīghat al-Amr) — «أحيوا ما خلقتم» (Give life to what you have created) is an imperative used as a taḥaddī (challenge) and taklīf (imposition of the impossible), a rhetorical device known as amr mustaḥīl.
chapters.translation:
**§ 303 — Chapter on the Prohibition of Going to Soothsayers (kuhhān), Astrologers (munajjimūn), Diviners (ʿarrāfūn), Practitioners of Sand-Divination (aṣḥāb al-raml), and Those Who Cast Auguries with Pebbles, Barley, and the Like**

**1668** — On the authority of ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: People asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about soothsayers, and he said: «They are nothing.» They said: O Messenger of God, they sometimes relate to us a thing, and it turns out to be true. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «That is a word of truth which the jinn snatches, then whispers it into the ear of his ally, and they mix with it a hundred lies.» Agreed upon. (1)

In a narration of al-Bukhārī on the authority of ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her: that she heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: «Indeed, the angels descend in the 'anān — and it is the cloud — and mention an affair that has been decreed in heaven. Then the devil steals the hearing, hears it, and conveys it to the soothsayers, and they fabricate with it a hundred lies from themselves.»

His saying «fa-yuqirruhā» — it is with a fatḥah on the yāʾ and ḍammah on the qāf and the rāʾ, meaning: he casts it. And «al-ʿanān» is with a fatḥah on the ʿayn.

**1669** — On the authority of Ṣafiyyah bint Abī ʿUbayd, from one of the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, may God be pleased with her, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: «Whoever goes to a diviner (ʿarrāf) and asks him about something and believes him, his prayer will not be accepted for forty days.» Narrated by Muslim. (2)

**1670** — On the authority of Qabīṣah ibn al-Mukhāriq, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: «Augury by bird-cries (ʿiyāfah), superstitious omens (ṭiyarah), and divination by casting pebbles (ṭarq) are of al-jibt.» Narrated by Abū Dāwūd with a good chain. (1)

He said: «al-ṭarq» is the driving away — i.e., the augury by birds, which is taking a good or bad omen from their flight: if it flies to the right, one takes a good omen; if it flies to the left, one takes a bad omen. Abū Dāwūd said: «al-ʿiyāfah» is the drawing of lines. Al-Jawharī said in al-Ṣiḥāḥ (2): al-jibt is a word that applies to the idol, the soothsayer, the sorcerer, and the like.

**1671** — On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «Whoever acquires a branch of knowledge from the stars (1), has acquired a branch of sorcery; the more he increases, the more he increases in it.» Narrated by Abū Dāwūd with a sound chain. (2)

**1672** — On the authority of Muʿāwiyah ibn al-Ḥakam, may God be pleased with him, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, I have recently emerged from the jāhiliyyah, and God, Exalted is He, has brought Islam. Among us there are men who go to soothsayers? He said: «Do not go to them.» I said: And among us there are men who take superstitious omens? He said: «That is something they find in their breasts, so let it not deter them.» I said: And among us there are men who draw lines? He said: «There was a prophet among the prophets who drew lines; whoever matches his line, then that is it.» Narrated by Muslim. (1)

**1673** — On the authority of Abū Masʿūd al-Badrī, may God be pleased with him: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the price of a dog (1), the earnings of a prostitute (2), and the fee of a soothsayer (3). Agreed upon. (4)

**§ 304 — Chapter on the Prohibition of Superstitious Omens (al-Ṭiyarah)**
The preceding hadiths in the previous chapter apply here. (1)

**1674** — On the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «There is no contagion and no superstitious omen, and I like the good omen (al-faʾl).» They said: What is the good omen? He said: «A good word.» Agreed upon. (1)

**1675** — On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «There is no contagion and no superstitious omen. If there is ill-omen in anything, then in the house, the woman, and the horse (1).» Agreed upon. (2)

**1676** — On the authority of Buraydah, may God be pleased with him: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, never took superstitious omens. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd with a sound chain. (1)

**1677** — On the authority of ʿUrwah ibn ʿĀmir, may God be pleased with him, who said: Superstitious omens were mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: «The best of it is the good omen (al-faʾl), and it does not turn back a Muslim. When any of you sees something he dislikes, let him say:

O God, none brings good things but You, and none repels evil things but You, and there is no might and no power except with You.» A sound hadith narrated by Abū Dāwūd with a sound chain. (1)

**§ 305 — Chapter on the Prohibition of Depicting Living Beings on a Carpet, Stone, Garment, Coin, Pillow, Dinar, Cushion, and the Like; the Prohibition of Making Images on Walls, Ceilings, Curtains, Turbans, Garments, and Similar Items; and the Command to Destroy Images (1)**

**1678** — On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them both: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «Indeed, those who make these images will be tormented on the Day of Resurrection. It will be said to them: Give life to what you have created.» Agreed upon. (2)

**1679** — On the authority of ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from a journey, and I had screened a niche of mine (sahwah) with a curtain (qirām) upon which there were figures. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw it, his face changed color, and he said: «O ʿĀʾishah, the most severely tormented of people before God on the Day of Resurrection are those who imitate God's creation!» She said: So we cut it up and made from it one or two cushions. Agreed upon. (1)

«al-Qirām» — with a kasrah on the qāf — is the curtain. «al-Sahwah» — with a fatḥah on the sīn — is the portico at the front of the house; it is also said it is the niche that penetrates the wall.

**1680** — On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: «Every image-maker is in the Fire. For every image he made, a soul will be created for him, and it will torment him in Hell.» Ibn ʿAbbās said: If you must do it, then make trees and that which has no soul. Agreed upon. (1)

**1681** — On his authority, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: «Whoever makes an image in this world will be charged with breathing the spirit into it on the Day of Resurrection, and he will not be able to breathe.» Agreed upon. (1)

**1682** — On the authority of Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: «Indeed, the most severely tormented of people on the Day of Resurrection are the image-makers.» Agreed upon. (1)

**1683** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: «God, Exalted is He, said: And who is more unjust than one who goes to create like My creation? Let them create a speck, or let them create a grain, or let them create a barley-corn.» Agreed upon. (1)

**1684** — On the authority of Abū Ṭalḥah, may God be pleased with him: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: «The angels do not enter a house in which there is a dog or an image.» Agreed upon. (1)

| 1685 - 
# وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، قال: وعد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

جبريل أن يأتيه، فراث عليه حتى اشتد على رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

فخرج فلقيه جبريل فشكا إليه، فقال: إنا لا ندخل بيتا فيه كلب ولا صورة.

رواه البخاري. (1)
# «راث»: أبطأ، وهو بالثاء المثلثة.

| 1686 - 
# وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت: واعد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

جبريل عليه السلام، في ساعة أن يأتيه، فجاءت تلك الساعة ولم يأته! قالت:

وكان بيده عصا، فطرحها من يده وهو يقول: «ما يخلف الله وعده ولا رسله» ثم

التفت، فإذا جرو كلب تحت سريره. فقال: «متى دخل هذا الكلب؟» فقلت: والله ما

دريت به، فأمر به فأخرج، فجاءه جبريل - عليه السلام - فقال رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم: «وعدتني، فجلست لك ولم تأتني» فقال: منعني الكلب الذي كان

في بيتك، إنا لا ندخل بيتا فيه كلب ولا صورة. رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1687 - 
# وعن أبي الهياج حيان بن حصين، قال: قال لي علي بن أبي طالب - رضي الله

عنه: ألا أبعثك على ما بعثني عليه رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم؟ أن لا

تدع صورة إلا طمستها، ولا قبرا (1) مشرفا إلا سويته. رواه مسلم. (2)

$ 306 - باب تحريم اتخاذ الكلب إلا لصيد أو ماشية أو زرع

| 1688 - 
# عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

يقول: «من اقتنى كلبا إلا كلب صيد أو ماشية فإنه ينقص من أجره كل يوم

قيراطان». متفق عليه. (1)
# وفي رواية: «قيراط».

| 1689 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «من أمسك كلبا، فإنه ينقص من عمله كل يوم قيراط إلا كلب حرث أو

ماشية».  متفق عليه. (1)
# وفي رواية لمسلم: «من اقتنى كلبا ليس بكلب صيد، ولا ماشية ولا أرض، فإنه

ينقص من أجره قيراطان كل يوم».

$ 307 - باب كراهية تعليق الجرس في البعير وغيره من الدواب وكراهية استصحاب الكلب والجرس في السفر

| 1690 - 
# عن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«لا تصحب الملائكة رفقة فيها كلب أو جرس». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1691 - 
# وعنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «الجرس مزامير الشيطان».

رواه مسلم. (1)

$ 308 - باب كراهة ركوب الجلالة، وهي البعير أو الناقة التي تأكل العذرة، فإن أكلت علفا طاهرا فطاب لحمها، زالت الكراهة

| 1692 - 
# وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، قال: نهى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

عن
# الجلالة في الإبل أن يركب عليها. رواه أبو داود بإسناد صحيح. (1)

$ 309 - باب النهي عن البصاق في المسجد والأمر بإزالته منه إذا وجد فيه، والأمر بتنزيه المسجد عن الأقذار

| 1693 - 
# عن أنس - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«البصاق في المسجد خطيئة، وكفارتها دفنها». متفق عليه. (1)

| [ص: 473]
# والمراد بدفنها إذا كان المسجد ترابا أو رملا ونحوه، فيواريها تحت ترابه.
# قال أبو المحاسن الروياني (2) من أصحابنا في كتابه «البحر» وقيل: المراد

بدفنها إخراجها من المسجد، أما إذا كان المسجد مبلطا أو مجصصا، فدلكها عليه

بمداسه أو بغيره كما يفعله كثير من الجهال، فليس ذلك بدفن، بل زيادة في

الخطيئة وتكثير للقذر في المسجد، وعلى من فعل ذلك أن يمسحه بعد ذلك بثوبه

أو بيده أو غيره أو يغسله.

| 1694 - 
# وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - رأى في

جدار القبلة مخاطا، أو بزاقا، أو نخامة، فحكه. متفق عليه. (1)

| 1695 - 
# وعن أنس - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «إن

هذه المساجد لا تصلح لشيء من هذا البول ولا القذر، إنما هي لذكر الله

تعالى، وقراءة القرآن» أو كما قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه  وسلم. رواه

مسلم. (1)

$ 310 - باب كراهة الخصومة في المسجد ورفع الصوت فيه ونشد الضالة والبيع والشراء والإجارة ونحوها من المعاملات

| 1696 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أنه سمع رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

يقول: «من سمع رجلا ينشد ضالة (1) في المسجد فليقل: لا ردها الله عليك، فإن

المساجد لم تبن لهذا». رواه مسلم. (2)

| 1697 - 
# وعنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «إذا رأيتم من يبيع أو

يبتاع في المسجد،

| [ص: 474]
# فقولوا: لا أربح الله تجارتك، وإذا رأيتم من ينشد ضالة فقولوا: لا ردها

الله عليك». رواه الترمذي، (1) وقال: «حديث حسن».

| 1698 - 
# وعن بريدة - رضي الله عنه: أن رجلا نشد في المسجد فقال: من دعا إلى الجمل

الأحمر؟ فقال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا وجدت؛ إنما بنيت المساجد

لما بنيت له». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1699 - 
# وعن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - نهى عن الشراء والبيع في المسجد، وأن تنشد فيه ضالة؛ أو

ينشد فيه شعر. رواه أبو داود والترمذي، (1) وقال: «حديث حسن».

| 1700 - 
# وعن السائب بن يزيد الصحابي - رضي الله عنه - قال: كنت في المسجد فحصبني

(1) رجل، فنظرت فإذا عمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنه - فقال: اذهب فأتني

بهذين، فجئته بهما، فقال: من أين أنتما؟ فقالا: من أهل الطائف، فقال: لو

كنتما من أهل البلد، لأوجعتكما، ترفعان أصواتكما في مسجد رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم! رواه البخاري. (2)

$ 311 - باب نهي من أكل ثوما أو بصلا أو كراثا أو غيره مما له رائحة كريهة عن دخول المسجد قبل زوال رائحته إلا لضرورة

| 1701 - 
# عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «من
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ع-د (wa-ʿa-da)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To promise, to appoint a time; core sense of a binding commitment or fixed appointment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, denotes divine promise (waʿd) as an immutable decree of God, contrasted with threat (waʿīd).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for a stated covenant; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to God's fulfillment, emphasizing certainty.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) — The phrase "من اقتنى" (whoever acquires) introduces a conditional protasis, with the apodosis stating the consequence (decrease in reward), parsed as a general legal ruling.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) made an appointment with Gabriel (peace be upon him) to visit him, but Gabriel tarried (rātha) — meaning he delayed, with the letter thāʾ (ث) — until the delay became severe upon the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). He went out and met Gabriel, and complained to him. Gabriel said: "We do not enter a house in which there is a dog or an image." Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

And ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) appointed a time with Gabriel (peace be upon him) to come to him. That hour arrived, but he did not come. She said: He had a staff in his hand, and he cast it from his hand, saying: "Allah does not break His promise, nor do His messengers." Then he turned, and behold, there was a puppy under his bed. He said: "When did this dog enter?" I said: "By Allah, I did not know of it." He ordered it to be removed, and it was taken out. Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) came, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "You promised me, and I waited for you, but you did not come." He said: "The dog that was in your house prevented me. We do not enter a house in which there is a dog or an image." Narrated by Muslim.

And Abū al-Hayyāj Ḥayyān ibn Ḥuṣayn said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him) said to me: "Shall I not send you on a mission upon which the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) sent me? That you leave no image without effacing it, and no elevated grave without leveling it." Narrated by Muslim.

Section 306: Prohibition of Keeping a Dog Except for Hunting, Herding Livestock, or Farming

Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "Whoever keeps a dog, except a dog for hunting or herding livestock, two qīrāṭs are deducted from his reward every day." Agreed upon. In another narration: "One qīrāṭ."

And Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever retains a dog, a qīrāṭ is deducted from his deeds every day, except a dog for farming or herding livestock." Agreed upon. In a narration by Muslim: "Whoever keeps a dog that is not a hunting dog, nor for livestock, nor for land, two qīrāṭs are deducted from his reward every day."

Section 307: Dislike of Hanging a Bell on a Camel or Other Beasts, and Dislike of Taking a Dog or Bell on a Journey

Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Angels do not accompany a company in which there is a dog or a bell." Narrated by Muslim.

And from him: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The bell is the flute of Satan." Narrated by Muslim.

Section 308: Dislike of Riding the Jalālah — That Is, a Camel or She-Camel That Eats Filth; If It Eats Pure Fodder and Its Meat Becomes Wholesome, the Dislike Ceases

Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade riding the jalālah among camels. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd with a sound chain.

Section 309: Prohibition of Spitting in the Mosque, the Command to Remove It If Found There, and the Command to Keep the Mosque Free of Filth

Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Spitting in the mosque is a sin, and its expiation is to bury it." Agreed upon.

I say: The meaning of "burying it" is when the mosque floor is earth, sand, or the like, so one conceals it beneath its soil. Abū al-Maḥāsin al-Rūyānī, one of our companions, said in his book "al-Baḥr": It is also said that the meaning of "burying it" is to remove it from the mosque. However, if the mosque is paved with tiles or plastered, then rubbing it with one's sandal or otherwise — as many ignorant people do — that is not burial, but rather an increase in sin and an accumulation of filth in the mosque. Whoever does that must wipe it afterward with his garment, hand, or other means, or wash it.

And ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) saw mucus, spittle, or phlegm on the wall facing the qiblah, and he scraped it off. Agreed upon.

And Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "These mosques are not fit for any of this urine or filth; they are only for the remembrance of Allah the Exalted and the recitation of the Qurʾān" — or as the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said. Narrated by Muslim.

Section 310: Dislike of Quarreling in the Mosque, Raising One's Voice There, Announcing Lost Property, Buying and Selling, Leasing, and Similar Transactions

Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) said that he heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "Whoever hears a man announcing lost property in the mosque, let him say: 'May Allah not return it to you,' for the mosques were not built for this." Narrated by Muslim.

And from him: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "If you see someone buying or selling in the mosque, say: 'May Allah not profit your trade.' And if you see someone announcing lost property, say: 'May Allah not return it to you.'" Narrated by al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A good (ḥasan) hadith."

And Buraydah (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that a man announced in the mosque: "Who will guide me to the red camel?" The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "May you not find it; the mosques were only built for that for which they were built." Narrated by Muslim.

And ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather (may Allah be pleased with him), reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade buying and selling in the mosque, announcing lost property therein, or reciting poetry therein. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, who said: "A good (ḥasan) hadith."

And al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, the Companion (may Allah be pleased with him), said: I was in the mosque, and a man threw pebbles at me. I looked, and behold, it was ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him). He said: "Go and bring those two to me." I brought them to him. He said: "Where are you from?" They said: "From the people of al-Ṭāʾif." He said: "If you were from the people of this town, I would have hurt you. You raise your voices in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him)!" Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

Section 311: Prohibition of Entering the Mosque for One Who Has Eaten Garlic, Onion, Leek, or Anything Else with a Foul Odor, Before Its Smell Has Gone, Except Out of Necessity

Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) reported that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever..."
