- Root: ش ر ع (shar-ʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes a path to water, then a clear, well-trodden way; from it derives 'legislation' (sharīʿah) as the divinely ordained path.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sharʿ signifies the divine law revealed through prophets, distinguishing permissible (ḥalāl) from forbidden (ḥarām).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for the revealed law; metaphorically for any established normative practice.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The protasis (e.g., 'if one points') governs the apodosis ('angels curse him'), with the conditional particle 'man' (whoever) requiring a verb in the past tense for generality.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, used to say after every obligatory prayer: «There is no god but God alone, with no partner; His is the sovereignty and His is the praise, and He is over all things capable. O God, none can withhold what You have given, none can give what You have withheld, and no wealth or majesty (al-jadd) avails its possessor against You.» And it was conveyed to him (Muʿāwiyah) that he (the Prophet) used to forbid idle talk and gossip (qīla wa-qāla), wasting wealth, and excessive questioning; and he used to forbid disobedience to mothers, burying daughters alive, and refusing to give while demanding from others. Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim). Its explanation has preceded.

Section 357 — Prohibition of Pointing at a Muslim with a Weapon or Similar, Whether in Earnest or in Jest, and Prohibition of Handling an Unsheathed Sword

[1783] — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, from the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, who said: «Let none of you point at his brother with a weapon, for he does not know — perhaps Satan will snatch it from his hand, and he will fall into a pit of Hellfire.» Agreed upon.
In a narration by Muslim, he said: Abū al-Qāsim, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, said: «Whoever points at his brother with an iron implement, the angels curse him until he desists, even if he is his brother from his father and mother.»
His saying, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, «yanziʿa» (snatch) is recorded with the unpointed ʿayn and kasrah on the zāy, and also with the pointed ghayn and fatḥah; their meanings are close. With the unpointed ʿayn it means 'to throw', and with the pointed ghayn it also means 'to throw and to corrupt'. The origin of nazʿ is piercing and corruption.

[1784] — On the authority of Jābir, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, forbade handling an unsheathed sword. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, who said: 'A good (ḥasan) hadith.'

Section 358 — Dislike of Leaving the Mosque After the Call to Prayer (Adhān) Without an Excuse Until the Obligatory Prayer is Performed

[1785] — On the authority of Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ, who said: We were sitting with Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, in the mosque. The muezzin gave the call to prayer, and a man stood up from the mosque and walked out. Abū Hurayrah followed him with his gaze until he left the mosque, then said: 'As for this one, he has disobeyed Abū al-Qāsim, may God's blessings and peace be upon him.' Narrated by Muslim.

Section 359 — Dislike of Refusing Sweet Basil (rayḥān) Without an Excuse

[1786] — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, said: «Whoever is offered sweet basil, let him not refuse it, for it is light to carry and fragrant of scent.» Narrated by Muslim.

[1787] — On the authority of Anas ibn Mālik, may God be pleased with him: The Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, never refused perfume. Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

Section 360 — Dislike of Praising Someone to Their Face When Harm Is Feared from It, Such as Self-Admiration and the Like; and Its Permissibility for One Whose Safety from That Is Assured

[1788] — On the authority of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, heard a man praising another man and exaggerating in the praise. He said: «You have destroyed — or cut — the man's back.» Agreed upon.
'Exaggeration in praise' (al-iṭrāʾ) means going to excess in commendation.

[1789] — On the authority of Abū Bakrah, may God be pleased with him: A man was mentioned before the Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, and another man praised him well. The Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, said: «Woe to you! You have cut off your companion's neck!» — repeating it — «If one of you must praise, let him say: 'I reckon so-and-so to be such-and-such, if he thinks he is so — and God is his reckoner — and let him not declare anyone pure before God.» Agreed upon.

[1790] — On the authority of Hammām ibn al-Ḥārith, from al-Miqdād, may God be pleased with him: A man began to praise ʿUthmān, may God be pleased with him. Al-Miqdād deliberately knelt on his knees and began to throw gravel at his face. ʿUthmān said to him: 'What is the matter with you?' He replied: 'The Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, said: «When you see the praisers (al-maddāḥīn), throw dust in their faces.»' Narrated by Muslim.
These hadiths concern prohibition, and many authentic hadiths have come concerning permissibility.
The scholars said: The way to reconcile the hadiths is to say: If the one praised possesses complete faith and certainty, discipline of the soul, and full self-knowledge such that he will not be seduced, deceived, or played upon by his ego, then it is neither forbidden nor disliked. But if any of these things is feared for him, then praising him to his face is severely disliked. Upon this differentiation the various hadiths on this matter are to be interpreted.
Among what has come concerning permissibility is his saying, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, to Abū Bakr, may God be pleased with him: «I hope that you will be among them» — meaning among those who are called from all the gates of Paradise for its entry.
In the other hadith: «I am not of them» — meaning: I am not of those who drag their garments out of pride.
And he said, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, to ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him: «Satan never sees you taking a path except that he takes a path other than yours.»
The hadiths on permissibility are numerous, and I have mentioned a portion of their various aspects in the book «al-Adhkār».

Section 361 — Dislike of Leaving a Land Struck by Plague (wabāʾ) to Flee from It, and Dislike of Entering It
God, the Exalted, says: {«Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers of lofty construction»} [al-Nisāʾ: 78]. And He, the Exalted, says: {«And do not throw yourselves into destruction»} [al-Baqarah: 195].

[1791] — On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, set out for Syria until, when he was at Sargh, the commanders of the armies — Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ and his companions — met him and informed him that the plague had broken out in Syria. Ibn ʿAbbās said: ʿUmar said to me: 'Summon for me the early emigrants (al-muhājirūn al-awwalūn).' So I summoned them, and he consulted them and informed them that the plague had struck Syria. They differed. Some said: 'You have set out for a purpose, and we do not think you should turn back from it.'

chapters.title_en: Section 164 — On the Prohibition of Approaching a Plague-Stricken Land and the Severe Warning Against Sorcery, Along with Related Prohibitions
chapters.arabic_text:
بعضهم: معك بقية الناس وأصحاب رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ولا نرى أن

تقدمهم على هذا الوباء. فقال: ارتفعوا عني. ثم قال: ادع لي الأنصار،

فدعوتهم، فاستشارهم، فسلكوا سبيل المهاجرين، واختلفوا كاختلافهم، فقال:

ارتفعوا عني. ثم قال: ادع لي من كان هاهنا من مشيخة قريش من مهاجرة الفتح،

فدعوتهم، فلم يختلف عليه منهم رجلان، فقالوا: نرى أن ترجع بالناس، ولا

تقدمهم على هذا الوباء، فنادى عمر - رضي الله عنه - في الناس: إني مصبح على

ظهر، فأصبحوا عليه، فقال أبو عبيدة بن الجراح - رضي الله عنه: أفرارا من

قدر الله؟ فقال عمر - رضي الله عنه: لو غيرك قالها يا أبا عبيدة! - وكان

عمر يكره خلافه - نعم، نفر من قدر الله إلى قدر الله، أرأيت لو كان لك إبل،

فهبطت واديا له عدوتان،  إحداهما خصبة، والأخرى جدبة، أليس إن رعيت الخصبة

رعيتها بقدر الله، وإن رعيت الجدبة رعيتها بقدر الله؟ قال: فجاء عبد

الرحمان بن عوف - رضي الله عنه - وكان متغيبا في بعض حاجته، فقال: إن عندي

من هذا

| [ص: 498]
# علما، سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يقول: «إذا سمعتم به بأرض

فلا تقدموا عليه، وإذا وقع بأرض وأنتم بها فلا تخرجوا فرارا منه» فحمد الله

تعالى عمر - رضي الله عنه - وانصرف. متفق عليه. (2)
# و «العدوة»: جانب الوادي.

| 1792 - 
# وعن أسامة بن زيد - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«إذا سمعتم الطاعون (1) بأرض، فلا تدخلوها، وإذا وقع بأرض، وأنتم فيها، فلا

تخرجوا منها». متفق عليه. (2)

$ 362 - باب التغليظ في تحريم السحر
# قال الله تعالى: {وما كفر سليمان ولكن الشياطين كفروا يعلمون الناس

السحر} [البقرة: 102].
#

| 1793 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«اجتنبوا السبع الموبقات». قالوا: يا رسول الله، وما هن؟ قال: «الشرك

بالله، والسحر، وقتل النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق، وأكل الربا، وأكل مال

اليتيم، والتولي يوم الزحف؛ وقذف المحصنات المؤمنات الغافلات». متفق عليه.

(1)

$ 363 - باب النهي عن المسافرة بالمصحف إلى بلاد الكفار إذا خيف وقوعه بأيدي العدو

| 1794 - 
# عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، قال: نهى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

أن يسافر بالقرآن إلى أرض العدو. متفق عليه. (1)

$ 364 - باب تحريم استعمال إناء الذهب وإناء الفضة في الأكل والشرب والطهارة وسائر وجوه الاستعمال

| 1795 - 
# عن أم سلمة رضي الله عنها: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«الذي يشرب في آنية الفضة، إنما يجرجر (1) في بطنه نار جهنم» متفق عليه.

(2)
# وفي رواية لمسلم: «إن الذي يأكل أو يشرب في آنية الفضة والذهب».

| 1796 - 
# وعن حذيفة - رضي الله عنه - قال: إن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - نهانا

عن الحرير، والديباج، والشرب في آنية الذهب والفضة، وقال: «هن لهم في

الدنيا، وهي لكم في الآخرة». متفق عليه. (1)
# وفي  رواية في الصحيحين عن حذيفة - رضي الله عنه: سمعت رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - يقول: «لا تلبسوا الحرير ولا الديباج، ولا تشربوا في آنية

الذهب والفضة ولا تأكلوا في صحافها».

| 1797 - 
# وعن أنس بن سيرين، قال: كنت مع أنس بن مالك - رضي الله عنه - عند نفر من

المجوس؛ فجيء بفالوذج (1) على إناء من فضة، فلم يأكله، فقيل له: حوله،

فحوله على إناء من خلنج وجيء به فأكله. رواه البيهقي بإسناد حسن. (2)
# «الخلنج»: الجفنة (3).

$ 365 - باب تحريم لبس الرجل ثوبا مزعفرا

| 1798 - 
# عن أنس - رضي الله عنه - قال: نهى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن

يتزعفر (1) الرجل. متفق عليه. (2)

| 1799 - 
# وعن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما، قال: رأى النبي - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - علي ثوبين معصفرين، فقال: «أمك أمرتك بهذا؟» (1) قلت:

أغسلهما؟ قال: «بل أحرقهما».
# وفي رواية، فقال: «إن هذا من ثياب الكفار فلا تلبسها». رواه مسلم. (2)

$ 366 - باب النهي عن صمت يوم إلى الليل

| 1800 - 
# عن علي - رضي الله عنه - قال: حفظت عن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«لا يتم بعد احتلام، ولا صمات يوم إلى الليل». رواه أبو داود بإسناد حسن.

(1)
# قال الخطابي (2) في تفسير هذا الحديث: كان من نسك الجاهلية الصمات. فنهوا

في الإسلام عن ذلك وأمروا بالذكر والحديث بالخير.

| 1801 - 
# وعن قيس بن أبي حازم، قال: دخل أبو بكر الصديق - رضي الله عنه - على

امرأة من أحمس يقال لها: زينب، فرآها لا تتكلم. فقال: ما لها لا تتكلم؟

فقالوا: حجت مصمتة، فقال لها: تكلمي، فإن هذا لا يحل، هذا من عمل الجاهلية،

فتكلمت. رواه البخاري. (1)

$ 367 - باب تحريم انتساب الإنسان إلى غير أبيه وتوليه إلى غير مواليه

| 1802 - 
# عن سعد بن أبي وقاص - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

قال: «من ادعى إلى غير أبيه وهو يعلم أنه غير أبيه، فالجنة عليه حرام» (1).

متفق عليه. (2)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ب-أ (w-b-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Pestilence, widespread affliction; a land stricken by epidemic disease.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A divinely decreed calamity; theological context frames it as qadar (divine decree) testing human trust (tawakkul) and obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical plague; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual corruption, as in sorcery's harm.
- Root: س-ح-ر (s-ḥ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Deception, illusion; anything whose cause is hidden; sorcery as a false reality.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Acts of jinn or incantations producing illusory effects; kufr (disbelief) when practiced, as per Quranic context.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the act; metaphorical for eloquent speech that "enchants" hearts (as in ḥadīth "min al-bayān la-sihran").
- Root: م-و-ت (m-w-t) [implied in "الموبقات"]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Death; "mūbiqāt" — destructive sins leading to perdition.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Acts that destroy one's afterlife (ākhirah), akin to spiritual death.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal death vs. metaphorical ruin of the soul.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — "If you hear... do not enter" (idhā samiʿtum... fa-lā tadkhulūhā); the protasis (condition) governs the apodosis (command), requiring immediate obedience without deliberation.
chapters.translation:
Some of them said: "With you are the rest of the people and the companions of the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — and we do not see that you should advance them into this plague." He (ʿUmar) said: "Withdraw from me." Then he said: "Call the Anṣār to me." So I called them, and he consulted them, and they followed the path of the Muhājirūn, differing among themselves as they had differed. He said: "Withdraw from me." Then he said: "Call to me whoever is here of the elders of Quraysh, from the emigrants of the Conquest (of Mecca)." So I called them, and not two men among them differed with him. They said: "We see that you should return the people, and not advance them into this plague." So ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with him — called out to the people: "I shall set out in the morning upon a mount, so you should also set out in the morning upon mounts." Then Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ — may Allah be pleased with him — said: "Is this a flight from the decree of Allah?" ʿUmar said: "Were it someone other than you who said this, O Abū ʿUbaydah!" — and ʿUmar disliked opposing him — "Yes, we flee from the decree of Allah to the decree of Allah. Consider: if you had camels and you descended into a valley having two sides — one fertile and the other barren — would you not, if you grazed them on the fertile side, graze them by the decree of Allah, and if you grazed them on the barren side, graze them by the decree of Allah?" He said: Then ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf — may Allah be pleased with him — came, having been absent for some of his needs, and said: "I have knowledge of this matter. I heard the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — say: {«If you hear of it (the plague) in a land, do not advance upon it, and if it occurs in a land while you are in it, do not flee from it»}." So ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with him — praised Allah and departed. Agreed upon (by al-Bukhārī and Muslim). (2)
And "al-ʿudwah" (in the narration) means: the side of the valley.

1792 — And from Usāmah ibn Zayd — may Allah be pleased with him — from the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — who said: {«If you hear of the plague (ṭāʿūn) in a land, do not enter it, and if it occurs in a land while you are in it, do not leave it»}. Agreed upon. (2)

Section 362 — On the Severe Warning Against the Prohibition of Sorcery
Allah the Exalted said: {«And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery»} [al-Baqarah: 102].

1793 — And from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — from the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — who said: "Avoid the seven destructive sins (al-mūbiqāt)." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah (shirk), sorcery (siḥr), killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, consuming usury (ribā), consuming the wealth of an orphan, turning one's back on the day of advance (in battle), and slandering chaste, believing, heedless women." Agreed upon. (1)

Section 363 — On the Prohibition of Traveling with the Muṣḥaf to the Lands of the Disbelievers When There is Fear of It Falling into the Hands of the Enemy
1794 — From Ibn ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with them both — who said: The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — forbade traveling with the Qurʾān to the land of the enemy. Agreed upon. (1)

Section 364 — On the Prohibition of Using Vessels of Gold and Vessels of Silver for Eating, Drinking, Purification, and All Other Forms of Use
1795 — From Umm Salamah — may Allah be pleased with her — that the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: "The one who drinks in vessels of silver only gurgles into his belly the fire of Hell." Agreed upon. (2)
In a narration of Muslim: "Indeed, the one who eats or drinks in vessels of silver and gold."

1796 — And from Ḥudhayfah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — forbade us from silk (al-ḥarīr), brocade (al-dībāj), and drinking in vessels of gold and silver, and said: "They are for them in this world, and for you in the Hereafter." Agreed upon. (1)
In a narration in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from Ḥudhayfah — may Allah be pleased with him: I heard the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — say: "Do not wear silk or brocade, do not drink in vessels of gold and silver, and do not eat in their plates."

1797 — And from Anas ibn Sīrīn, who said: I was with Anas ibn Mālik — may Allah be pleased with him — among a group of Magians; a pudding (fālūdhaj) was brought on a silver vessel, and he did not eat it. It was said to him: "Transfer it." So he transferred it to a vessel of khilnaj (a type of wood), and it was brought, and he ate it. Narrated by al-Bayhaqī with a good (ḥasan) chain. (2)
"Al-khilnaj" means: a large bowl (jafnah).

Section 365 — On the Prohibition of a Man Wearing a Garment Dyed with Saffron (muʿaṣfar)
1798 — From Anas — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — forbade a man from dyeing himself with saffron (yatazaʿfar). Agreed upon. (2)

1799 — And from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ — may Allah be pleased with them both — who said: The Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — saw two saffron-dyed garments on me and said: "Did your mother command you to do this?" I said: "Shall I wash them?" He said: "Rather, burn them." In another narration, he said: "Indeed, this is from the garments of the disbelievers, so do not wear them." Narrated by Muslim. (2)

Section 366 — On the Prohibition of Silence (ṣumāt) from Day to Night
1800 — From ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: I preserved from the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "There is no (valid) vow of silence after puberty, and no silence (ṣumāt) from day to night." Narrated by Abū Dāwūd with a good (ḥasan) chain. (1)
Al-Khaṭṭābī (2) said in interpreting this ḥadīth: "Silence (al-ṣumāt) was among the devotional practices of the Jāhiliyyah. They were forbidden from that in Islam and commanded to engage in remembrance (dhikr) and speaking of good."

1801 — And from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, who said: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq — may Allah be pleased with him — entered upon a woman from Aḥmas called Zaynab, and saw her not speaking. He said: "What is wrong with her that she does not speak?" They said: "She performed the pilgrimage in silence (muṣmittah)." He said to her: "Speak, for this is not permissible; this is from the deeds of the Jāhiliyyah." So she spoke. Narrated by al-Bukhārī. (1)

Section 367 — On the Prohibition of a Person Attributing Himself to Other Than His Father, and Claiming Loyalty (walāʾ) to Other Than His Patrons
1802 — From Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ — may Allah be pleased with him — that the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: "Whoever claims (lineage) to other than his father, knowing that it is not his father, Paradise is forbidden to him." (1) Agreed upon. (2)

chapters.title_en: Section 165 — The Prohibition of Renouncing One's Lineage, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
| 1803 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم  - قال:

«لا ترغبوا عن آبائكم، فمن رغب عن أبيه، فهو كفر». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1804 - 
# وعن يزيد بن شريك بن طارق، قال: رأيت عليا - رضي الله عنه - على المنبر

يخطب، فسمعته يقول: لا والله ما عندنا من كتاب نقرؤه إلا كتاب الله، وما في

هذه الصحيفة (1)، فنشرها فإذا فيها أسنان الإبل، وأشياء من الجراحات،

وفيها: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «المدينة حرم ما بين عير إلى

ثور، فمن أحدث فيها حدثا، أو آوى محدثا، فعليه لعنة الله والملائكة والناس

أجمعين، لا يقبل الله منه يوم القيامة صرفا ولا عدلا. ذمة المسلمين واحدة،

يسعى بها أدناهم، فمن أخفر مسلما، فعليه لعنة الله والملائكة والناس

أجمعين، لا يقبل الله منه يوم القيامة صرفا ولا عدلا. ومن ادعى إلى غير

أبيه، أو انتمى إلى غير مواليه، فعليه لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين؛

لا يقبل الله منه يوم القيامة صرفا ولا عدلا». متفق عليه. (2)
# «ذمة المسلمين» أي: عهدهم وأمانتهم. «وأخفره»: نقض عهده.
# «والصرف»: التوبة، وقيل الحيلة. «والعدل»: الفداء.

| 1805 - 
# وعن أبي ذر - رضي الله عنه: أنه سمع رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

يقول: «ليس من رجل ادعى لغير أبيه وهو يعلمه إلا كفر، ومن ادعى ما ليس له،

فليس منا، وليتبوأ مقعده من

| [ص: 502]
# النار، ومن دعا رجلا بالكفر، أو قال: عدو الله، وليس كذلك إلا حار (1)

عليه». متفق عليه، وهذا لفظ رواية مسلم. (2)

$ 368 - باب التحذير من ارتكاب ما نهى الله - عز وجل - أو رسوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عنه
# قال الله تعالى: {فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره أن تصيبهم فتنة أو يصيبهم

عذاب أليم} [النور: 63]، وقال تعالى: {ويحذركم الله نفسه} [آل عمران: 30]،

وقال تعالى: {إن بطش ربك لشديد} [البروج: 12]، وقال تعالى: {وكذلك أخذ ربك

إذا أخذ القرى وهي ظالمة إن أخذه أليم شديد? [هود: 102].
#

| 1806 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «إن

الله تعالى يغار، وغيرة الله، أن يأتي المرء ما حرم الله  عليه». متفق عليه.

(1)

$ 369 - باب ما يقوله ويفعله من ارتكب منهيا عنه
# قال الله تعالى: {وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله} [فصلت: 36]،

وقال تعالى: {إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم

مبصرون} [الأعراف: 201]، وقال تعالى: {والذين إذا فعلوا فاحشة أو ظلموا

أنفسهم ذكروا الله فاستغفروا لذنوبهم ومن يغفر الذنوب إلا الله ولم يصروا

على ما فعلوا وهم يعلمون أولئك جزاؤهم مغفرة من ربهم وجنات تجري من تحتها

الأنهار خالدين فيها ونعم أجر العاملين} [آل عمران: 135 - 136]، وقال

تعالى: {وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيها المؤمنون لعلكم تفلحون} [النور: 31].
#

| 1807 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«من حلف فقال في حلفه: باللات والعزى (1)، فليقل: لا إله إلا الله، ومن قال

لصاحبه: تعال أقامرك فليتصدق».متفق عليه. (2)

| (18) - كتاب المنثورات والملح 
# (1)

$ 370 - باب أحاديث الدجال وأشراط الساعة وغيرها

| 1808 - 
# عن النواس بن سمعان - رضي الله عنه - قال: ذكر رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - الدجال ذات غداة، فخفض فيه ورفع حتى ظنناه في طائفة النخل. فلما

رحنا إليه، عرف ذلك فينا، فقال: «ما شأنكم؟» قلنا: يا رسول الله، ذكرت

الدجال الغداة، فخفضت فيه ورفعت، حتى ظنناه في طائفة النخل، فقال: «غير

الدجال أخوفني عليكم، إن يخرج وأنا فيكم، فأنا حجيجه دونكم؛ وإن يخرج ولست

فيكم، فامرؤ حجيج نفسه، والله خليفتي على كل مسلم. إنه شاب قطط عينه طافية

(2)، كأني أشبهه بعبد العزى بن قطن، فمن أدركه منكم، فليقرأ عليه فواتح

سورة الكهف (3)؛ إنه خارج خلة بين الشام والعراق، فعاث يمينا وعاث شمالا،

يا عباد الله فاثبتوا» قلنا: يا رسول الله، وما لبثه في الأرض؟ قال:

«أربعون يوما: يوم كسنة، ويوم كشهر، ويوم كجمعة، وسائر أيامه كأيامكم»

قلنا: يا رسول الله، فذلك اليوم الذي كسنة أتكفينا فيه صلاة يوم؟ قال: «لا،

اقدروا له قدره». قلنا: يا رسول الله، وما إسراعه في الأرض؟ قال: «كالغيث

استدبرته الريح، فيأتي على القوم، فيدعوهم فيؤمنون به ويستجيبون له،  فيأمر

السماء فتمطر، والأرض فتنبت، فتروح عليهم سارحتهم أطول ما كانت ذرى

# وأسبغه ضروعا، وأمده خواصر، ثم يأتي القوم فيدعوهم، فيردون عليه قوله،

فينصرف عنهم، فيصبحون ممحلين ليس بأيديهم شيء من أموالهم، ويمر بالخربة،

فيقول لها: أخرجي كنوزك، فتتبعه كنوزها كيعاسيب النحل، ثم يدعو رجلا ممتلئا

شبابا فيضربه بالسيف، فيقطعه جزلتين رمية الغرض، ثم يدعوه، فيقبل، ويتهلل

وجهه يضحك، فبينما هو كذلك إذ بعث الله تعالى المسيح ابن مريم - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - فينزل عند المنارة البيضاء شرقي دمشق بين مهرودتين، واضعا كفيه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-غ-ب (r-gh-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To desire, incline toward, or turn away from; the core sense involves aversion and turning aside from something.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, renunciation (rugūb) of one's father implies a rejection of divinely ordained social and legal bonds, tantamount to disbelief in its severest form.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes physical turning away; here it is metaphorical (majāz) for disavowing legal paternity and kinship obligations.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (Jumla Shartiyya) — The protasis "man raghiba" (whoever renounces) is followed by an apodosis "fahuwa kufr" (it is disbelief), establishing a legal-moral equivalence.

- Root: ذ-م-م (dh-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Blame, censure; also covenant, protection, and security (dhimmah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The "dhimmah" of Muslims denotes a collective sacred pact of protection and mutual guarantee, binding on all.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is blameworthiness; here it is a transferred (majāz) usage for the inviolable covenant of security.
- Sībawayh Rule: Apposition (Badal) — The gloss "ay: ʿahduhum wa-amānatuhum" (i.e., their covenant and security) is explanatory apposition, clarifying the technical term.

- Root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To forbid, make sacred, or declare inviolable; the sanctuary (ḥaram) of Medina is a protected zone.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine prohibition (taḥrīm) establishes a sacred boundary; violating it incurs curse and rejection of atonement.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage for physical sanctuary; metaphorical for the spiritual sanctity of communal bonds.
- Sībawayh Rule: Emphatic Negation (Nafy al-Jins) — "lā yuqbal Allāhu minhu ṣarfan wa-lā ʿadlan" (God will not accept from him any compensation or ransom) uses the absolute negation to stress total rejection.
chapters.translation:
**1803** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said:

«Do not renounce your fathers; for whoever renounces his father, it is an act of disbelief.» Agreed upon (by al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

**1804** — On the authority of Yazīd ibn Sharīk ibn Ṭāriq, who said: I saw ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) upon the pulpit delivering a sermon, and I heard him say: "No, by God, we have no book that we recite except the Book of God, and what is in this scroll." He then unfolded it, and behold, it contained [rulings on] the teeth of camels and matters concerning wounds. And in it [was written]: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Medina is a sacred sanctuary from ʿAyr to Thawr. Whoever introduces therein an innovation (ḥadath), or shelters an innovator, upon him is the curse of God, the angels, and all mankind; God will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any compensation (ṣarf) nor ransom (ʿadl). The covenant (dhimmah) of the Muslims is one; the lowest of them may grant protection on their behalf. Whoever breaches the covenant of a Muslim, upon him is the curse of God, the angels, and all mankind; God will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any compensation nor ransom. And whoever claims lineage to other than his father, or affiliates himself to other than his patrons (mawālī), upon him is the curse of God, the angels, and all mankind; God will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any compensation nor ransom.» Agreed upon.

[The commentator says:] "The covenant (dhimmah) of the Muslims" means: their pact and their security. "And whoever breaches it (akhfara)" means: violates his pact. "And al-ṣarf" means: repentance; it is also said: a stratagem. "And al-ʿadl" means: the ransom.

**1805** — On the authority of Abū Dharr (may God be pleased with him): that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: «There is no man who claims lineage to other than his father while knowing it, except that he has committed disbelief. And whoever claims what is not his, he is not of us; let him take his seat in the Fire. And whoever calls a man an unbeliever, or says: "O enemy of God," when he is not so, it recoils upon him.» Agreed upon, and this is the wording of Muslim's narration.

**Section 368 — The Warning Against Committing What God (Mighty and Majestic) or His Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) Has Forbidden**

God the Exalted said: {«So let those who oppose his command beware, lest a trial befall them or a painful punishment afflict them»} [al-Nūr 24:63]. And He said: {«And God warns you of Himself»} [Āl ʿImrān 3:30]. And He said: {«Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe»} [al-Burūj 85:12]. And He said: {«And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing — indeed, His seizure is painful and severe»} [Hūd 11:102].

**1806** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him): that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Indeed, God the Exalted is jealous, and the jealousy of God is that a person commits what God has forbidden upon him.» Agreed upon.

**Section 369 — What One Who Has Committed a Forbidden Act Should Say and Do**

God the Exalted said: {«And if an evil whisper from Satan tries to divert you, then seek refuge in God»} [Fuṣṣilat 41:36]. And He said: {«Indeed, those who fear God — when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember [Him], and at once they have insight»} [al-Aʿrāf 7:201]. And He said: {«And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins — and who forgives sins except God? — and do not persist in what they did while they know. Those — their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally; and excellent is the reward of the workers»} [Āl ʿImrān 3:135–136]. And He said: {«And turn to God in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you might succeed»} [al-Nūr 24:31].

**1807** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: «Whoever swears an oath and says in his oath: "By al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā," let him say: "There is no god but God." And whoever says to his companion: "Come, let us gamble with you," let him give in charity.» Agreed upon.

**Book 18 — Miscellaneous Narrations and Anecdotes**

**Section 370 — Hadiths Concerning the Dajjāl, the Portents of the Hour, and Other Matters**

**1808** — On the authority of al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) mentioned the Dajjāl one morning, and he spoke of him with belittlement and exaggeration until we thought he was in a cluster of palm trees. When we returned to him, he perceived that in us, and said: «What is the matter with you?» We said: O Messenger of God, you mentioned the Dajjāl this morning, and you spoke of him with belittlement and exaggeration until we thought he was in a cluster of palm trees. He said: «Other than the Dajjāl, I fear for you more. If he emerges while I am among you, then I shall be his disputant on your behalf; and if he emerges while I am not among you, then each man shall be his own disputant, and God is my successor over every Muslim. Indeed, he is a young man with curly hair, with a protruding eye, as if I liken him to ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn Qaṭan. Whoever among you reaches him, let him recite upon him the opening verses of Sūrat al-Kahf. Indeed, he will emerge from a gap between Syria and Iraq, and he will wreak havoc right and left. O servants of God, be steadfast.» We said: O Messenger of God, and how long will he remain on the earth? He said: «Forty days: a day like a year, a day like a month, a day like a week, and the rest of his days like your days.» We said: O Messenger of God, that day which is like a year — will the prayer of one day suffice us therein? He said: «No, measure it according to its due proportion.» We said: O Messenger of God, and what is his speed upon the earth? He said: «Like rain driven by the wind. He will come upon a people and call them, and they will believe in him and respond to him. He will command the sky, and it will rain; and the earth, and it will sprout. Their livestock will return to them with the tallest humps, the fullest udders, and the most distended flanks. Then he will come upon a people and call them, and they will reject his words, so he will turn away from them, and they will wake up destitute, with nothing of their wealth in their hands. And he will pass by a ruin and say to it: "Bring forth your treasures," and its treasures will follow him like swarms of bees. Then he will call a man full of youth, and strike him with the sword, cutting him into two pieces the distance of an archery target. Then he will call him, and he will come forward, his face beaming with joy and laughing. And while he is in that state, God the Exalted will send the Messiah, son of Mary (peace be upon him), and he will descend at the white minaret east of Damascus, between two garments, placing his palms...»

chapters.arabic_text:
على أجنحة ملكين، إذا طأطأ رأسه قطر، وإذا رفعه تحدر منه جمان كاللؤلؤ، فلا

يحل لكافر يجد ريح نفسه إلا مات، ونفسه ينتهي إلى حيث ينتهي طرفه، فيطلبه

حتى يدركه بباب لد (1) فيقتله، ثم يأتي عيسى - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قوما

قد عصمهم الله منه، فيمسح عن وجوههم ويحدثهم بدرجاتهم في الجنة، فبينما هو

كذلك إذ أوحى الله تعالى إلى عيسى - صلى الله عليه وسلم: أني قد أخرجت

عبادا لي لا يدان لأحد بقتالهم، فحرز عبادي إلى الطور. ويبعث الله يأجوج

ومأجوج وهم من كل حدب ينسلون، فيمر أوائلهم على بحيرة طبرية فيشربون ما

فيها، ويمر آخرهم فيقولون: لقد كان بهذه مرة ماء، ويحصر نبي الله عيسى -

صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأصحابه حتى يكون رأس الثور لأحدهم خيرا من مئة دينار

لأحدكم اليوم، فيرغب نبي الله عيسى - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأصحابه - رضي

الله عنهم - إلى الله تعالى، فيرسل الله تعالى عليهم النغف في رقابهم،

فيصبحون فرسى كموت نفس واحدة، ثم يهبط نبي الله عيسى - صلى الله عليه وسلم

- وأصحابه - رضي الله عنهم - إلى الأرض، فلا يجدون في الأرض موضع شبر إلا

ملأه زهمهم ونتنهم، فيرغب نبي الله عيسى - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأصحابه -

رضي الله عنهم - إلى الله تعالى، فيرسل الله تعالى طيرا كأعناق البخت،

فتحملهم، فتطرحهم حيث شاء الله، ثم يرسل الله - عز وجل - مطرا لا يكن منه

بيت مدر ولا وبر، فيغسل الأرض حتى  يتركها كالزلقة، ثم يقال للأرض: أنبتي

ثمرتك، وردي بركتك، فيومئذ تأكل العصابة من الرمانة، ويستظلون بقحفها،

ويبارك في الرسل حتى أن اللقحة من الإبل لتكفي الفئام من الناس؛ واللقحة من

البقر لتكفي القبيلة من الناس، واللقحة من الغنم لتكفي الفخذ من الناس؛

فبينما هم كذلك إذ بعث الله تعالى ريحا طيبة فتأخذهم تحت آباطهم

# فتقبض روح كل مؤمن وكل مسلم؛ ويبقى شرار الناس يتهارجون فيها تهارج

الحمر، فعليهم تقوم الساعة». رواه مسلم. (1)
# قوله: «خلة بين الشام والعراق»: أي طريقا بينهما. وقوله: «عاث» بالعين

المهملة والثاء المثلثة، والعيث: أشد الفساد. «والذرى»: بضم الذال المعجمة

وهو أعالي الأسنمة وهو جمع ذروة بضم الذال وكسرها «واليعاسيب»: ذكور النحل.

«وجزلتين»: أي قطعتين، «والغرض»: الهدف الذي يرمى إليه بالنشاب، أي: يرميه

رمية كرمية النشاب إلى الهدف. «والمهرودة» بالدال المهملة والمعجمة، وهي:

الثوب المصبوغ. قوله: «لا يدان»: أي لا طاقة. «والنغف»: دود. «وفرسى»: جمع

فريس، وهو القتيل. و «الزلقة»: بفتح الزاي واللام وبالقاف، وروي: الزلفة

بضم الزاي وإسكان اللام وبالفاء وهي المرآة. «والعصابة»: الجماعة. «والرسل»

بكسر الراء: اللبن. «واللقحة»: اللبون. «والفئام» بكسر الفاء وبعدها همزة

ممدودة: الجماعة. «والفخذ» من الناس: دون القبيلة.

| 1809 - 
# وعن ربعي بن حراش، قال: انطلقت مع أبي مسعود الأنصاري إلى حذيفة بن

اليمان - رضي الله عنهم - فقال له أبو مسعود: حدثني ما سمعت من رسول الله -

صلى الله عليه وسلم - في الدجال، قال: «إن الدجال يخرج، وإن معه ماء ونارا،

فأما الذي يراه الناس ماء فنار تحرق، وأما الذي يراه الناس نارا، فماء بارد

عذب. فمن أدركه منكم، فليقع في الذي يراه نارا، فإنه ماء عذب طيب» فقال أبو

مسعود: وأنا قد سمعته. متفق عليه. (1)

| 1810 - 
# وعن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما، قال: قال رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم: «يخرج الدجال في أمتي فيمكث أربعين، لا أدري أربعين يوما

أو أربعين شهرا، أو أربعين عاما، فيبعث الله تعالى عيسى ابن مريم - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - فيطلبه فيهلكه،  ثم يمكث الناس سبع سنين ليس بين اثنين

عداوة، ثم يرسل الله - عز وجل - ريحا باردة من قبل الشام، فلا يبقى على وجه

الأرض أحد في قلبه مثقال ذرة من خير أو إيمان إلا قبضته، حتى لو أن أحدكم

دخل في كبد جبل، لدخلته عليه حتى تقبضه، فيبقى شرار الناس في خفة الطير،

وأحلام السباع، لا يعرفون معروفا، ولا ينكرون منكرا، فيتمثل لهم الشيطان،

فيقول:

# ألا تستجيبون؟ فيقولون: فما تأمرنا؟ فيأمرهم بعبادة الأوثان، وهم في ذلك

دار رزقهم، حسن عيشهم، ثم ينفخ في الصور، فلا يسمعه أحد إلا أصغى ليتا ورفع

ليتا، وأول من يسمعه رجل يلوط (1) حوض إبله فيصعق ويصعق الناس حوله، ثم

يرسل الله -أو قال: ينزل الله - مطرا كأنه الطل أو الظل، فتنبت منه أجساد

الناس، ثم ينفخ فيه أخرى فإذا هم قيام ينظرون، ثم يقال: يا أيها الناس هلم

إلى ربكم، وقفوهم إنهم مسئولون، ثم يقال: أخرجوا بعث النار فيقال: من كم؟

فيقال: من كل ألف تسعمئة وتسعة وتسعين؛ فذلك يوم يجعل الولدان شيبا، وذلك

يوم يكشف عن ساق». رواه مسلم. (2)
# «الليت»: صفحة العنق. ومعناه يضع صفحة عنقه ويرفع صفحته الأخرى.

| 1811 - 
# وعن أنس - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ليس

من بلد إلا سيطؤه الدجال إلا مكة والمدينة؛ وليس نقب من أنقابهما إلا عليه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ص-م (ʿ-ṣ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To protect, guard, or preserve from harm; to hold back or restrain.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine protection (ʿiṣmah) from sin or affliction; here, God's safeguarding of a believing remnant from the Dajjāl's trial.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of physical restraint; metaphorical sense of spiritual preservation from fitnah.
- Root: ح-ش-ر (ḥ-sh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To gather, assemble, or muster a multitude.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The eschatological gathering (ḥashr) of creation for reckoning; here, the mustering of Gog and Magog.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal herding of beasts; metaphorical for the compelled assembly of nations by divine decree.
- Root: ق-ب-ض (q-b-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To seize, grasp, or take hold of; to contract.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The taking of the soul at death (qabḍ al-rūḥ); divine seizure of the faithful via a fragrant wind.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical grip; metaphorical for the angelic extraction of the spirit.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Temporal Clauses (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The particle "idhā" introduces a temporal-conditional clause where the protasis (e.g., "when he lowers his head") is followed by an apodosis (e.g., "it drips"), requiring precise coordination of verb tenses for narrative sequence.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) informed us of the Dajjāl's emergence and his trials, and of what God, Glorified and Exalted, will manifest through him. Among the hadiths on this is the one transmitted by Muslim from al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān (may God be pleased with him), in which the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, describing the Dajjāl: "He will come upon a people, and he will call them, and they will believe in him and respond to him. Then he will command the sky, and it will rain, and the earth, and it will sprout. Then he will pass by a people, and he will call them, and they will refuse his call, so he will turn away from them, and they will be afflicted with drought, having nothing in their hands of wealth. Then he will traverse the earth like a swift cloud, and he will say to a people: 'Do you see that I have killed their man and revived him for you?' — referring to a young man he had killed and then revived. Then he will pass by the people of a monastery and say: 'Bring out your martyr.' But they will not bring out anyone. Then he will come to a people, and he will call them, and they will respond to him. Then he will say: 'Do you see that I have killed their man and revived him?' — and he will kill a man and revive him. Then he will say: 'By God, I am your lord.' And a man from among them will say: 'You are not my lord, but you are the Dajjāl, the liar, whom we have been told about.' So he will say to him: 'If I kill this man and revive him, will you then doubt the matter?' They will say: 'No.' So he will kill him and revive him. Then the man will say: 'By God, I have never been more certain of you than I am today.' So the Dajjāl will seek to kill him, but he will not be given power over him. Then he will come to a woman, and he will say: 'I am your lord.' She will say: 'You are a liar.' So he will seize her, and she will be unable to resist him. Then he will come to a barren land and say to it: 'Bring forth your treasures.' So its treasures will follow him like swarms of bees. Then he will call a young man in the prime of youth, and he will strike him with a sword, cutting him in two, then he will place the two pieces at a distance like the target of an archer, then he will call him, and he will come forward, his face beaming with laughter. So while he is in that state, God, Glorified and Exalted, will send the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him). He will descend at the white minaret to the east of Damascus, wearing two garments lightly dyed with saffron, placing his hands on the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, it will drip, and when he raises it, pearls like beads will fall from it. It is not lawful for any disbeliever who smells his breath to remain alive, and his breath reaches as far as his eye can see. So he will pursue him until he overtakes him at the gate of Ludd and kills him. Then Jesus (peace be upon him) will come to a people whom God has protected from him, and he will wipe their faces and inform them of their ranks in Paradise. While he is thus engaged, God, Glorified and Exalted, will reveal to Jesus (peace be upon him): 'I have brought forth servants of Mine whom none has the power to fight, so take My servants to the Mount.' And God will send Gog and Magog, and they will pour down from every elevated place. Their first wave will pass by the Lake of Tiberias and drink all that is in it, and their last wave will pass by and say: 'There was water here once.' And the Prophet of God, Jesus (peace be upon him), and his companions will be besieged until the head of an ox becomes better for one of them than a hundred dinars is for one of you today. So the Prophet of God, Jesus (peace be upon him), and his companions (may God be pleased with them) will supplicate to God, Glorified and Exalted, and God will send upon them the maggots (al-naghaf) in their necks, and they will become dead corpses, as one soul dying. Then the Prophet of God, Jesus (peace be upon him), and his companions will descend to the earth, and they will not find a handspan of ground that is not filled with their stench and filth. So the Prophet of God, Jesus (peace be upon him), and his companions will supplicate to God, Glorified and Exalted, and God will send birds like the necks of Bactrian camels, and they will carry them and cast them wherever God wills. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, will send rain that no clay house nor woolen tent can withhold, and it will wash the earth until it leaves it like a mirror (al-zalaqah). Then it will be said to the earth: 'Bring forth your fruit and restore your blessing.' On that day, a group (al-ʿiṣābah) will eat from a single pomegranate and seek shade in its husk. And blessing will be placed in milk (al-rusl), such that a milch camel (al-laqaḥah) will suffice a large company (al-fīʾām) of people, a milch cow will suffice a tribe (al-qabīlah), and a milch sheep will suffice a clan (al-fakhdh). While they are thus, God, Glorified and Exalted, will send a pleasant wind that will seize them under their armpits and take the soul of every believer and every Muslim. And the wickedest of people will remain, fornicating among themselves like donkeys, and upon them the Hour will be established." Narrated by Muslim.

His saying: "A road between Syria and Iraq" — meaning a path between them. His saying: "ʿātha" (with the unpointed ʿayn and the triple-pointed thāʾ) — and al-ʿayth is the most severe corruption. "Al-dhurā" (with ḍammah on the dhāl) — the upper parts of the humps, plural of dhurawah (with ḍammah or kasrah on the dhāl). "Al-yaʿāsīb" — the male bees. "Jazlatayn" — meaning two pieces. "Al-gharaḍ" — the target at which arrows are shot, i.e., he shoots him with a shot like an arrow's shot to the target. "Al-mahruwdah" (with the unpointed dāl or the pointed one) — the dyed garment. His saying: "Lā yadān" — meaning no power. "Al-naghaf" — worms. "Farsā" — plural of farīs, meaning the slain. "Al-zalaqah" (with fatḥah on the zāy and lām, and qāf) — and it is also narrated as al-zulfah (with ḍammah on the zāy, sukūn on the lām, and fāʾ), which is the mirror. "Al-ʿiṣābah" — the group. "Al-rusl" (with kasrah on the rāʾ) — milk. "Al-laqaḥah" — the milch animal. "Al-fīʾām" (with kasrah on the fāʾ, followed by a prolonged hamzah) — the company. "Al-fakhdh" of people — smaller than the tribe.

| 1809 —
And from Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh, who said: I set out with Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī to Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān (may God be pleased with them), and Abū Masʿūd said to him: "Tell me what you heard from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) concerning the Dajjāl." He said: "The Dajjāl will emerge, and with him will be water and fire. What people see as water is a burning fire, and what people see as fire is cool, sweet water. So whoever among you reaches him, let him throw himself into what he sees as fire, for it is sweet, pure water." Abū Masʿūd said: "And I too have heard it." Agreed upon.

| 1810 —
And from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may God be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The Dajjāl will emerge among my nation and remain for forty — I do not know whether forty days, forty months, or forty years. Then God, Glorified and Exalted, will send Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him), and he will seek him and destroy him. Then people will remain for seven years with no enmity between any two. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, will send a cold wind from the direction of Syria, and there will remain on the face of the earth no one in whose heart is an atom's weight of good or faith, except that it will seize him — even if one of you were to enter the core of a mountain, it would enter upon him until it seizes him. Then the wickedest of people will remain, with the lightness of birds and the intellects of beasts, not knowing good nor denouncing evil. Then Satan will appear to them and say: 'Will you not respond?' They will say: 'What do you command us?' So he will command them to worship idols, and in that state their provision will be abundant and their life pleasant. Then the Trumpet will be blown, and no one will hear it except that he will incline his neck (laytan) and raise it. The first to hear it will be a man watering his camels' trough, and he will be struck down, and the people around him will be struck down. Then God will send — or he said: God will send down — rain like dew or shade, and from it the bodies of people will sprout. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on. Then it will be said: 'O people, come to your Lord, and stop them, for they will be questioned.' Then it will be said: 'Bring forth the people of the Fire.' It will be said: 'How many?' It will be said: 'From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.' That is the day that makes children gray-haired, and that is the day when the shin is uncovered." Narrated by Muslim. "Al-layt" — the side of the neck; its meaning is that he places one side of his neck and raises the other.

| 1811 —
And from Anas (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "There is no land that the Dajjāl will not tread upon, except Mecca and Medina; and there is no passage among their passages except that upon it..."

chapters.title_en: Section 167 — On the Major Portents of the Hour: The Dajjāl, the Slaying of the Jews, and the Uncovering of the Euphrates' Treasure
chapters.arabic_text:
الملائكة صافين تحرسهما، فينزل بالسبخة (1)، فترجف المدينة ثلاث رجفات،

يخرج الله منها كل كافر ومنافق». رواه مسلم. (2)

| 1812 - 
# وعنه - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «يتبع

الدجال من يهود أصبهان (1) سبعون ألفا عليهم الطيالسة». رواه مسلم. (2)

| 1813 - 
# وعن أم شريك رضي الله عنها: أنها سمعت النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

يقول: «لينفرن الناس من الدجال في الجبال». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1814 - 
# وعن عمران بن حصين رضي الله عنهما، قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - يقول: «ما بين خلق آدم إلى قيام الساعة أمر أكبر من الدجال». رواه

مسلم. (1)

| 1815  - 
# وعن أبي سعيد الخدري - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

قال: «يخرج الدجال فيتوجه قبله رجل من المؤمنين فيتلقاه المسالح: مسالح

الدجال. فيقولون له: إلى أين تعمد فيقول: أعمد إلى هذا الذي خرج. فيقولون

له: أوما تؤمن بربنا؟ فيقول: ما بربنا خفاء! فيقولون: اقتلوه. فيقول بعضهم

لبعض: أليس قد نهاكم ربكم أن تقتلوا أحدا دونه، فينطلقون به إلى الدجال،

فإذا رآه المؤمن قال: يا أيها الناس، إن هذا الدجال الذي ذكر رسول الله -

صلى الله عليه وسلم -؛ فيأمر الدجال به فيشبح؛ فيقول: خذوه وشجوه. فيوسع

ظهره وبطنه ضربا، فيقول: أوما تؤمن بي؟ فيقول: أنت المسيح الكذاب! فيؤمر

به، فيؤشر بالمنشار من مفرقه حتى يفرق بين رجليه. ثم يمشي الدجال بين

القطعتين ثم يقول له: قم، فيستوي قائما. ثم يقول له: أتؤمن بي؟ فيقول: ما

ازددت فيك إلا بصيرة. ثم يقول: يا أيها الناس إنه لا يفعل بعدي بأحد من

الناس؛ فيأخذه الدجال ليذبحه، فيجعل الله ما بين رقبته إلى ترقوته نحاسا،

فلا يستطيع إليه سبيلا، فيأخذه بيديه ورجليه فيقذف به، فيحسب الناس أنه

قذفه إلى النار، وإنما ألقي في الجنة». فقال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «هذا أعظم الناس شهادة عند رب العالمين». رواه مسلم. وروى البخاري

بعضه بمعناه (1).
# «المسالح»: هم الخفراء والطلائع.

| 1816 - 
# وعن المغيرة بن شعبة - رضي الله عنه - قال: ما سأل أحد رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - عن الدجال أكثر مما سألته؛ وإنه قال لي: «ما يضرك» قلت:

إنهم يقولون: إن معه جبل خبز ونهر ماء. قال: «هو أهون على الله من ذلك».

متفق عليه. (1)

| 1817 - 
# وعن أنس - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما

من نبي إلا وقد أنذر أمته الأعور الكذاب، ألا إنه أعور، وإن ربكم - عز وجل

- ليس بأعور، مكتوب بين عينيه ك ف ر (1)». متفق عليه. (2)

| 1818 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «ألا أحدثكم  حديثا عن الدجال ما حدث به نبي قومه! إنه أعور، وإنه

يجيء معه بمثال الجنة والنار، فالتي يقول إنها الجنة هي النار». متفق عليه

(1).

| 1819 - 
# وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ذكر

الدجال بين ظهراني الناس، فقال: «إن الله ليس بأعور، ألا إن المسيح الدجال

أعور العين اليمنى، كأن عينه عنبة طافية (1)». متفق عليه. (2)

| 1820 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«لا تقوم الساعة حتى يقاتل المسلمون اليهود، حتى يختبئ اليهودي من وراء

الحجر والشجر. فيقول الحجر والشجر: يا مسلم هذا يهودي خلفي تعال فاقتله؛

إلا الغرقد فإنه من شجر اليهود» (1). متفق عليه. (2)

| 1821 - 
# وعنه - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «والذي

نفسي بيده لا تذهب الدنيا حتى يمر الرجل على القبر، فيتمرغ عليه ويقول: يا

ليتني كنت مكان صاحب هذا القبر، وليس به الدين، ما به إلا البلاء». متفق

عليه (1).

| 1822 - 
# وعنه - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا

تقوم الساعة حتى يحسر الفرات عن جبل من ذهب يقتتل عليه، فيقتل من كل مائة

تسعة وتسعون، فيقول كل رجل منهم: لعلي أن أكون أنا أنجو».
# وفي رواية: «يوشك أن يحسر الفرات عن كنز من ذهب، فمن حضره فلا يأخذ منه

شيئا». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1823 - 
# وعنه، قال: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يقول: «يتركون المدينة

على خير ما كانت، لا يغشاها إلا العوافي يريد - عوافي السباع والطير - وآخر

من يحشر راعيان من مزينة يريدان المدينة ينعقان بغنمهما فيجدانها وحوشا،

حتى إذا بلغا ثنية الوداع خرا على وجوههما». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1824 - 
# وعن أبي سعيد الخدري - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

قال: «يكون خليفة من خلفائكم في آخر الزمان يحثو المال ولا يعده». رواه

مسلم. (1)

| 1825 - 
# وعن أبي موسى الأشعري - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

قال: «ليأتين  على الناس زمان يطوف الرجل فيه بالصدقة من الذهب فلا يجد أحدا

يأخذها منه، ويرى الرجل الواحد يتبعه أربعون امرأة يلذن (1) به من قلة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ر-س (ḥ-r-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To guard, protect, keep watch; a guard (ḥaras) or sentinel.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine preservation of the two cities (Mecca and Medina) from the Dajjāl's entry; protective custody by angels.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal guarding by angelic sentinels; metaphorical extension to divine decree shielding sacred precincts.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ḥāl Clause (الْحَال) — The phrase "صافين" (in rows) functions as a circumstantial accusative describing the angels' state during the guarding action.
chapters.translation:
I say — and Allah knows best:

From Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The angels guard the two cities [Mecca and Medina] in rows, then the Dajjāl descends upon the salty barren land (al-sabakhah), and the city [Medina] quakes three quakes, and Allah expels from it every disbeliever and hypocrite." Narrated by Muslim.

| 1812 —
And from him (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Seventy thousand Jews of Iṣfahān will follow the Dajjāl, wearing striped cloaks (al-ṭayālisah)." Narrated by Muslim.

| 1813 —
And from Umm Sharīk (may Allah be pleased with her): She heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "The people will certainly flee from the Dajjāl into the mountains." Narrated by Muslim.

| 1814 —
And from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn (may Allah be pleased with them both), he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "From the creation of Adam until the establishment of the Hour, there is no matter greater than the Dajjāl." Narrated by Muslim.

| 1815 —
And from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), he said: "The Dajjāl will emerge, and a believing man will set out toward him. The outposts (al-masāliḥ) — the outposts of the Dajjāl — will meet him and say: 'Where are you heading?' He replies: 'I am heading to this one who has emerged.' They say to him: 'Do you not believe in our lord?' He says: 'There is nothing hidden about our Lord!' They say: 'Kill him.' Then some of them say to others: 'Has your lord not forbidden you to kill anyone other than him?' So they take him to the Dajjāl. When the believer sees him, he says: 'O people, this is the Dajjāl whom the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) mentioned.' The Dajjāl then orders him to be stretched out, saying: 'Take him and split him.' They beat him severely on his back and belly. He says: 'Do you not believe in me?' He replies: 'You are the false Messiah (al-Masīḥ al-Kadhdhāb)!' He is then ordered, and a saw is placed from the crown of his head until it splits him between his two legs. Then the Dajjāl walks between the two halves and says to him: 'Rise,' and he stands upright. Then he says: 'Do you believe in me?' He replies: 'I have only increased in certainty about you.' Then he says: 'O people, he will not do this to anyone after me.' The Dajjāl takes him to slaughter him, but Allah turns the space between his neck and collarbone into copper, so he finds no way to him. He then seizes him by his hands and feet and throws him, and the people think he threw him into the Fire, but he was only cast into Paradise." The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "This is the greatest of people in martyrdom before the Lord of the Worlds." Narrated by Muslim. Al-Bukhārī narrated part of it with its meaning.
Note: "Al-masāliḥ" (outposts) are the guards and advance scouts.

| 1816 —
And from al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: No one asked the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) about the Dajjāl more than I did. He said to me: "What harm will he do to you?" I said: "They say he will have with him a mountain of bread and a river of water." He said: "He is more insignificant before Allah than that." Agreed upon.

| 1817 —
And from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "There was no prophet who did not warn his nation of the one-eyed liar. Indeed, he is one-eyed, and your Lord, Glorified and Exalted, is not one-eyed. Between his eyes is written: K F R (disbeliever)." Agreed upon.

| 1818 —
And from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Shall I not tell you a narration about the Dajjāl that no prophet has told his people? He is one-eyed, and he will come with a likeness of Paradise and Hellfire. That which he calls Paradise is in fact Hellfire." Agreed upon.

| 1819 —
And from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) mentioned the Dajjāl among the people and said: "Allah is not one-eyed. Indeed, the Messiah the Dajjāl is one-eyed in the right eye, as if his eye is a floating grape." Agreed upon.

| 1820 —
And from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The Hour will not be established until the Muslims fight the Jews, until the Jew hides behind a stone or a tree. The stone and the tree will say: 'O Muslim, this is a Jew behind me, come and kill him' — except the boxthorn (al-gharqad), for it is of the Jews' trees." Agreed upon.

| 1821 —
And from him (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "By Him in Whose hand is my soul, the world will not pass away until a man passes by a grave, rolls upon it, and says: 'Would that I were in the place of the occupant of this grave!' — not due to religion, but solely due to tribulation." Agreed upon.

| 1822 —
And from him (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The Hour will not be established until the Euphrates uncovers a mountain of gold over which people fight, and of every hundred, ninety-nine are killed. Each man among them says: 'Perhaps I will be the one who survives.'"
In another narration: "The Euphrates will soon uncover a treasure of gold. Whoever is present should take nothing of it." Agreed upon.

| 1823 —
And from him, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "They will leave Medina in its best state, and none will enter it except the wild creatures (al-ʿawāfī) — meaning the wild beasts and birds. The last to be gathered will be two shepherds from Muzaynah, driving their sheep toward Medina, and they will find it full of wild beasts. When they reach Thaniyyat al-Wadāʿ, they will fall on their faces." Agreed upon.

| 1824 —
And from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "There will be a caliph from among your caliphs in the end of time who will heap up wealth and not count it." Narrated by Muslim.

| 1825 —
And from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "A time will come upon the people when a man will go about with alms of gold and find no one to accept it from him. And a single man will be seen followed by forty women, seeking refuge with him due to the scarcity of men."

chapters.title_en: Section 168 — On the Virtues of the Righteous, the Excellence of Badr's Witnesses, and Related Judgments
chapters.arabic_text:
الرجال وكثرة النساء». رواه مسلم. (2)

| 1826 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«اشترى رجل من رجل عقارا، فوجد الذي اشترى العقار في عقاره جرة فيها ذهب،

فقال له الذي اشترى العقار: خذ ذهبك، إنما اشتريت منك الأرض ولم أشتر

الذهب، وقال الذي له

| [ص: 510]
# الأرض: إنما بعتك الأرض وما فيها، فتحاكما إلى رجل، فقال الذي تحاكما

إليه: ألكما ولد؟ قال أحدهما: لي غلام، وقال الآخر: لي جارية قال: أنكحا

الغلام الجارية، وأنفقا على أنفسهما منه وتصدقا». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1827 - 
# وعنه - رضي الله عنه: أنه سمع رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يقول:

«كانت امرأتان معهما ابناهما، جاء الذئب فذهب بابن إحداهما. فقالت

لصاحبتها: إنما ذهب بابنك، وقالت الأخرى: إنما ذهب بابنك، فتحاكما إلى داود

- صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقضى به للكبرى، فخرجتا على سليمان بن داود - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - فأخبرتاه. فقال: ائتوني بالسكين أشقه بينهما. فقالت

الصغرى: لا تفعل! رحمك الله، هو ابنها. فقضى به للصغرى». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1828 - 
# وعن مرداس الأسلمي - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال النبي - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «يذهب الصالحون الأول فالأول، ويبقى حثالة كحثالة (1) الشعير أو

التمر لا يباليهم الله بالة». رواه البخاري. (2)

| 1829 - 
# وعن رفاعة بن رافع الزرقي - رضي الله عنه - قال: جاء جبريل إلى النبي -

صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: ما تعدون أهل بدر فيكم؟ قال: «من أفضل المسلمين»

أو كلمة نحوها. قال: وكذلك من شهد بدرا من الملائكة. رواه البخاري. (1)

| 1830 - 
# وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«إذا أنزل الله تعالى بقوم عذابا، أصاب العذاب من كان فيهم، ثم بعثوا على

أعمالهم». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1831 - 
# وعن جابر - رضي الله عنه - قال: كان جذع يقوم إليه النبي - صلى الله عليه

وسلم - يعني في  الخطبة - فلما وضع المنبر سمعنا للجذع مثل صوت العشار، حتى

نزل النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فوضع يده عليه فسكن.

| [ص: 511]
# وفي رواية: فلما كان يوم الجمعة قعد النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - على

المنبر، فصاحت النخلة التي كان يخطب عندها حتى كادت أن تنشق.
# وفي رواية: فصاحت صياح الصبي، فنزل النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - حتى

أخذها فضمها إليه، فجعلت تئن أنين الصبي الذي يسكت حتى استقرت، قال: «بكت

على ما كانت تسمع من الذكر». رواه البخاري. (1)

| 1832 - 
# وعن أبي ثعلبة الخشني جرثوم بن ناشر - رضي الله عنه - عن رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - قال: «إن الله تعالى فرض فرائض فلا تضيعوها، وحد حدودا

فلا تعتدوها، وحرم أشياء فلا تنتهكوها، وسكت عن أشياء رحمة لكم غير نسيان

فلا تبحثوا عنها» حديث حسن. رواه الدارقطني وغيره. (1)

| 1833 - 
# وعن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى رضي الله عنهما، قال: غزونا مع رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - سبع غزوات نأكل الجراد.
# وفي رواية: نأكل معه الجراد. متفق عليه. (1)

| 1834 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «لا

يلدغ المؤمن من جحر واحد مرتين». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1835 - 
# وعنه، قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ثلاثة لا يكلمهم الله

يوم القيامة، ولا ينظر إليهم، ولا يزكيهم، ولهم عذاب أليم: رجل على فضل ماء

بالفلاة يمنعه من ابن السبيل، ورجل بايع رجلا سلعة بعد العصر (1) فحلف

بالله لأخذها بكذا وكذا فصدقه

| [ص: 512]
# وهو على غير ذلك، ورجل بايع إماما لا يبايعه إلا لدنيا فإن أعطاه منها

وفى وإن لم يعطه منها لم يف». متفق عليه. (2)

| 1836 - 
# وعنه، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «بين النفختين أربعون»

قالوا: يا أبا هريرة أربعون يوما؟ قال: أبيت، قالوا: أربعون سنة؟ قال:

أبيت. قالوا: أربعون شهرا؟ قال: أبيت. «ويبلى كل شيء من الإنسان إلا عجب

الذنب (1)، فيه يركب الخلق، ثم ينزل الله من السماء ماء فينبتون كما ينبت

البقل».  متفق عليه. (2)

| 1837 - 
# وعنه، قال: بينما النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في مجلس يحدث القوم، جاء

أعرابي فقال: متى الساعة؟ فمضى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يحدث،

فقال بعض القوم: سمع ما قال فكره ما قال، وقال بعضهم: بل لم يسمع، حتى إذا

قضى حديثه قال: «أين السائل عن الساعة؟» قال: ها أنا يا رسول الله. قال:

«إذا ضيعت الأمانة فانتظر الساعة». قال: كيف إضاعتها؟ قال: «إذا وسد الأمر

إلى غير أهله فانتظر الساعة». رواه البخاري. (1)

| 1838 - 
# وعنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «يصلون لكم، فإن أصابوا

فلكم، وإن أخطئوا فلكم وعليهم» (1). رواه البخاري. (2)

| 1839 - 
# وعنه - رضي الله عنه: {كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس} [البقرة: 110] قال: خير

الناس للناس يأتون بهم في السلاسل في أعناقهم حتى يدخلوا في الإسلام. (1)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-ر (ʿ-q-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Landed property, real estate; a tract of land that is cultivated or built upon.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal contexts, denotes immovable property as distinct from movable wealth (gold, chattels).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here for physical land; the dispute hinges on whether "what is in it" (mā fīhā) is included in the sale — a matter of contractual scope, not metaphor.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Implied Protasis (الشّرط المضمر) — In Hadith 1837, the Prophet's reply "If the trust is betrayed, then await the Hour" employs a conditional where the apodosis is understood from context, requiring the listener to supply the logical consequence.
chapters.translation:
**1826** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — from the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — who said:

"A man purchased a piece of land from another man, and the one who bought the land found in his land a jar containing gold. The buyer said to the seller: 'Take your gold, for I bought only the land from you, and I did not buy the gold.' And the one who owned the land said: 'I sold you the land and whatever is in it.' So they referred their dispute to a man [for arbitration]. The arbiter asked: 'Do either of you have a child?' One said: 'I have a son.' The other said: 'I have a daughter.' He said: 'Marry the son to the daughter, and spend from it upon yourselves, and give charity from it.'" — Agreed upon (Al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

**1827** — On his authority — may Allah be pleased with him — that he heard the Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — say:

"There were two women, each with her son. A wolf came and took the son of one of them. She said to her companion: 'It took your son.' And the other said: 'It took your son.' So they referred their dispute to Dāwūd — peace be upon him — and he ruled in favor of the elder [woman]. Then they went out to Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd — peace be upon him — and informed him. He said: 'Bring me a knife that I may split him between them.' The younger one said: 'Do not do so! May Allah have mercy upon you — he is her son.' So he ruled in favor of the younger one." — Agreed upon.

**1828** — On the authority of Mirdās al-Aslamī — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "The righteous will pass away, one after another, and there will remain scum (ḥuthālah) like the scum of barley or dates, whom Allah will not regard with the least consideration." — Narrated by Al-Bukhārī.

**1829** — On the authority of Rifāʿah ibn Rāfiʿ al-Zuraqī — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: Jibrīl came to the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — and asked: "How do you reckon the people of Badr among you?" He replied: "Among the best of the Muslims" — or words to that effect. Jibrīl said: "Likewise, those angels who witnessed Badr." — Narrated by Al-Bukhārī.

**1830** — On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with them both — who said: The Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "When Allah the Exalted sends down punishment upon a people, the punishment afflicts all who are among them; then they will be resurrected according to their deeds." — Agreed upon.

**1831** — On the authority of Jābir — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: There was a palm-trunk upon which the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — used to lean while delivering the sermon. When the pulpit (minbar) was placed, we heard the trunk emit a sound like that of a pregnant she-camel, until the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — descended and placed his hand upon it, and it became still.

In another narration: "When Friday came, the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — sat upon the pulpit, and the palm-tree that he used to address cried out until it nearly split apart."

In yet another narration: "It cried out with the cry of a child. The Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — descended until he took hold of it and embraced it, and it began to moan like a child being soothed until it settled. He said: 'It wept for what it used to hear of the remembrance [of Allah].'" — Narrated by Al-Bukhārī.

**1832** — On the authority of Abū Thaʿlabah al-Khushanī, Jurthūm ibn Nāshir — may Allah be pleased with him — from the Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — who said: "Verily, Allah the Exalted has ordained obligations, so do not neglect them; and He has set limits, so do not transgress them; and He has forbidden things, so do not violate them; and He has remained silent about things out of mercy for you — not out of forgetfulness — so do not inquire into them." — A good (ḥasan) hadith, narrated by Al-Dāraquṭnī and others.

**1833** — On the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā — may Allah be pleased with them both — who said: We went on seven military expeditions with the Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — during which we ate locusts.

In another narration: "We ate locusts with him." — Agreed upon.

**1834** — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — that the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "A believer is not stung from the same hole twice." — Agreed upon.

**1835** — On his authority, who said: The Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "Three persons Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor look upon them, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: a man who has surplus water in a desert and withholds it from the wayfarer; a man who sells a commodity to another after the afternoon prayer (al-ʿAṣr) and swears by Allah that he was given such-and-such for it, and the buyer believes him — while it was not so; and a man who pledges allegiance to a ruler only for worldly gain — if he is given from it he fulfills, and if he is not given from it he does not fulfill." — Agreed upon.

**1836** — On his authority, from the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — who said: "Between the two trumpet-blasts there are forty." They said: "O Abū Hurayrah, forty days?" He said: "I refuse [to specify]." They said: "Forty years?" He said: "I refuse." They said: "Forty months?" He said: "I refuse." "And every part of the human being will decay except the coccyx (ʿajb al-dhanab); from it the creation will be re-formed. Then Allah will send down rain from the sky, and they will sprout forth as vegetation sprouts." — Agreed upon.

**1837** — On his authority, who said: While the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — was in a gathering speaking to the people, a Bedouin came and asked: "When is the Hour?" The Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — continued speaking. Some of those present said: "He heard what he said and disliked it." Others said: "Rather, he did not hear." When he finished his speech, he said: "Where is the one asking about the Hour?" The man said: "Here I am, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "When the trust is betrayed, then await the Hour." He asked: "How is it betrayed?" He said: "When authority is entrusted to those unworthy of it, then await the Hour." — Narrated by Al-Bukhārī.

**1838** — On his authority: The Messenger of Allah — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "They lead you in prayer. If they are correct, then the reward is yours; and if they err, then the reward is yours and the burden is upon them." — Narrated by Al-Bukhārī.

**1839** — On his authority — may Allah be pleased with him — regarding the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس»} [Al-Baqarah: 110] — "You are the best nation brought forth for mankind" — he said: "The best of people for [the benefit of] people; they bring them in chains upon their necks until they enter into Islam."

chapters.title_en: Section 169 — On the Virtues of the Mosque, the Blameworthiness of the Market, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
| 1840 - 
# وعنه، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «عجب الله - عز وجل - من قوم

يدخلون الجنة في السلاسل». رواهما البخاري. (1)
# معناه: يؤسرون ويقيدون ثم يسلمون فيدخلون الجنة.

| 1841 - 
# وعنه، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «أحب البلاد إلى الله

مساجدها، وأبغض البلاد إلى الله أسواقها». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1842 - 
# وعن سلمان الفارسي - رضي الله عنه - من قوله قال: لا تكونن إن استطعت أول

من يدخل السوق، ولا آخر من يخرج منها، فإنها معركة الشيطان، وبها ينصب

رايته. رواه مسلم هكذا. (1)
# ورواه البرقاني في صحيحه عن سلمان، قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «لا تكن أول من يدخل السوق، ولا آخر من يخرج منها. فيها باض الشيطان

وفرخ».

| 1843 - 
# وعن عاصم الأحول، عن عبد الله بن سرجس - رضي الله عنه - قال: قلت لرسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: يا رسول الله، غفر الله لك، قال: «ولك». قال

عاصم: فقلت له: أستغفر لك رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم؟ قال: نعم ولك،

ثم تلا هذه الآية: {واستغفر لذنبك وللمؤمنين والمؤمنات} [محمد: 19]. رواه

مسلم. (1)

| 1844 - 
# وعن أبي مسعود الأنصاري - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال النبي - صلى الله  عليه

وسلم: «إن مما أدرك الناس من كلام النبوة الأولى: إذا لم تستح فاصنع ما

شئت». رواه البخاري. (1)

| 1845 - 
# وعن ابن مسعود - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «أول ما يقضى بين الناس يوم القيامة في الدماء». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1846 - 
# وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها، قالت: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم:

«خلقت الملائكة من نور، وخلق الجان من مارج من نار (1)، وخلق آدم مما وصف

لكم». رواه مسلم. (2)

| 1847 - 
# وعنها رضي الله عنها، قالت: كان خلق نبي الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

القرآن. رواه مسلم في جملة حديث طويل (1).

| 1848 - 
# وعنها، قالت: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من أحب لقاء الله أحب

الله لقاءه، ومن كره لقاء الله كره الله لقاءه» فقلت: يا رسول الله،

أكراهية الموت، فكلنا نكره الموت؟ قال: «ليس كذلك، ولكن المؤمن إذا بشر

برحمة الله ورضوانه وجنته أحب لقاء الله فأحب الله لقاءه، وإن الكافر إذا

بشر بعذاب الله وسخطه كره لقاء الله وكره الله لقاءه». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1849 - 
# وعن أم المؤمنين صفية بنت حيي رضي الله عنها، قالت: كان النبي - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - معتكفا، فأتيته أزوره ليلا، فحدثته ثم قمت لأنقلب فقام معي

ليقلبني، فمر رجلان من الأنصار رضي الله عنهما، فلما رأيا النبي - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - أسرعا. فقال - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «على رسلكما، إنها صفية بنت

حيي» فقالا: سبحان الله يا رسول الله، فقال: «إن الشيطان يجري من ابن آدم

مجرى الدم، وإني خشيت أن يقذف في قلوبكما شرا - أو قال: شيئا». متفق عليه.

(1)

| 1850 - 
# وعن أبي الفضل العباس بن عبد المطلب - رضي الله عنه - قال: شهدت مع رسول

الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يوم حنين (1)، فلزمت أنا وأبو سفيان بن الحارث

بن عبد المطلب رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فلم

| [ص: 515]
# نفارقه، ورسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - على بغلة له بيضاء، فلما

التقى المسلمون والمشركون، ولى المسلمون مدبرين، فطفق  رسول الله - صلى الله

عليه وسلم - يركض بغلته قبل الكفار، وأنا آخذ بلجام بغلة رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - أكفها إرادة أن لا تسرع، وأبو سفيان آخذ بركاب رسول الله

- صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أي عباس،

ناد أصحاب السمرة (2)». قال العباس - وكان رجلا صيتا - فقلت بأعلى صوتي:

أين أصحاب السمرة، فوالله لكأن عطفتهم حين سمعوا صوتي عطفة البقر على

أولادها، فقالوا: يا لبيك يا لبيك، فاقتتلوا هم والكفار، والدعوة في

الأنصار يقولون: يا معشر الأنصار، يا معشر الأنصار، ثم قصرت الدعوة على بني

الحارث بن الخزرج، فنظر رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وهو على بغلته

كالمتطاول عليها إلى قتالهم، فقال: «هذا حين حمي الوطيس»، ثم أخذ رسول الله

- صلى الله عليه وسلم - حصيات فرمى بهن وجوه الكفار، ثم قال: «انهزموا ورب

محمد»، فذهبت أنظر فإذا القتال على هيئته فيما أرى، فوالله ما هو إلا أن

رماهم بحصياته، فما زلت أرى حدهم كليلا وأمرهم مدبرا. رواه مسلم. (3)
# «الوطيس» التنور، ومعناه: اشتدت الحرب. وقوله: «حدهم» هو بالحاء المهملة:

أي بأسهم.

| 1851 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «أيها الناس، إن الله طيب لا يقبل إلا طيبا، وإن الله أمر المؤمنين

بما أمر به المرسلين. فقال تعالى:
# {يا أيها الرسل كلوا من الطيبات واعملوا صالحا} [المؤمنون: 51]، وقال

تعالى: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم} [البقرة: 172]. ثم

ذكر الرجل يطيل السفر أشعث أغبر يمد يديه إلى السماء: يا رب يا رب، ومطعمه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ج-ب (ʿajiba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Astonishment, wonderment; a state of marvel at something extraordinary
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In divine attribution, wonder (taʿajjub) denotes divine approval and magnification of an act's merit, not human perplexity
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in human context; metaphorical (majāz) when ascribed to Allah, signifying His pleasure and reward
- Sībawayh Rule: Predicate Fronting (Taqdīm al-Khabar) — "أحب البلاد إلى الله مساجدها" fronts the predicate for emphasis and exclusivity
chapters.translation:
**1840** — And on his authority (Abū Hurayrah), from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: «Allah, Glorified and Exalted, marvels at a people who enter Paradise in chains». Both were narrated by al-Bukhārī. (1)
Its meaning: They are taken captive and fettered, then they surrender [to Islam], and so they enter Paradise.

**1841** — And on his authority, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: «The most beloved of lands to Allah are their mosques, and the most detested of lands to Allah are their marketplaces». Narrated by Muslim. (1)

**1842** — And on the authority of Salmān al-Fārsī — may Allah be pleased with him — from his own saying, he said: Do not be, if you are able, the first to enter the marketplace, nor the last to leave it, for it is the battlefield of Satan, and therein he plants his banner. Narrated by Muslim in this manner. (1)
And al-Barqānī narrated it in his Ṣaḥīḥ on the authority of Salmān, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Do not be the first to enter the marketplace, nor the last to leave it. In it Satan has laid his eggs and hatched his young».

**1843** — And on the authority of ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sarjis — may Allah be pleased with him — he said: I said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: O Messenger of Allah, may Allah forgive you. He said: «And you». ʿĀṣim said: So I said to him: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seek forgiveness for you? He said: Yes, and for you. Then he recited this verse: {And seek forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women} [Muḥammad: 19]. Narrated by Muslim. (1)

**1844** — And on the authority of Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī — may Allah be pleased with him — he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: «Indeed, among what people have grasped from the words of the first prophethood is: If you feel no shame, then do as you wish». Narrated by al-Bukhārī. (1)

**1845** — And on the authority of Ibn Masʿūd — may Allah be pleased with him — he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «The first matter judged between people on the Day of Resurrection will be concerning bloodshed». Agreed upon. (1)

**1846** — And on the authority of ʿĀʾishah — may Allah be pleased with her — she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «The angels were created from light, and the jinn were created from a smokeless flame of fire (1), and Ādam was created from what has been described to you». Narrated by Muslim. (2)

**1847** — And on her authority — may Allah be pleased with her — she said: The character of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was the Qurʾān. Narrated by Muslim within a lengthy ḥadīth. (1)

**1848** — And on her authority, she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Whoever loves the meeting with Allah, Allah loves meeting with him; and whoever detests the meeting with Allah, Allah detests meeting with him». So I said: O Messenger of Allah, is it the detestation of death? For all of us detest death. He said: «It is not so.
