| 1884 - 
# وعن ابن مسعود - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم: «إني لأعلم آخر أهل النار خروجا منها، وآخر أهل الجنة  دخولا الجنة.

رجل يخرج من النار حبوا، فيقول الله - عز وجل - له: اذهب فادخل الجنة،

فيأتيها، فيخيل إليه أنها ملأى، فيرجع، فيقول: يا رب وجدتها ملأى! فيقول

الله - عز وجل - له: اذهب فادخل الجنة، فيأتيها، فيخيل إليه أنها ملأى،

فيرجع. فيقول: يا رب وجدتها ملأى، فيقول الله - عز وجل - له: اذهب فادخل

الجنة. فإن لك مثل الدنيا وعشرة أمثالها؛ أو إن لك مثل عشرة أمثال الدنيا،

فيقول: أتسخر بي، أو تضحك بي وأنت الملك». قال: فلقد رأيت رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - ضحك حتى بدت نواجذه فكان يقول: «ذلك أدنى أهل الجنة

منزلة» متفق عليه. (1)

| 1885 - 
# وعن أبي موسى - رضي الله عنه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «إن

للمؤمن في الجنة لخيمة من لؤلؤة واحدة مجوفة طولها في السماء ستون ميلا.

للمؤمن فيها أهلون يطوف عليهم المؤمن فلا يرى بعضهم بعضا» متفق عليه. (1)
# «الميل»: ستة آلاف ذراع.

| 1886 - 
# وعن أبي سعيد الخدري - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

قال: «إن في الجنة شجرة يسير الراكب الجواد المضمر (1) السريع مائة سنة ما

يقطعها» متفق عليه. (2)
# وروياه في الصحيحين أيضا من رواية أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - قال: «يسير

الراكب في ظلها مئة سنة ما يقطعها».

| 1887 - 
# وعنه (1)، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «إن أهل الجنة ليتراءون

أهل الغرف من فوقهم كما تراءون الكوكب الدري الغابر في الأفق من المشرق أو

المغرب لتفاضل ما

| [ص: 531]
# بينهم» قالوا: يا رسول الله؛ تلك منازل الأنبياء لا يبلغها غيرهم قال:

«بلى والذي نفسي بيده، رجال آمنوا بالله وصدقوا المرسلين». متفق عليه. (2)

| 1888 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«لقاب (1) قوس في الجنة خير مما تطلع عليه الشمس أو تغرب» متفق عليه. (2)

| 1889 - 
# وعن أنس - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «إن

في الجنة سوقا يأتونها كل جمعة. فتهب ريح الشمال، فتحثو في وجوههم وثيابهم،

فيزدادون حسنا وجمالا فيرجعون إلى أهليهم، وقد ازدادوا حسنا وجمالا، فيقول

لهم أهلوهم: والله لقد ازددتم حسنا وجمالا! فيقولون: وأنتم والله لقد

ازددتم بعدنا حسنا وجمالا!». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1890 - 
# وعن سهل بن سعد - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

قال: «إن أهل الجنة ليتراءون الغرف في الجنة كما تتراءون الكوكب في السماء»

متفق عليه. (1)

| 1891 - 
# وعنه - رضي الله عنه - قال: شهدت من النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - مجلسا

وصف فيه الجنة حتى انتهى، ثم قال في آخر حديثه: «فيها ما لا عين رأت، ولا

أذن سمعت، ولا خطر على قلب بشر» ثم قرأ: {تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع} إلى

قوله تعالى: {فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين} [السجدة: 16 - 17].

رواه البخاري. (1)

| 1892 - 
# وعن أبي سعيد وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهما: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه

وسلم -
# قال: «إذا دخل أهل الجنة الجنة ينادي مناد: إن لكم أن تحيوا، فلا تموتوا

أبدا، وإن لكم أن تصحوا، فلا تسقموا أبدا، وإن لكم أن تشبوا فلا تهرموا

أبدا، وإن لكم أن تنعموا، فلا تبأسوا أبدا». رواه مسلم. (1)

| 1893 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال:

«إن أدنى مقعد أحدكم من الجنة أن يقول له: تمن، فيتمنى ويتمنى فيقول له: هل

تمنيت؟ فيقول: نعم، فيقول له: فإن لك ما تمنيت ومثله معه». رواه مسلم (1).

| 1894 - 
# وعن أبي سعيد الخدري - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم

- قال: «إن الله - عز وجل - يقول لأهل الجنة: يا أهل الجنة، فيقولون: لبيك

ربنا وسعديك، والخير في يديك، فيقول: هل رضيتم؟ فيقولون: وما لنا لا نرضى

يا ربنا وقد أعطيتنا ما لم تعط أحدا من خلقك، فيقول: ألا أعطيكم أفضل من

ذلك؟ فيقولون: وأي شيء أفضل من ذلك؟ فيقول: أحل عليكم رضواني فلا أسخط

عليكم بعده أبدا». متفق عليه. (1)

| 1895 - 
# وعن جرير بن عبد الله - رضي الله عنه - قال: كنا عند  رسول الله - صلى

الله عليه وسلم - فنظر إلى القمر ليلة البدر، وقال: «إنكم سترون ربكم عيانا

كما ترون هذا القمر، لا تضامون في رؤيته» متفق عليه. (1)

| 1896 - 
# وعن صهيب - رضي الله عنه: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: «إذا

دخل أهل الجنة الجنة يقول الله تبارك وتعالى: تريدون شيئا أزيدكم؟ فيقولون:

ألم تبيض وجوهنا؟ ألم تدخلنا الجنة وتنجنا من النار؟ فيكشف الحجاب، فما

أعطوا شيئا أحب إليهم من النظر إلى ربهم».رواه مسلم. (1)
# قال الله تعالى: {إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات يهديهم ربهم بإيمانهم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Emptiness, solitude; a place devoid of occupants
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, denotes what is concealed from human perception — the unseen realities of the Hereafter
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here for "what has not occurred to the heart"; metaphorical extension for the ineffable nature of Paradise
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Construction (الشّرط والجزاء) — The protasis (e.g., "if he wishes") governs the apodosis, requiring precise verb mood sequencing in reported divine speech
chapters.translation:
1884 — On the authority of Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «I indeed know the last person of the Fire to emerge from it, and the last person of Paradise to enter it. A man crawls out of the Fire, and Allah (Mighty and Majestic) says to him: "Go and enter Paradise." He comes to it, and it appears to him as if it is full, so he returns and says: "O Lord, I found it full!" Allah (Mighty and Majestic) says to him: "Go and enter Paradise." He comes to it, and it appears to him as if it is full, so he returns and says: "O Lord, I found it full!" Allah (Mighty and Majestic) says to him: "Go and enter Paradise, for you shall have the like of the world and ten times its equivalent" — or "you shall have the like of ten times the world." He says: "Do You mock me, or laugh at me, while You are the King?"» He (Ibn Masʿūd) said: I indeed saw the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) laugh until his molars became visible, and he would say: «That is the lowest of the people of Paradise in rank.» Agreed upon (by al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

1885 — On the authority of Abū Mūsā (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Indeed, for the believer in Paradise there is a tent hollowed from a single pearl, its length in the sky sixty miles. The believer has therein family members who circulate around him, yet none of them sees the others.» Agreed upon. (The "mile" is six thousand cubits.)

1886 — On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: «Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree which a rider upon a swift, well-trained, fast steed would traverse for a hundred years without crossing it.» Agreed upon. Both (al-Bukhārī and Muslim) also narrated it in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: «A rider travels in its shade for a hundred years without crossing it.»

1887 — On his authority (Abū Saʿīd), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: «Indeed, the people of Paradise behold the people of the lofty chambers above them just as you behold the brilliant, fading planet on the horizon in the east or the west, due to the superiority of some over others.» They said: "O Messenger of Allah, those are the abodes of the prophets; none besides them can reach them." He said: «By Him in Whose hand is my soul, men who believed in Allah and affirmed the truth of the messengers (shall reach them).» Agreed upon.

1888 — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «A span of a bow in Paradise is better than that upon which the sun rises or sets.» Agreed upon.

1889 — On the authority of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Indeed, in Paradise there is a market which they attend every Friday. The north wind blows, scattering (fragrance) upon their faces and garments, and they increase in beauty and comeliness. They return to their families, having increased in beauty and comeliness, and their families say to them: "By Allah, you have indeed increased in beauty and comeliness!" They reply: "And you, by Allah, have indeed increased in beauty and comeliness after us!"» Narrated by Muslim.

1890 — On the authority of Sahl ibn Saʿd (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Indeed, the people of Paradise behold the lofty chambers in Paradise just as you behold the planet in the sky.» Agreed upon.

1891 — On his authority (Sahl ibn Saʿd, may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I witnessed a gathering with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in which he described Paradise until he reached its end. Then, at the conclusion of his speech, he said: «In it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has not occurred to the heart of any human.» Then he recited: {Their sides forsake their beds} up to His (Mighty and Majestic) saying: {No soul knows what comfort has been concealed for them} [al-Sajdah 32:16–17]. Narrated by al-Bukhārī.

1892 — On the authority of Abū Saʿīd and Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with them both): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, a caller proclaims: "Indeed, for you is that you live and never die; for you is that you be healthy and never fall ill; for you is that you remain young and never age; for you is that you enjoy bliss and never suffer adversity."» Narrated by Muslim.

1893 — On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Indeed, the lowest seat of any of you in Paradise is that He says to him: "Wish." So he wishes and wishes. Then He says to him: "Have you wished?" He says: "Yes." He says to him: "Then for you is what you wished, and its like along with it."» Narrated by Muslim.

1894 — On the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Indeed, Allah (Mighty and Majestic) says to the people of Paradise: "O people of Paradise!" They say: "At Your service, our Lord, and blessed be Your call; all good is in Your hands." He says: "Are you pleased?" They say: "Why should we not be pleased, O our Lord, when You have given us what You have not given any of Your creation?" He says: "Shall I not give you something better than that?" They say: "And what thing is better than that?" He says: "I bestow upon you My good pleasure, and I shall never be wrathful with you after it, ever."» Agreed upon.

1895 — On the authority of Jarīr ibn ʿAbdillāh (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon, and said: «Indeed, you shall see your Lord with your own eyes, just as you see this moon, without any harm in seeing Him.» Agreed upon.

1896 — On the authority of Ṣuhayb (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, Allah (Blessed and Exalted) says: "Do you desire anything that I may increase you?" They say: "Have You not whitened our faces? Have You not admitted us into Paradise and saved us from the Fire?" Then the veil is lifted, and nothing is given to them more beloved to them than looking upon their Lord.» Narrated by Muslim. Allah (Mighty and Majestic) said: {Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds — their Lord will guide them by their faith} [Yūnus 10:9].

chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ع-و (da-ʿa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of calling, supplication, or invocation; also used for legal claim or assertion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic usage, denotes the act of addressing God in prayer or the declaration of one’s state before Him; here, the inhabitants’ “call” is their glorification.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — an uttered supplication; metaphorical (majāz) — their very state of being is a silent invocation of praise.
- Root: ح-م-د (ḥa-mī-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Praise arising from gratitude and recognition of beneficence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradats): Theologically, praise (ḥamd) is attributed to God alone as the ultimate object of all commendation, distinct from mere thanks (shukr) which may be directed to creatures.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — verbal praise; metaphorical — the conclusive acknowledgment of God’s sovereignty as the seal of all affairs.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase «وآخر دعواهم» is in apposition to the preceding clause, clarifying the sequence of the inhabitants’ utterances; the genitive construction «دعواهم» governs the entire quoted supplication as a single syntactic unit.
chapters.translation:
I say: God the Exalted has said: {«Rivers flow beneath them in the Gardens of Delight. Their call therein is: “Glory be to You, O God,” and their greeting therein is “Peace,” and the last of their call is: “Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds”»} [Yūnus 10:9–10].

Praise be to God who has guided us to this, and we would never have been guided had God not guided us. O God, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger, the Unlettered Prophet, and upon the family of Muhammad, his wives, and his descendants, just as You sent blessings upon Abraham and upon the family of Abraham; and bless Muhammad, the Unlettered Prophet, and the family of Muhammad, his wives, and his descendants, just as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham in all the worlds. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.

The author (may God have mercy on him) said: I completed this work on Monday, the fourth day of the month of Ramadan, in the year six hundred and seventy (AH), in Damascus.
